description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Organization Overview

At Lilly, we serve an extraordinary purpose. We make a difference for people around the globe by discovering, developing, and delivering medicines that help them live longer, healthier, more active lives. Lilly is making transformational investments in direct-to-consumer healthcare delivery through LillyDirect and other digital health initiatives. LillyDirect’s mission is to deliver a world-class consumer healthcare experience by transforming how patients access Lilly’s innovative medicines and digital health solutions through an end-to-end consumer health platform.

Position Overview

Customer Insights and Analytics (CI&A) is focused on improved patient and business outcomes through strategic and innovative insights grounded in data and analytics. The Senior Director CI&A LillyDirect will build and lead the team responsible for delivering analytical insights that drive LillyDirect business decisions in the U.S. and outside the United States (OUS), while also providing leadership, technical guidance and career development support for individuals in their organization. This role will assume strategic and people leadership of Lilly's existing LillyDirect data strategy function and will scale that foundation into a broader analytics organization serving U.S. and OUS markets. This role reports to the CFO of LillyDirect.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive analytics strategy for LillyDirect, with a consumer-first, and AI-first approach, aligned with business goals.
  • Set the strategic direction and roadmap for LillyDirect analytics, providing oversight and thought leadership to direct reports accountable for day-to-day execution, including dashboard development, KPI tracking, and cross-functional data partnership with CI&A, Tech@Lilly, and Finance.
  • Work closely with both the Chief Product and Technology Officer and the Sr Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer LillyDirect to define the analytical agenda for the LillyDirect product and marketing functions – setting priorities for what data is captured, what questions are investigated, and what insights are acted upon.

People Leadership – Build and Lead a World-Class C&IA Team

  • Scale and lead a team of business analysts capable of operating with the speed and agility of a health-tech company who support LillyDirect in the delivery of high-impact insights to the organization for US and OUS markets.
  • Develop a pipeline of analytics talent and leadership, and contribute to an inclusive community of expert practitioners through recruiting, training, coaching, and retaining top talent
  • Ensure the team delivers business recommendations and solutions that are supported by solid evidence, grounded in analytics
  • Promote a culture of accountability and operational excellence by ensuring CI&A team delivers work on time and maintain an operations calendar
  • Partner with Lilly BI&A organization to replicate and/or share best practices

Business Integration

  • Provide objective data used to measure business performance for the overall LillyDirect business as well as specific parts of the business
  • Influence business decisions and deliver data-driven insights to the LillyDirect leadership team that help more patients
  • Influence LillyDirect leaders on the effective adoption of analytics recommendations and solutions
  • Engage fully with business teams by providing an objective perspective and facilitating data-driven decision making
  • Proactively bring recommendations and solutions to the business to improve outcomes
  • Champion efforts to challenge the status quo and drive solutions that help LillyDirect reach its goals

We’re on an exciting journey to transform our Group and the way we’re shaping finance for good. We’re focusing on the future, investing in our technologies, workplaces, and colleagues to make our Group a great place for everyone.

  • Experience working closely with design and product teams to identify and prioritise the right research questions.
  • Able to create research roadmaps and plans to keep the team on track, helping set both short-term objectives and strategic direction.

  • Able to operate effectively in environments where research practices are still developing, building trust in insights and increasing the adoption of evidence-led approaches.

  • Experience with accessibility research and/or vulnerable customers.

title: Deputy Prothonotary 1 - Supreme - Western District Filing Office
description:
The Deputy Prothonotary supervises the work of clerical staff in the Supreme Court’s Western District filing office, working closely with the Chief Clerk to oversee the day-to-day operations of the filing office. The Deputy also works closely with the Prothonotary to ensure efficient operation of the Western District office. The Deputy is responsible for the daily monitoring and management of the workflow, performing jurisdictional reviews, ensuring that filings are compliant with the Rules of Appellate Procedure, and answering questions from staff, chambers, the public, and other administrative offices, and performing other duties at the direction of the Prothonotary. The Deputy will also work collaboratively with the Deputy Prothonotaries in both the Middle and Eastern Districts.

Primary Duties


  • Supervises staff, manages workflow in the office by assigning work to staff, reviews staff work product, answers questions, completes performance evaluations, and oversees the physical office space and courtroom.
  • Reviews filings via mail and PACFile for compliance with the Pennsylvania Rules of Appellate Procedure.
  • Reviews filings thoroughly, drafts appropriate responses, or assigns filings for processing in the office in accordance with internal processes.
  • Closely monitors the case flow of the office and takes appropriate action.
  • Ensures that staff are advised of any Rule changes adopted by the Court and that all changes are properly applied by staff in daily processes.
  • Works with the Prothonotary to ensure that the Western District office is efficiently and properly functioning.

title: Director, Technology & Business Enablement - UC Davis
description:
At a glance

UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education is looking for a Director of Technology & Business Enablement to lead a talented team of approximately 15 at the intersection of technology, data, and business strategy. This is a great opportunity for a collaborative, solutions-oriented leader who enjoys bringing clarity to complex environments, developing teams, and translating business needs into sustainable technology solutions. You’ll help shape technology strategy, strengthen data and governance, and play a key role in upcoming transformation efforts, including AI implementation and modernizing how the organization works. We’re open to someone ready to step into a broader leadership opportunity and grow their scope, as well as a seasoned leader who brings deep experience navigating technology and business enablement within a large, complex organization. Interested in making an impact at UC Davis?

Description: What you'll be doing

Another Source's client, University of California, Davis, is recruiting a Director, Technology and Business Enablement Team to join their Continuing and Professional Education team in Davis, California. This hybrid role is onsite two days per week, with a third onsite day as needed for CPE meetings. Internally, this position is titled Director, Business Enablement Team

Here's a little about UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education:

UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education (CPE) is the university’s academic division dedicated to workforce and career development, helping working professionals upskill, reskill, and advance their careers. CPE brings the expertise and resources of UC Davis to learners around the world through partnerships with campus schools, colleges, faculty, employers, government agencies, and international universities.

The scale and reach of CPE create an especially dynamic environment for technology and business enablement leadership. The division records nearly 74,000 enrollments annually across more than 4,400 classes, serving learners in all 50 states and more than 100 countries. CPE also manages UC Davis’ relationship with Coursera, which has generated more than one million enrollments, and supports approximately 180 employees, more than 60 student employees during peak periods, and approximately 1,700 instructors.

The salary range for this role is $160,000 –190,000 per year with relocation support available.

About this role:

Reporting to the Chief Operations and People Officer, the Director of the Business Enablement Team (BET) is an opportunity to shape how technology, data, projects, and emerging capabilities enable CPE’s continued evolution.

This leader will oversee a multidisciplinary team spanning technology strategy and solution design, systems and application development, data and business intelligence, portfolio and project management, technology support and operations, and governance and innovation. With responsibility for a complex ecosystem of enterprise applications, cloud platforms, learning technologies, integrated data services, cybersecurity, AI, and emerging technologies, the Director will translate organizational priorities into scalable solutions that improve effectiveness, enable innovation, and support CPE’s learners, instructors, staff, and partners.

This position offers the opportunity to bring together technology, data, business intelligence, project delivery, and organizational enablement within a mission-driven university environment - while influencing how CPE uses emerging technologies and AI to support its future.

How you will spend your time

Leadership, Governance & Organizational Effectiveness – 25%

  • Provide strategic leadership for the Business Enablement Team across technology, systems and applications, data and business intelligence, portfolio and project management, technology operations, and innovation.
  • Establish goals, priorities, performance measures, and service standards aligned with CPE’s strategic direction.
  • Lead workforce planning, staff development, succession planning, budget management, and resource allocation.
  • Build governance frameworks, operational policies, risk-management practices, and decision structures that strengthen accountability and organizational effectiveness.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on technology, data, operational excellence, and strategic investments.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, inclusion, and service excellence.

Strategic Technology & Digital Transformation Leadership – 20%

  • Establish and advance CPE’s long-term technology roadmap and digital transformation strategy.
  • Guide enterprise architecture, systems integration, application portfolio management, and technology investment decisions.
  • Evaluate AI, automation, emerging technologies, and evolving business needs for opportunities to improve the organization.
  • Ensure technology capabilities can scale with CPE’s growth while supporting learner success and workforce effectiveness.
  • Represent the division in campus, UC-wide, and external technology initiatives.

Portfolio, Program & Change Management – 20%

  • Provide executive sponsorship and oversight for strategic initiatives, technology projects, process improvements, and organizational change programs.
  • Monitor capacity, dependencies, project risks, and outcomes across the portfolio.
  • Guide change-management strategies that help people successfully adopt new systems, technologies, and business processes.
  • Keep investments focused on measurable business value and divisional priorities.

Data Strategy, Analytics & Decision Support – 15%

  • Establish data governance, analytics, and reporting strategies that strengthen decision-making.
  • Ensure leaders have access to reliable dashboards, performance metrics, reporting tools, and business intelligence.
  • Guide long-term planning for data architecture, warehousing, analytics platforms, and institutional reporting.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage predictive analytics, forecasting, operational intelligence, and AI-enabled insights.

Business Enablement Consulting & Stakeholder Engagement – 15%

  • Partner with divisional leaders to identify opportunities for process redesign, operational improvement, technology adoption, and service enhancement.
  • Translate business objectives into actionable technology, data, and organizational initiatives.
  • Build productive partnerships across UC Davis, the broader UC system, and external organizations.
  • Facilitate executive-level conversations around investments, priorities, organizational readiness, and strategic opportunities.
  • Serve as a senior connection between CPE business units and Business Enablement Team leadership.

Administrative Management – 5%

  • Oversee departmental budgets, contracts, procurement, vendor relationships, and resource planning.
  • Monitor organizational performance, compliance, audits, and operational effectiveness.
  • Support additional strategic initiatives in partnership with the Chief Operations and People Officer.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Business Administration, Public Administration, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Progressive leadership experience overseeing technology, data, business intelligence, project management, or related operational functions.
  • Experience managing professional staff, organizational resources, budgets, and vendor relationships.
  • Experience leading enterprise initiatives involving technology, process improvement, organizational transformation, or service delivery.
  • Demonstrated strength in strategic planning, staff development, performance management, and resource stewardship.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise technology, data management, business intelligence, project management, and service delivery principles.
  • Ability to assess complex organizational challenges, develop effective solutions, and lead change across diverse stakeholder groups.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, Public Administration, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Organizational Leadership, or a related field.
  • Experience in higher education, continuing and professional education, workforce development, or another complex, mission-driven organization.
  • Experience leading enterprise technology, digital transformation, business intelligence, portfolio management, or organizational change initiatives.
  • Knowledge of enterprise architecture, systems integration, cloud platforms, cybersecurity, technology governance, data governance, analytics, and reporting.
  • Ability to develop long-range strategies aligning technology, data, projects, and operations with organizational goals.
  • Experience fostering innovation and developing collaborative, high-performing teams in complex environments.
  • PMP, Agile, ITIL, Lean, Prosci Change Management, CDMP, or similar professional certification.

What's in it for you:

UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at one of the nation's top public research universities while advancing lifelong learning and workforce development.

Employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package through the University of California, including:

  • Competitive medical, dental, vision, and retirement plans
  • Generous vacation, paid holidays, and leave programs
  • Tuition assistance and professional development opportunities
  • A strong commitment to work-life balance
  • The stability, resources, and collaborative culture of the University of California system

Learn more about UC Davis Benefits: https://hr.ucdavis.edu/employees/benefits

UC Davis is a diverse community comprised of individuals with many perspectives and identities. We come from a multitude of backgrounds and experiences, with distinct needs and goals. We recognize that to create an inclusive and intellectually vibrant community, we must understand and value both our individual differences and our common ground. The UC Davis Principles of Community is an aspirational statement that embodies this commitment and reflects the ideals we seek to uphold.

About RMIT University

RMIT is a multi-sector university of technology, design, and enterprise.Our mission is to help shape the world through research, innovation, and engagement, creating transformative experiences for students that prepare them for life and work. With campuses in Melbourne and Vietnam and a centre in Barcelona, RMIT is a truly international university.

About the Role

RMIT Council is the governing body of the University, providing strategic leadership and oversight of its operations, financial stewardship, and academic mission.


Council members play a critical role in shaping RMIT’s long-term strategy, guiding innovation, risk management, and major investments, and ensuring the University’s continued success as a globally engaged institution.


This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced Director or senior executive to contribute strategic governance, financial and investment expertise, and community and business engagement experience within a leading university of technology, design and enterprise.


As a Council Member, you will:

  • Contribute to the strategic direction, sustainability, and future positioning of the University.
  • Appoint and oversee the performance of the Vice-Chancellor.
  • Approve the University’s mission and strategic direction, annual budget, business plan, and significant commercial activities.
  • Oversee financial and risk management, control, and accountability systems.
  • Engage with complex and future-facing challenges, including digital innovation, education transformation, research commercialisation, and global partnerships.
  • Work collegially with an outstanding Council comprising leaders from business, government, and academia.
  • Oversee and monitor the University’s academic activities.

Meetings are held primarily at RMIT’s Melbourne City campus, with six meetings per year (including two full strategy days).

We are seeking interest from candidates who live and work in Victoria. To be successful, you will bring:

  • Director or senior executive experience in a complex, medium-to-large organisation.
  • Completion of, or current participation in, an AICD qualification (or equivalent).
  • Strong strategic governance expertise, strategic oversight capability, and commercial acumen.
  • Intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and an ability to critically assess complex information.
  • Financial management and investment experience, including evaluating and advising on strategic investments and investment strategy.
  • Demonstrated integrity, independence, and commitment to acting in the best interests of RMIT and the broader community.
  • Community and business engagement experience.
  • Education sector experience will be highly regarded.

RMIT is committed to ensuring that Council reflects the rich diversity of the Victorian and broader community, and we welcome applications from candidates of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

Council members are eligible for remuneration, consistent with the RMIT Act and Victorian Government guidelines.

All applicants will be required to undertake pre-appointment checks, including:

National Police Records Check

Insolvency and disqualification checks


Upon appointment, members must comply with the RMIT Code of Conduct, policies, confidentiality obligations, and attend induction and Council meetings as required.

title: Process Instrument Technician - Maintenance - IAPI
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


At Lilly, we serve an extraordinary purpose. We make a difference for people around the globe by discovering, developing and delivering medicines that help them live longer, healthier, more active lives. Not only do we deliver breakthrough medications, but you also can count on us to develop creative solutions to support communities through philanthropy and volunteerism.


This position provides Process Instrumentation maintenance support within Indy Pharmaceutical Manufacturing.

This position will focus on equipment uptime, calibration and reliability. The applicant will work closely with Production, Engineering, Quality Control, Labs and various other groups to troubleshoot, maintain and perform Corrective and Preventative maintenance on Process Instrumentation and provide project support on production and utility related equipment.


Key Objectives/Deliverables:

  • Demonstrate a good process aptitude and application of skills in a variety of real-world process experiences. (e.g., transmitters ranging from pressure, temperature, flow, PH, and level.)
  • Install/set-up/replace Instrument/electrical equipment (e.g., switches, transmitters, controllers, VFDs, various types of process instrumentation).
  • Diagnose basic electrical problems, to effect repairs and restore equipment/systems to operating condition (e.g., 3-wire motor control, 12/24V control circuits, 120V circuitry, etc).
  • Effectively troubleshoot electrical equipment from 24 VDC to 480 VAC to restore equipment/systems to operating condition.
  • Operate basic electrical/pneumatic test equipment and meters (e.g., fluke, signal generators, oscilloscopes, Amtek, MKS).
  • Provide Process instrumentation support for equipment qualification.
  • Provide accurate, complete, and legible Work Order documentation on both paper copy (when required) and in CMMS work order system (Maximo, SAP, etc).

Basic Qualification:

  • High school diploma/GED
  • Associate degree or Technical Trade Certificate in Electrical/Automation/Instrumentation, or equivalent experience
  • Minimum 3 Years of Maintenance instrumentation experience

title: Analista de Ventas (Región Sureste)
description:
Buscamos un líder que convierta la estrategia comercial en resultados visibles en el punto de venta.
Será responsable de liderar la ejecución de la región Sureste a través de equipos de representantes y promotoría, asegurando que nuestras marcas estén disponibles, visibles y activadas correctamente, mientras desarrolla talento, identifica oportunidades de crecimiento y moviliza a las áreas necesarias para resolverlas.
Buscamos a alguien capaz de liderar la región como un negocio: entender qué está pasando, definir dónde actuar, desarrollar a su equipo y transformar oportunidades en resultados.

Principales responsabilidades


1. Liderar la estrategia y los resultados de la región


Ser responsable integral de la ejecución del territorio, estableciendo prioridades y planes de acción por cliente, canal y geografía. Utilizar resultados de Sell Out, Perfect Store y ejecución para identificar oportunidades, asignar recursos y asegurar su implementación en campo. Gestionar eficazmente un territorio geográficamente complejo, definiendo dónde estar, dónde priorizar y cómo mantener un mismo estándar de ejecución en todas las plazas, combinando liderazgo presencial y remoto.


2. Desarrollar un equipo de alto desempeño


Liderar, acompañar y desarrollar representantes y equipos de promotoría mediante coaching en campo, objetivos claros y retroalimentación continua. Construir una cultura de ownership, colaboración, reconocimiento y accountability, desarrollando personas capaces de tomar decisiones, negociar y resolver problemas. Crear un entorno donde el equipo entienda no solamente qué hacer, sino también por qué importa para el negocio.


3. Ganar a través de Perfect Store – D·V·A


Elevar consistentemente los estándares de ejecución a través de tres fundamentos:

· Distribución: disponibilidad, venta cero, inventarios y corrección de inventario fantasma.

· Visibilidad: Share of Shelf, facings, planogramas, precio y promoción.

· Activación: exhibiciones adicionales, material POP e implementación de iniciativas comerciales.

Convertir estos fundamentos en hábitos sostenibles de ejecución, no solamente en indicadores.


Experiencia

· 3 a 5 años de experiencia en posiciones de liderazgo comercial, ejecución, ventas de campo o promotoría, idealmente en consumo masivo.

· Experiencia comprobable liderando equipos de campo y/o agencias de promotoría.

· Experiencia previa en Pedidos Directos Walmart – MUST.

· Experiencia trabajando y negociando directamente en punto de venta.

· Conocimiento sólido de indicadores como Sell In, Sell Out, disponibilidad/OOS, inventarios, Share of Shelf, exhibiciones y Perfect Store.

· Inglés avanzado.

· Disponibilidad para viajar frecuentemente dentro de la región.


Competencias que harán la diferencia


· Liderazgo y desarrollo de personas: Capacidad para inspirar, desarrollar, retar y generar accountability en equipos.

· Mentalidad comercial: Entender la ejecución no como una actividad, sino como una palanca para generar crecimiento y venta incremental.

· Ownership y orientación a resultados: No limitarse a identificar problemas: hacerse responsable de llevarlos hasta su resolución.

· Negociación e influencia: Capacidad para movilizar clientes, equipos internos y agencias, incluso sin autoridad directa.

· Pensamiento analítico y priorización: Transformar grandes cantidades de información en pocas prioridades accionables.

· Comunicación ejecutiva: Presentar resultados, oportunidades y recomendaciones de manera sencilla, estructurada y convincente.

· Adaptabilidad y mentalidad de evolución: Curiosidad para cuestionar, aprender, experimentar y adoptar nuevas formas de trabajar.

· Power BI – interpretación y utilización de dashboards para toma de decisiones.

· Microsoft Office, particularmente Excel y PowerPoint.

· Facilidad para utilizar Inteligencia Artificial y nuevas herramientas digitales como aceleradores de productividad, análisis y toma de decisiones.

Inclusion & Diversity

We’re a global business, with people from every culture, ethnicity, race, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age and ability. We recognize the breadth of human experience, and we work to celebrate it. It is our goal to build a diverse, inclusive and supportive work environment where all people can thrive.

We’re committed to ongoing efforts that help us attract, hire, and retain diverse talent who want to build a positive, inclusive environment. Read more about our ongoing initiatives at .

title: Director of Health Services
description:
Director of Health Services

At MBK Senior Living, we're committed to putting people first – our residents and team members. Exceeding expectations and enriching lives drives our day-to-day. And it's all powered by Yoi Shigoto, a Japanese concept that translates to "good, quality work." It's more than a mantra. It's part of our company-wide commitment to build trust, set high standards, and develop potential in ourselves and others!

Whether you're looking for a flexible, part-time job or the pathway to a lasting career, you'll find it here at MBK Senior Living–and a whole lot more! When you join the MBK Senior Living team, you'll enjoy:

-Impacting lives and building lasting relationships

-Executing exceptional signature programs in dining, fitness, wellness, and care

-A supportive community team that encourages personal and professional growth and celebrates your

success

-A fun-filled, energetic environment that's centered in hospitality and high-quality service

-Competitive salaries

-Professional development, training, and personal coaching through our Mentor, Buddy, and Executive

Director in Training Programs

-Education loan assistance & scholarships

-Financial and legal services

-Team Member discounts

-Health and Wellness resources

Full-time benefits include:

-Rich benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision and 401k matching up to 4%

-Childcare and eldercare assistance

-Flexible spending accounts

If you're looking for a place where you can make an impact, find purpose and joy, and receive the training, tools, and support to reach your career goals – look no further, apply today!

Job Description

Schedule: Monday-Friday
Salary Range: $90,000-$100,000/year

Job Summary:

The Director of Health Services (DHS) leads the overall implementation of clinical health and wellness services in the community. The DHS serves as a liaison between families, hospital personnel, physicians, community organizations, and other related service agencies to provide quality care to MBK Senior Living residents. The DHS collaborates with the Director of Sales and the Executive Director (ED) to set the stage for MBK Senior Living to become the senior living provider of choice. Additionally, the DHS is responsible for coordinating care with outside agencies, communicating with families, managing a clinical team, and developing personalized plans of care for residents’ needs, then communicating them to the care team.


Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Interview, hire, train, set performance goals and timelines, monitor performance, and provide coaching for Medication Technicians.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Conduct and coordinate assessments/evaluations of potential residents and make recommendations for admission in accordance with current rules, regulations, and community policies and procedures.
  • Conduct and/or approve routinely scheduled re-assessments and change of condition assessments promptly.
  • Draft initial Individualized Service Plans (ISP) and update based on schedule and change of condition for residents and partner with ED to review with responsible parties and/or residents.
  • Alert the ED, family members, and others (as necessary) of any changes in residents’ physical or emotional health, and institute interventions as appropriate.
  • Assess the community’s ability to meet resident needs under licensure and collaborate with the ED on plans to retain the residents or move them to a higher level of care when necessary.
  • Develop and maintain good working relationships and effective communication with families and service providers.
  • Train, assign, and supervise Medication Technicians.
  • Perform all administrative duties accurately and timely, including expense reporting, submission of invoices, team member evaluations, etc.
  • Coordinate prescription orders with doctors’ offices, as well as pharmacy delivery of medications, including oversight of the central storage, tracking, and delivery of medications, and ensuring the Medication Administration Records are completed according to company policy and State regulations.
  • Responsible for the overall safety, health, and wellness of residents.
  • Ensure that clinical and care-related regulations and policies are closely monitored and followed.
  • Ensure that physician orders are carried out properly.
  • Aid in the community marketing effort through positive interactions, acting as a liaison between the community and families/outside health service providers.
  • Key management member acting as Manager on Duty when necessary.
  • Collaborate with Department Directors on resident care and caregiver oversight.
  • Collaborate with the Regional Director of Health Services to ensure compliance with MBK policy and procedure and State Regulatory Guidelines
  • Maintain a safe and secure environment for staff, residents, and guests following established safety standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Understand and comply with Federal, State, and local regulations, and company policies and procedures concerning the department.
  • Promote and lead with a spirit of teamwork and open communication in accordance with the MBK principles and core values.
  • Manage labor and other expenses to align with the community budget.
  • Perform other job duties or special projects as assigned or requested by Supervisor and/or Regional Team.

Education Requirements:

  • College Degree required or equivalent work experience and license.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Nursing, Human Services, or the Health Care field is highly desirable.

Experience Requirements (in years):

  • 2+ years of prior related work experience functioning in a similar healthcare management role, within a similar industry/work environment is essential.
  • 2+ years of prior management or supervisory experience required.

Required Competencies/Licenses/Certifications:

  • Licensed RN, LPN, or LVN and must adhere to all requirements to have and maintain a license, including CEU completion and timely renewal.
  • CPR certification required.
  • Must complete required Background clearances, health screening, and provide negative TB test results within 7 days of employment (must be within the last 6 months).
  • Valid state-issued driver’s license and valid insurance or reliable method of transportation for resident assessments.
  • Demonstrated proficiency using Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, and Outlook) and operating standard office equipment.
  • Must have excellent communication skills, including the ability to speak, write, and read English.
  • Must possess the ability to make sound, independent decisions when circumstances warrant such action, and to remain calm during stressful or emergency situations.
  • Must possess the ability to always deal tactfully and professionally with personnel, residents, family members, and guests.
  • Must possess strong organizational, problem-solving, and time management skills.

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • Must be mobile and able to perform the physical requirements of the job, including standing, walking, bending, kneeling, squatting, pulling, reaching overhead, and repetitive motion.
  • Must be able to move intermittently throughout the workday, in the community, and between neighborhoods.
  • Ability to sit and work at a computer for prolonged periods.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds and push up to 250 pounds, as necessary.
  • Ability to assist in the physical movement of residents during routine transfers or in emergency situations.
  • Ability to travel within 50 miles of the community to perform assessments/evaluations.
  • Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Full-time benefits include:

-Rich benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, and 401k matching up to 4%

-Childcare and eldercare assistance

-Flexible spending accounts

-Paid sick leave under the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act

Application Review: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Inspiring people, creating experiences, and supporting goals are just a few ways MBK Senior Living creates a positive work environment. It's how we support our team members, serve our residents, and achieve our pursuit – to be the senior living provider of choice in each market we serve.

MBK Senior Living has pursued this goal for more than 30 years. Currently, the company owns and operates 35 Independent Living, Assisted Living, and Memory Care services in senior living communities throughout the Western United States. We’re proud to have been ranked among the Top 50 "Best Workplaces in Aging Services" by Fortune magazine and certified as a “Great Place to Work” by the Great Place to Work Institute since 2017.

MBK is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, genetic information, or other protected reason. Our company is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for qualifying individuals in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact talentacquisition@mbk.com.

If employed at one of our senior living communities that receives Medicare or Medicaid funding, team members must not be considered an “Excluded Party” as defined by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, any state Medicaid Programs, and any additional federal and state government contract programs. If, as a team member, you learn that you are an Excluded Party at any time, you must present your Excluded Party notice letter to your supervisor immediately.

Other Regulatory Requirements: If employed at one of our senior living communities, team members must continually comply with certain laws and regulations that impact the company, including, but not limited to, as applicable, state licensing regulations, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), Resident Rights as defined by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and any other federal or state laws relating to team members’ professional licenses.

If as an associate you learn you are an Excluded Party, you must present your Excluded Party notice letter to your supervisor immediately. An Excluded Party is a person that the federal or state government found not eligible to provide care and services in a Community that receives Medicare or Medicaid funding. In addition, at all times, during your employment, all associates must be in compliance with certain laws and regulations that affect the company, including but not limited to Resident Rights, HIPAA, State licensing regulations, and those laws relating you an associates’ professional license.

title: Service Engineering Planner
description:
JOB MISSION


To plan and coordinate Service Engineer activities efficiently, ensuring customer visits, planned maintenance, breakdowns and project work are scheduled with the right resources, information and materials. The role supports high levels of engineer utilisation, customer satisfaction and service delivery through accurate planning, proactive communication and effective coordination across the Service organisation.

KEY ACTIVITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES

· Plan and schedule planned maintenance, breakdown, commissioning, warranty and project visits

  • Allocate work to Service Engineers based on competence, location, availability and customer requirements
  • Maintain accurate engineer diaries and optimise routes to improve utilisation and reduce unnecessary travel
  • Confirm appointments with customers and provide timely updates when schedules change
  • Ensure work orders contain the correct scope, site information, permits, risk information and customer contacts
  • Coordinate parts, tools, access equipment and subcontract support so work can be completed as planned
  • Monitor outstanding work, overdue visits and schedule risks, escalating issues where required
  • Support urgent breakdown planning and reprioritise resources to meet customer needs
  • Review completed visits, service reports and follow-up requirements to support timely closure
  • Maintain accurate planning, customer and installed-base information within business systems
  • Work with Service Managers to balance workload, capacity, holidays, training and regional coverage
  • Contribute to service improvement activities and undertake projects assigned by the Line Manager

KEY INTERFACES

· Service Managers and Team Leaders

  • Field Service Engineers
  • Customers and site contacts
  • Service Sales, Spare Parts and Technical Support teams
  • Projects team
  • Warehouse, purchasing, subcontractors and other support functions

KNOWLEDGE

· Working knowledge of service planning, scheduling and field-service coordination

  • Competence in Microsoft Office, CRM and field-service management systems
  • Understanding of customer service principles, work-order processes and service-level commitments
  • General knowledge of the Company’s products, services and engineer competence requirements
  • Awareness of health, safety and site-access requirements relevant to field-service activities

SKILLS AND ABILITIES

· Highly organised with strong planning and coordination skills

  • Able to prioritise competing demands and respond effectively to changing circumstances
  • Clear and professional written and verbal communication
  • Accurate data entry and strong attention to detail
  • Sound judgement and practical problem-solving ability
  • Able to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams
  • Confident in using scheduling, CRM and reporting systems

CHARACTER ATTRIBUTES

· Customer focused and professional

  • Calm and decisive under pressure
  • Proactive, dependable and accountable
  • Flexible and willing to adapt to operational priorities
  • Positive team player who builds constructive working relationships
  • Continuous-improvement mindset

TYPE AND LEVEL OF EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

· Good general education, including GCSE English and Mathematics or equivalent

  • Previous experience in service coordination, planning, scheduling, logistics or customer support is preferred

title: Senior Customer Program Specialist
description:
About FWD Group

FWD Group (1828.HK) is a pan-Asian life and health insurance business that serves approximately 40 million customers across 10 markets, including BRI Life in Indonesia. FWD’s customer-led and tech-enabled approach aims to deliver innovative propositions, easy-to-understand products and a simpler insurance experience. Established in 2013, the company operates in some of the fastest-growing insurance markets in the world with a vision of changing the way people feel about insurance. FWD Group is listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under the stock code 1828.

For more information, please visit



Job Purpose


Drive the design, execution, and performance management of customer programs that strengthen customer tiering, benefits, and privilege propositions. The role translates customer, business, and channel priorities into practical program mechanics, coordinates cross-functional delivery, and uses performance insights to continuously optimize engagement, experience, retention, and business outcomes for high-value FWD customer segments.


Key Responsibilities:


Customer tier program:

  • Streamline the FWD customer tier structure into a single, clear framework across products, channels and systems.
  • Work with SCB to co-create a compelling and exclusive HNW/UHNW value proposition and engagement model that differentiates FWD in the Thailand HNW domain.
  • Define tier criteria, entry and exit rules, and the benefit, privilege and insurance priority service set for each tier.
  • Build the business case for tier benefits, balancing customer value against cost.

Program execution:

  • Plan and execute tier initiatives end to end, covering operational process, system requirements, SLA and frontline readiness.
  • Work with Products, Distribution, Operations and partners to deliver insurance priority services, privileges and offers on time.

Performance & governance:

  • Track tier take-up, engagement and retention performance, and report results with recommendations.
  • Maintain program governance, documentation and stakeholder updates.
  • Stakeholder management:
  • Establish productive relationships with internal teams, FWD Group and external partners supporting the tier program.

title: Director, Finance Business Systems
description:

The Business Systems Director provides strategic leadership and operational management for the enterprise applications team, focusing on the continuous support, enhancement, and optimization of the cloud-based Oracle Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Oracle Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) systems. This role acts as a key liaison between IT, Finance, Accounting, and Business Operations, ensuring system configurations and reporting capabilities (including OTBI, BI Publisher, and Smart View) are fully aligned with corporate and regional objectives.


Although this is a remote role, candidates must reside in CO, FL, IL, MA, MN, OH, OK, PA, or TX


What you will do:


  • Lead technical and functional support, administration, and strategic enhancement of the Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (GL, FA, CM, AP & Expenses) and EPM Suites (EPRCS, EDM, ARCS)
  • Oversee the planning, budgeting, timeline execution, and risk management of system upgrade releases and corporate system projects

  • Direct, mentor and allocate resources across the team, including Senior Oracle Analysts, Consultants and external technical partners as required
  • Collaborate closely with Oracle to manage vendor relations and contract renewals, ensuring alignment with emerging platform features and updates
  • Design, implement, and maintain various key business system integrations and provide ongoing support and maintenance for various key business systems
  • Work directly with key business system integration partners both internally and externally, such as banking institutions and other key business partners
  • Manage the internal business systems core team



What you will bring:


  • Deep expertise in Oracle Cloud ERP and Oracle EPM Cloud.
  • Proficient in Oracle Reporting and analytic utilities (OTBI, BI Publisher, and Excel Smartview)
  • Strong understanding of financial accounting standards, budgeting/forecasting processes, and corporate organizational structures
  • Analytical problem-solving with the ability to navigate complex business workflows
  • Project Management skills to manage complex projects spanning multiple business units, ownership structures, intercompany relationships, system integrations, and other functions
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Information Systems, Accounting, Computer Science, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).
  • 8+ years of management experience leading corporate systems or IT enterprise applications teams
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting, customizing, and managing Oracle ERP and EPM platforms
  • Demonstrated success in managing cross-functional projects and leading change adoption in standard office and remote environments

Benefits and Compensation:


The annual salary range is $140,000 - $170,000 + potential annual bonus of 15%. Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to geographic location, education, work experience, time in role, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, the Company offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, life and disability insurance, 401k, as well as paid time off and select paid holidays (all benefits are based on eligibility). title: Brand Standards, Guest Experience, & Food Safety Advisor
description:
Want to build a brighter, bolder future and cultivate your career? Join Ecolab’s team and help create a world in which we all thrive.


EcoSure, the brand protection division of Ecolab, partners with global brands to create an end-to-end brand protection strategy. Through a collaborative approach to on-site assessments, coaching, digital learning and industry best practices, we create a unique program that encompasses the critical components of any operation. EcoSure conducts more than 500,000 assessments annually in 140+ countries around the world. The results are real-time insights and actionable steps that mitigate brand risk and optimize guest experience.


Ecolab is seeking a Brand Protection Advisor to join our team in Farmington, NM. As a Brand Protection Advisor, you’ll deliver on-site evaluations, coaching, and insights that elevate food safety, guest experience, workplace safety, and operational excellence. You’ll partner with clients to identify risks, reinforce brand standards, and drive continuous improvement, making a measurable impact on public health and customer satisfaction.


How You’ll Make an Impact:

  • Conduct a variety of brand protection visits at client locations using a foundation of consulting, coaching, and training to meet the unique expectations and program requirements of the clients and help protect their brand and delight their guests
  • Develop and deliver summary presentations of assessment findings, areas of improvement, and recommendations to client leadership
  • Partner with other EcoSure and Ecolab teams to solve client challenges
  • Complete a budgeted number of visits each week, delivering an exceptional client experience
  • Utilize an iPad, Microsoft Suite, and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology to ensure efficient planning and perform essential job functions
  • Support the growth initiatives of our company and our clients
  • Adhere to HIPAA guidelines (where applicable) while completing operational visits within hotels, restaurants, convenience stores, the education sector, healthcare and senior living facilities by interacting with staff and residents

Position Details:

  • Candidate must reside within a commutable distance of Farmington, NM
  • Percent of overnight travel required: 50%
  • Position requires the ability to work occasional evenings, weekends, and overtime as business needs dictate
  • Based on customer requirements, obtaining ServSafe and/or CP-FS certification(s) may be a condition of continued employment

What’s Unique About This Role:

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives and ideas to achieve our best
  • Paid training program that includes job shadowing, e-learning modules, structured field activities, and customized classroom-style training
  • Company-paid vehicle for business and personal use, where applicable
  • Plan and manage your schedule in an independent work environment
  • Be part of a company that values a culture of safety that includes top-notch safety training and personal protective equipment

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma
  • Two years of hospitality industry-related experience
  • Position requires a current and valid Driver’s License with no restrictions
  • Due to the nature and hours of the work, must be 21 years of age or older
  • No Immigration Sponsorship available for this position

Physical Requirements of Position:

  • Being around, touching and potentially consuming food made from or with animal products and/or top allergens
  • Lifting and carrying 25 pounds
  • Inspecting client playgrounds by climbing, crawling in tight areas and going down tube slides
  • Bending, squatting, shifting and adjusting movement to assess areas low to the ground and above the head
  • Standing and walking for extended periods of time in client locations
  • Driving and/or flying to client locations as needed; you are responsible to have the proper documentation to fly such as a Real ID or other acceptable form of identification
  • Driving a company-paid vehicle as required to perform job duties (pre-employment and ongoing motor vehicle record checks will be performed to determine eligibility to drive a company vehicle)

Ecolab is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with a disability.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in culinary, hospitality or business field
  • Multilingual (Spanish & French preferred)
  • High-level customer service and advanced consultative skills
  • Ability to work well under pressure, juggle tasks and work efficiently against deadlines
  • Strong planning and organizational skills and high attention to detail
  • Ability to work effectively without supervision, show initiative, good judgment, and superior decision-making and problem-solving skills

What’s in it For You:

  • Starting on Day 1: Access to our comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, matching 401K, company-paid pension, stock purchase plan, paid parental leave, select discounted childcare resources, and more!
  • The opportunity to take on some of the world’s most meaningful challenges, helping customers achieve clean water, safe food, and healthy environments
  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth
  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best

About Ecolab:

At Ecolab, we prioritize our talent-first philosophy by creating the most capable and diverse team to excel at our nearly three million customer sites. Building on a century of innovation, our 48,000 associates help deliver comprehensive science-based solutions, data-driven insights and world-class service to advance food safety, maintain clean and safe environments, and optimize water and energy use, and improve operational efficiencies and sustainability for customers in the food, healthcare, life sciences, hospitality and industrial markets in more than 170 countries around the world. Our solutions not only enhance operational efficiency but also contribute to sustainability and public health, making a positive impact on the world. We are committed to eliminating unnecessary complexities and embracing a beginner's mindset, continuously seeking new perspectives and innovative solutions to stay ahead in a rapidly changing world.

Annual or Hourly Compensation Range

The pay range for this position is $48,700-$73,000. Many factors are taken into consideration when determining compensation, such as experience, education, training, geography, etc. We comply with all minimum wage and overtime laws.

Benefits

Ecolab strives to provide comprehensive and market-competitive benefits to meet the needs of our associates and their families. Click here to see our benefits.

If you are viewing this posting on a site other than our Ecolab Career website, view our benefits at jobs.ecolab.com/working-here.

description:

Job Description

Bring your EMT skills to a role where every donor interaction helps save lives. At BioLife Plasma Services, you'll use your clinical assessment and patient care expertise to ensure donor safety and support the plasma donation process that makes life changing therapies possible for patients with rare and chronic conditions.


Please take this virtual tour to get a sneak peek of one of our Plasma Donation Centers.

About BioLife Plasma Services

Every day, the donors you meet will motivate you. The high-quality plasma you collect will become life-changing medicines. Here, a commitment to customer service and quality is expected. You will report to the Plasma Center Manager and will perform as a Medical Support Specialist to support plasma center operations.


BioLife Plasma Services is a subsidiary of Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Ltd.


About the role:

Every day, the donors you meet will motivate you. The high-quality plasma you collect will become life-changing medicines. Here, a commitment to customer service and quality is expected. You will determine donor eligibility to donate plasma, management of donor adverse events, review of laboratory test results, and donor notification of unsuitable test results. The Medical Support Specialist works under the guidance of the Center Manager (or Assistant Manager as applicable) for operational guidance and under the management of the Center Physician for medical issues. The Medical Support Specialist will be familiar with regulations of the plasma collection industry or a manufacturing environment. The Medical Support Specialist follows guidance provided by BioLife Medical Affairs and provides center level support of environmental, health and safety (EHS).


How you will contribute

  • You will determine donor eligibility; to include, proper management of informed consent, AIDS education and confidential self-exclusion, medical history interview and acceptance requirements, physical examination, blood testing, and reviewing Serological Protein Electrophoresis (SPE).
  • You will evaluate donor reaction(s), which occurs at the facility as outlined in the SOPs. Follow applicable SOPs for medical emergencies including the development of Center Physician's standing orders and donor transport to emergency care facilities.
  • You will refer to the Center Physician or Medical Affairs (as applicable) when in need of providing unacceptable findings to donors, or guidance concerning medical or technical issues, including donor safety and eligibility.
  • You will support the Hepatitis B and Seasonal Flu vaccination programs for employees as applicable.
  • You will manage employee incidents and determine whether further evaluation is required by occupational health/ER. Refer to EHS guidance regarding employee incidents.
  • You can be a Pandemic Coordinator when authorized by EHS and support investigations associated with pandemic threats within the local community as indicated by EHS or Medical Affairs.


What you bring to Takeda:

  • High school diploma or equivalent to including graduate equivalent of a recognized educational nursing program with state requirements
  • Currently licensed or certified in the state where responsibilities will be assigned: Emergency Medical Technician -Basic (EMT-B), Advanced (EMT-A), Intermediate (EMT-I), and Paramedic (EMT-P), Licensed Practical Nurse / Licensed Vocational Nurse (LPN/LVN), and Registered Nurse (RN)
  • Current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and AED certification
  • Fulfill state requirements (in state of licensure) for basic IV therapy
  • Satisfactorily complete the FDA approved training requirements for BioLife Medical Support Specialist
  • Two years in a clinical or hospital setting


What Takeda can offer you:

Every day at Takeda, we feel good knowing that what we do helps improve the lives of patients with rare diseases. At BioLife, while you focus on our donors, we will support you. We offer a purpose you can believe in, a team you can count on, opportunities for career growth, and a comprehensive benefits program to include medical/dental, paid time off and retirement benefits, all in a fast-paced, friendly environment.



More about us:

At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best in class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that will inspire and empower you to grow through life-changing work.

Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace, in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to bring Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world.

title: Resident Assistant-Kingsport
description:
Resident Assistant-All Shifts

Residents Assistants are an essential part of our wellness team by providing basic personal assistance to the residents in maintaining their highest level of functional independence and psychosocial wellness under the direction and supervision of a RN or LPN.

About American House

Start here, grow your career. American House offers paid training, clear advancement paths, and the chance to build a meaningful future in senior care—one resident at a time. American House Senior Living Communities has served Seniors for more than 40 years. Our Resident Assistants play a vital role in helping residents live with dignity, comfort, and independence.

Job Summary

As a Resident Assistant (RA) at American House, you will play a critical role supporting seniors, enriching their lives, and helping them live their best life. The meaningful relationships you develop will help you support the daily care needs of the residents and support community activities while creating a safe, warm and welcoming environment.---

What You’ll Do

· Assist residents with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), including bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility.

· Monitor residents for changes in condition and report observations to leadership.

· Encourage resident engagement in activities, programs, and social events.

· Follow individualized care plans to ensure high-quality, person-centered care.

· Maintain a clean, safe, and organized environment in resident apartments and common areas.

· Support residents with meals, hydration, and light housekeeping.

· Build positive, respectful relationships with residents, families, and team members.

· Support new resident orientation and help them feel welcome in the community.

Qualifications

· A passion for serving seniors and a compassionate, patient approach.

· Ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

· Previous caregiving, senior living, or healthcare experience required.

· Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 25–50 lbs as needed for resident care.

What We Offer

· Competitive pay and shift differentials

· Paid training and ongoing development

· Opportunities for advancement (Medication Tech, Lead Caregiver, Supervisor roles)

· Supportive, mission-driven leadership

· A workplace culture centered on respect, teamwork, and hospitality

· Benefits available for eligible team members (medical, dental, vision, PTO, retirement options)

Why You’ll Love Working at American House

· Your work makes a real difference every day.

· You’ll be part of a welcoming team.

· You’ll help seniors live with purpose, comfort, and joy.

Apply Today

If you’re compassionate, dependable, and ready to make an impact, we’d love to meet you. Join the American House family and help us enrich the lives of those we serve.

Company Overview

Founded in 1979, American House Senior Living Communities’ vision is to provide high-quality housing for senior at a price affordable for retirees and their families. That vision of excellence has endured for nearly 40 years and expanded to serve residents at a number of senior housing communities. Our mission is to enrich the lives of those we serve, providing an environment that fosters meaningful relationships. Our vision is to be an innovative senior housing company that created sustainable excellence and stakeholder value, with an unparalleled commitment to passionate care provided by compassionate people.

title: Assistent filiaalmanager Nijmegen Centrum
description:
Voor onze winkel in Nijmegen Centrum zijn wij op zoek naar jou! Ben jij iemand die graag de leiding neemt, maar ook zelf actief meewerkt op de werkvloer? Dan is de rol van Assistent Filiaalmanager bij Wibra echt iets voor jou.

Als Assistent Filiaalmanager ben je een meewerkende leidinggevende. Je werkt dagelijks samen met je team in de winkel en ondersteunt de filiaalmanager in het aansturen van het team en de winkel. Je geeft het goede voorbeeld door zelf mee te werken en zorgt er samen voor dat de winkel draait, de schappen gevuld zijn en klanten tevreden de deur uitgaan.

Werken bij Wibra is leuk. Je werkt in een klein team, de winkel is altijd in beweging en de werkdruk kan hoog zijn. Dat betekent dat je fysiek bezig bent, snel schakelt en overzicht houdt. Juist die dynamiek maakt het werk afwisselend en geeft het veel energie. Samen met de filiaalmanager ben je verantwoordelijk voor het reilen en zeilen van de winkel. Je coacht collega’s op de werkvloer, ondersteunt in de planning en zorgt dat alles soepel verloopt. Bij afwezigheid van de filiaalmanager neem jij het voortouw.

Een dag als Assistent Filiaalmanager bij Wibra
Je start je dag in de winkel en begint met een kop koffie en het doornemen van de planning. Vaak werk je met z’n tweeën of in een klein team, je stemt samen af wat er moet gebeuren en gaat daarna direct aan de slag op de werkvloer. Er is vracht binnengekomen, dus jullie zorgen ervoor dat alles snel en netjes in de winkel ligt. Je stuurt collega’s aan waar nodig terwijl je zelf volop meewerkt, houdt overzicht en zorgt dat de winkel er verzorgd en aantrekkelijk uitziet, ook als het druk is.

Tussendoor pak je administratieve taken op, help je collega’s op de werkvloer en werk je samen met de filiaalmanager aan de ontwikkeling van het team. Je springt bij waar nodig en zorgt dat alles blijft draaien. Geen dag is hetzelfde en juist die afwisseling maakt het werk dynamisch en leuk.

Dit is echt iets voor jou als je van aanpakken houdt en energie krijgt van drukte in de winkel.

  • Je hebt ervaring in de Retail, bijvoorbeeld als teamleider, senior verkoopmedewerker of in een vergelijkbare rol

  • Je hebt een mbo werk- en denkniveau

  • Je bent fysiek fit en vindt het fijn om actief bezig te zijn

  • Je vindt het leuk om collega’s aan te sturen en te helpen ontwikkelen

  • Je kunt goed plannen en organiseren, ook als het druk is

  • Je neemt initiatief en pakt verantwoordelijkheid

  • Je houdt van aanpakken en werkt graag actief mee

Dit bieden wij jou

Bij Wibra werken we hard en zetten we samen de schouders eronder. Je komt terecht in een organisatie die groeit en continu in ontwikkeling is, waar jouw inzet echt het verschil maakt. Verder bieden we jou:

  • Bruto maandsalaris tussen € 2.619 en € 2.751 (op basis van 38 uur per week)
    Waar je precies wordt ingeschaald, bepaalt de regiomanager en is afhankelijk van de ervaring die je meebrengt

  • 24 vakantiedagen (op basis van 38 uur per week)

  • Toeslagen op zon- en feestdagen

  • 20% personeelskorting

  • Aangesloten bij pensioenfonds Detailhandel

  • Mogelijkheid tot doorgroeien naar Filiaalmanager

Solliciteer meteen en beantwoord de volgende vragen, we kijken uit naar je reactie!

title: Research Fellow (Level A/B) - AI for EV Battery Repurposing
description:
Overview:

  • Full-time, Fixed Term position for 30 months (Research)
  • Salary Academic Level A ($83,985 - $113,917 p.a.) or Level B ($119,915 - $142,402 p.a.) + 17% Superannuation and Flexible Working Arrangements
  • Primarily based at Melbourne City campus, and the potential to work across other RMIT campuses as required


About the Role
Join RMIT’s School of Engineering and contribute to an industry-connected CRC-P project focused on advancing AI-powered automation for the repurposing of second-life electric vehicle batteries. As a Research Fellow (Level A), you will undertake high-quality research and development activities that support RMIT’s research strategy and help address a growing sustainability challenge in the energy and mobility sectors.


Working independently and collaboratively, you will apply your expertise in robotics, machine learning, battery systems or a related discipline to deliver project outcomes, build productive research partnerships and contribute to high-quality outputs. You will have the opportunity to work with research teams, industry partners and internal stakeholders to develop practical, scalable solutions with real-world impact, while strengthening research networks across RMIT and beyond.


To be successful in this position, you’ll bring research experience and capability appropriate to the level of appointment.

For Academic Level A appointment, you will demonstrate:

  • Emerging research experience relevant to the project, including robotic systems, battery systems, machine learning, AI-powered automation and/or related fields.
  • Ability to clearly communicate research concepts, technical knowledge and project outcomes to academic, industry and project stakeholders.
  • Initiative in research, analysis and problem solving, including the ability to contribute to practical research solutions.
  • Evidence of research engagement appropriate to career stage, such as doctoral research, emerging publications, conference presentations or project contributions.
  • Experience, or the capacity to develop experience, in laboratory-based or hardware-based testing, validation or prototyping of simulation, robotic, AI or battery-related systems.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a research team to meet agreed project outcomes, timelines and milestones.

For Academic Level B appointment, you will demonstrate:

  • Strong research experience relevant to the project, including robotic systems, battery systems, machine learning, AI-powered automation and/or related fields, with evidence of independent research contribution.
  • Ability to clearly communicate complex research concepts, technical knowledge and project outcomes to academic, industry and project stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated initiative in research leadership, analysis and problem solving, including the ability to develop and deliver practical research solutions.
  • A record of research engagement and outputs appropriate to Level B, including publications, collaborations, project contributions and evidence of research impact.
  • Experience in laboratory-based or hardware-based testing, validation or prototyping, including the testing of developed simulation, robotic, AI or battery-related systems.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a research team to meet agreed project outcomes, timelines and milestones.

Qualifications:

  • Mandatory for Academic Level A appointment: PhD or close to submission in robotics, machine learning or other relevant disciplines.
  • Mandatory for Academic Level B appointment: PhD in robotics, machine learning or other relevant disciplines.

Please Note: Appointment to this position is subject to passing a Working with Children and National Police Check.

The Sourcing Associate supports the Source-to-Contract process for assigned R&D categories, including CROs, Lab Services, and Pharma Sciences. Under the guidance of the Sourcing Lead, the role executes RFI, RFP, and RFQ events, conducts market and spend analysis, evaluates supplier proposals, and supports contract and supplier administration.

The role contributes to value delivery, supplier engagement, compliance, and standardized procurement execution. While primarily focused on R&D categories, the Sourcing Associate is expected to flex across other categories as required.

ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Execute RFI, RFP, and RFQ events for R&D categories under Sourcing Lead guidance and in line with Takeda procurement policies
  • Prepare scopes of work, supplier questionnaires, evaluation criteria, and tender packages

  • Conduct market research across CRO, Lab Services, Pharma Sciences, and related R&D categories

  • Support supplier onboarding, due diligence, ethical sourcing checks, and performance milestone tracking

  • Understanding of Source-to-Contract processes, procurement guidelines, supplier management, and governance requirements
  • Experience supporting RFI, RFP, and RFQ processes, supplier evaluation, and contract administration
  • Proficiency with SAP Ariba or equivalent eSourcing tools
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills and ability to analyze spend, pricing, and supplier proposals

PREFERRED

description:

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.


What else is cooking?

title: Professional Learning Specialist – ELA – Morgantown, West Virginia
description:
At Curriculum Associates, we believe in the potential of every child and are changing the face of education technology with award-winning learning programs like i-Ready that serve a third of the nation’s K–8 students. For more than 50 years, our commitment to making classrooms better places, serving educators, and supporting accessible learning experiences for all students has driven the continuous improvement of our innovative programs. Our team of more than 2,500 employees is composed of lifelong learners who stand behind this mission, working tirelessly to serve the educational community with world-class programs and support every day.

*This is NOT a remote position

*A heavy travel requirement. Please read the job description below.


Professional Learning Specialist – ELA – Morgantown, West Virginia

Are you an educator transitioning out of the classroom? This is an excellent opportunity to join a mission-driven company focused on creating equitable classrooms for students and still be part of a school community! Curriculum Associates seeks a Professional Learning Specialist to join our team. The ideal candidate has a background in teaching and/or coaching ELA or Reading, as well as experience leading professional development with school and district leaders.

Successful candidates will show flexibility and synergy with different team members including our Sales team, teachers, students, and school districts as part of day-to-day interactions. The Professional Learning Specialist will be responsible for providing targeted professional development, ongoing in-classroom support, data analysis, daily project management, and communication with district and site leaders. Dynamic, engaging leaders who are interested in making a lasting and direct impact with the way schools teach ELA/Reading to students from grades K–8 are encouraged to apply.


Why join this team:

  • Work with multiple stakeholders across large audiences.
  • Attend educational conferences related to your role.
  • Experience new environments and challenges on a day-to-day basis.
  • Collaborate in a supportive environment filled with feedback loops, a strong virtual community, and shared best practices.
  • Help districts choose and implement a product with lasting impact on learning.

The impact you'll have:

  • Become an expert on the company’s online Diagnostic and Instruction program, as well as core and supplemental products, with an emphasis on ELA or Reading
  • Support districts in selecting and implementing a product with lasting impact on learning
  • Work with multiple stakeholders across large audiences
  • Support district-wide adoptions of Curriculum Associates’ products
  • Help to ensure equity in the classroom by delivering professional learning to teachers, coaches and leaders on how to effectively implement Ready and i-Ready to impact classroom learning
  • Meet teachers where they are and provide tailored on-site support to teachers, coaches and leaders. This may range from providing lesson planning and pacing support, to helping educators analyze data and apply it to instruction, to working with leaders to identify evidence of implementation successes and challenges
  • Collaborate with district leader and site leaders to develop and revise annual professional learning plans and schedules
  • Serve as a thought leader for Curriculum Associates, exemplifying the company’s mission-driven approach and commitment to creating better classrooms for students and teachers
  • Stay current and attend company- provided educational conferences related to your role, when scheduling permits, and participate in team-provided development
  • Experience new environments and challenges on a day-to-day basis
  • Collaborate in a supportive environment filled with feedback loops, a strong virtual community, and shared best practices

Who we're looking for:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of experience in teaching ELA or Reading, coaching teachers of ELA or Reading, or providing ELA or Reading professional development learning. A Master's degree in ELA or Reading is preferred
  • Fluency using digital tools including online assessments, and a high level of comfort discussing and applying data with teachers and leaders
  • An understanding of principles of adult learning and how to apply them to professional learning
  • Ability to manage, monitor, evaluate, and ensure integrity of program implementations
  • Ability to provide high-quality classroom coaching to ensure teachers have the skills necessary to deliver CA solutions effectively
  • Willingness to travel within designated territory as well as to company meetings several times throughout the year (once safe to do so)
  • Candidates with a strong working knowledge of the State Standards for ELA or Reading for Grades K–8 (or comparable state standards), including both the content standards and the practice standards

Employees can enroll in our company’s 401k plan and receive an employer match. Employees have access to a flexible vacation and sick policy in addition to twelve paid holidays and a winter office closure between Christmas and New Year's, as well as a number of additional perks and benefits. Ability to keep all travel points for flights and hotels booked for work-related travel. Mileage reimbursement may be available for applicable travel.


Salary Range for this role: $60,750 - $99,750

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that Curriculum Associates considers in making compensation decisions based on our Compensation Philosophy. Actual base pay within that range will vary based upon several factors including, but not limited to, prior experience and relevant skill sets.
