title: Senior Software Engineer I
description:
A Senior Software Engineer I is an independent contributor who delivers moderately complex, production-quality software within a defined product or service scope.


They translate business requirements into secure, maintainable systems that support customer and business outcomes.


They are recognized as knowledgeable in core systems within their team and contribute to engineering quality, operational health, and team capability under guidance.


Technical Excellence:

  • Produces clear design documentation using the architectural principles.
  • Builds systems with solid foundations in performance, resilience, extensibility, and security
  • Applies testing strategies that improve deployment confidence
  • Makes pragmatic trade-offs between speed, quality, and maintainability within defined constraints.
  • Demonstrates strong code quality and provides constructive, actionable feedback within the team.
  • Introduces small-scale improvements to patterns, tools, or techniques within their immediate team.
  • Solves moderately complex technical problems with pragmatic, well-reasoned solutions.
  • Shares technical knowledge with peers and contributes to team-level practices.

Operational Excellence:

  • Takes responsibility for the operational health of components within their scope.
  • Uses monitoring, logging, and metrics to identify potential issues.
  • Builds systems with operational considerations in mind (fault tolerance, recoverability).
  • Contributes to incident response and post-mortem analysis.
  • Maintains runbooks, operational documentation, and knowledge-sharing material
  • Actively reduces technical debt in assigned areas, improving stability and maintainability.
  • Ensures security and software updates are applied to owned systems.
  • Incident frequency and MTTR decrease with team support.

Product Delivery & Business Impact:

  • Breaks down requirements into technically feasible tasks.
  • Delivers high-quality software with predictable cycle times and low change failure rates under guidance.
  • Collaborates with Product to align solutions to user and business outcomes
  • Reduces delivery risk through thoughtful design and incremental validation.
  • Identifies opportunities to simplify systems and remove unnecessary complexity.
  • Contributions directly support measurable business and customer outcomes
  • Delivery is predictable with low change failure rates.
  • Technical solutions meet expected reliability, cost, and time-to-market goals.

Leadership & Collaboration:

  • Communicates technical topics clearly to engineers and immediate stakeholders.
  • Synthesizes peers' input to make pragmatic recommendations.
  • Builds strong working relationships within the team and with close cross-team partners.
  • Demonstrates accountability, ownership, and bias for action.
  • Provides mentorship and guidance to less-experienced engineers through code reviews and pair programming.
  • Stakeholders trust their technical recommendations

Qualifications:

  • Typically 4+ years of professional software engineering experience
  • Proven delivery of large complex global multi-tenant production systems across multiple components
  • Experience translating ambiguous requirements into scalable solutions
  • Experience working in Agile cross-functional product development teams

Technical Skills:

  • Strong proficiency in C# (.NET), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), and SQL (PostgreSQL).
  • Strong system design skills, including SOLID, design patterns, API design, DDD, and event-driven architectures.
  • Experience designing and building modern web applications with React, Vite, REST, and GraphQL.
  • Experience building and operating cloud-native applications on AWS (EC2, Lambda, S3, SNS, SQS, Elastic Beanstalk), with a focus on reliability and observability.
  • Champions testing, DevSecOps, CI/CD (GitHub Actions), and Secure SDLC practices.
  • Proficient with observability and analytics tools such as Splunk and Mixpanel.
  • Proficiency with AI-assisted development using GitHub Copilot, Amazon Bedrock, and agentic AI workflows.

title: Overnight Street Sweeper (CDL B) – Full-Time
description:
JOB TITLE: Overnight Street Sweeper (CDL B) – Full-Time
LOCATION: 1250 Reames Rd, Middle River, MD 21220
HOURS: 3rd Shift
COMPENSATION: $22-$23 / Hour - Eligible for First Pay Increase at 6 Months
TRAVEL: Minimal (1-10%)

Who we are:
Sweeping Corporation of America (SCA) is the nation’s leading street sweeping company, operating in over 20 states and supporting more than 600 municipalities, counties, and government agencies. With over six million miles serviced annually, SCA is uniquely focused on the delivery of high-performance street sweeping, jet-vac, and environmental services. SCA has built its entire organization, its people, processes, technology, and investments around providing uninterrupted, accountable, and results-driven services tailored to the needs of our clients. Our mission is to provide essential sweeping and environmental services that support cleaner, safer, and more sustainable communities.

Your daily impact:
As our next Street Sweeper, you'll be at the heart of our mission—delivering essential services that help improve public safety and enhance environmental quality. In this role, you’ll take ownership of assigned routes, drive the street sweeper, and operate specialized equipment to keep streets clean and well-maintained.
The job responsibilities below outline the core duties and expectations of a position, providing clarity on how the role supports Company goals. However, not all duties can be listed, and as business needs evolve, responsibilities may shift over time to reflect new priorities, processes, or technologies:

Safety & Inspection: Perform required pre-trip and post-trip inspections of equipment in accordance with company standards. Ensure all safety features are operational before beginning route.
Execution: Review assigned routes thoroughly prior to departure. Be proactive in asking clarifying questions if the route or expectations are unclear. Complete assigned jobs within the allotted timeframe while maintaining expected quality and attention to detail.
Equipment Operation: Operate equipment safely and efficiently at all times, following all traffic laws, company safety procedures, and site-specific protocols. Exercise additional caution during inclement weather or challenging site conditions.
Material Handling: Handle materials safely and securely; Apply correct procedures for material types and disposal sites.
Reporting: Report any equipment issues, malfunctions, near misses, crashes, or injuries within 30 minutes or as soon as safely possible. Immediately escalate opportunities, work issues, or safety concerns to management.
Professional Communication: Maintain a professional attitude and appearance while representing the company on job sites or in public areas. Communicate effectively with team members, supervisors, and clients when needed.
Compliance & Documentation: Accurately complete required logs, manifests, and forms.
Adaptability & Problem Solving: Respond appropriately to changes and challenges; identify and solve issues timely.
Regular & Predictable Attendance: The ability to consistently report to work on time and as scheduled, with minimal unexcused absences. This includes being present and prepared to work throughout assigned shifts, and reliably adhering to start times, breaks, and end times.

Minimum Job Requirements:
Minimum job qualifications define the essential skills, experience, and abilities needed to succeed in the role. They set the baseline for hiring but may evolve as the job and business requirements change:

Education: High School or GED
Experience: 1 year DOT driving experience – waste & recycling services experience preferred
License: CDL-B & DOT Medical Card
Age: Must be at least 21 years of age
Compliance: Must maintain an acceptable driving record and successfully pass a motor vehicle record (MVR) check, background check, and drug screening in accordance with Company policy and applicable law.

Skills & Competencies:
Skills and competencies define the abilities and behaviors essential for success in the role. They guide performance expectations and may evolve as the role, team, or business priorities change:

Safety & Compliance Focus: Ability to follow safety procedures, conduct inspections, operate equipment responsibly, and comply with all traffic, site, and regulatory requirements.
Operational Execution & Reliability: Strong ability to plan routes, complete work efficiently and accurately, adapt to changing conditions, and maintain consistent, dependable attendance.
Communication & Issue Reporting: Effectively communicate with supervisors and teammates, represent the Company professionally, and promptly report equipment issues, incidents, or safety concerns.

Safety is #1:
Our safety culture is more than a policy—it’s a mindset. We have a full-time safety team, rigorous training programs, and detailed operating procedures to protect our people and the communities we serve. You’ll be supported from Day One with the tools and knowledge to work confidently and safely.

Benefits & Wellness at SCA:
We believe great people deserve great perks. When you join SCA, you’re not just keeping the streets clean—you’re paving the way to a better future (with some solid benefits under the hood).
Here’s what we’ve got in our hopper:

401(k) with Match: Plan for the long haul—retirement is another kind of clean sweep.
Weekly Pay: Consistent weekly pay you can count on, plus on-demand pay so you can access earned wages when you need them.
Health, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance: Take care of what matters most with benefits designed to support you and your family’s wellbeing and future.
Short- & Long-Term Disability: If life throws a pothole your way, we help you keep rolling.
Indemnity Insurance: Extra protection for life’s unexpected detours.
Paid Time Off & Holidays: Even the best machines need downtime.
Training Programs: Shift into high gear with learning and career advancement opportunities.
Team Focus: We show up for our customers and each other, every day.
A Culture that Cares: People are the heart of everything we do, fostering a culture of respect, safety, and growth
Rooted in Respect: A company with a name people know & trust - built on relationships, community pride and a people focused approach to leadership.

Physical Requirements:
Physical requirements outline the essential on-the-job demands needed to perform the role safely and effectively.

Work Environment & Exposure: Constant work outdoors with regular exposure to weather, elements, and traffic; occasional exposure to loud noise, dust/debris, and jarring conditions; limited exposure to chemicals.
Physical Demands: Frequent sitting and walking/standing; occasional bending, twisting, squatting, kneeling, pushing/pulling; limited stair climbing and crawling; ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs at varying heights, including overhead.
Cognitive & Sensory Requirements: Continuous reading, screen use, mental focus, and hand-eye coordination throughout the workday.
Equipment & Tools: Operation of specialized equipment (e.g., mechanical broom sweeper) and use of hand controls, foot controls, and fine motor skills.
Safety & Protective Gear: Required use of appropriate PPE, including high-visibility apparel, eye, ear, hand, foot, head, lung, and skin protection.

Ready to sweep your career to the next level? Apply today and join the SCA team!

Identifies recurring issues, recommends and implements process improvements, and maintains departmental procedures.

Facilitates communication between stakeholders and documents outcomes to ensure smooth transitions and successful adoption of changes.

Coordinates with external vendors to integrate services, resolve problems, and ensure alignment with internal standards and timelines.

Netflix’s Ads UK Measurement team is looking for a new Ads Measurement Specialist to join the team in a fixed-term role covering a period of leave. The person in this role will work cross-functionally with sales, marketing, consumer insights, data science, and vendor partners. This role requires the ability to work independently, apply strong attention to detail, and collaborate effectively across teams. For more information about Netflix’s culture, read Seeking Excellence.


This is a 12 month Fixed Term Contract


Key Responsibilities


  • Produce research and insights that communicate the Netflix Ads UK proposition to the marketplace and advertiser clients in areas such as audience insights, reach and frequency, campaign verification, and campaign measurement.
  • Use proprietary and syndicated tools to create regular reporting for internal and external stakeholders on the Netflix Ads UK audience in comparison to competitors.
  • Integrate measurement outputs into clear client-facing insights, present findings independently to clients and agencies, and offer guidance on optimizing media mix.
  • Manage the day-to-day effectiveness study process with third-party vendors from end to end, including sales requests, vendor intake, survey drafting, analysis, report creation, and presentation, while working closely with Sales Account Managers.
  • Partner with the UK Advertising Sales team on day-to-day measurement requests.
  • Lead client learning agendas, partnering with advertisers to create category-specific learning agendas and playbooks.
  • Manage product and engineering projects related to bringing complex measurement integrations to market.
  • Bring strong knowledge of TV/video and digital media, including the benefits of TV advertising and the Netflix Ads audience in the UK.
  • Develop case studies from ongoing and completed analyses.



Experience & Skills


  • At least 7 or more years of experience in media measurement and research at streaming, TV, or digital media companies or media agencies.
  • Strong understanding of methodology, data, and systems from syndicated research providers (e.g. Barb, GWI, TechEdge) and direct digital technology and analytics.
  • Experience with effectiveness measurements such as reach and frequency, incremental lift, brand lift, matched-market testing, A/B testing, marketing mix models, and bespoke campaign effectiveness studies, including questionnaire scripting.
  • Strong knowledge of the advertising landscape across all kinds of media channels and methods of buying, with TV-focused experience preferred.
  • Strong presentation skills with senior client-facing experience.
  • Dual TV/video and digital experience is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to generate strategic insights from rigorous analysis.
  • Experience managing projects independently with strong attention to detail.
  • Experience building and following processes to make working methods more efficient.
  • Able to adapt to a startup environment with ambiguity.
  • Builds strong relationships with clients and colleagues; values diverse perspectives for better decision-making.
  • Ability to interpret data thoughtfully and identify meaningful insights.
  • Excellent writing and presentation-building skills.

title: Senior Editor, Conferences & Events
description:
Location: Pensacola,Florida,United States

About the Role

Bionews is looking for a Senior Editor to build and lead the editorial strategy and content programming across live and virtual rare disease conferences and events. In this role, you will shape the narrative by curating high-impact agendas, securing interviews, delivering real-time reporting, and transforming complex industry trends into compelling digital content. As an editorial leader, you will bridge the gap between journalism and experiential production, collaborating across content, audience development, sales, and our advocacy teams to deliver best-in-class event coverage that’s credible, accessible, and engaging for our audiences.

Work Format & Travel

This is a remote position with frequent travel required to attend conferences in person (expected to attend 3-4 in-person events per year). Expect travel to fluctuate seasonally based on the conference calendar.

What You'll Do

Content Strategy & Conference Planning

  • Develop and execute the editorial strategy across a range of rare disease conferences, aligning coverage with audience needs and business objectives
  • Identify high-impact research, clinical developments, emerging trends and technologies, as well as other newsworthy stories
  • File timely, accurate stories under deadline pressure from the conference floor
  • In collaboration with the Events Manager, lead conference planning, including editorial calendars, coverage priorities, freelance staffing and assignments, budgets, and pre- and post-conference content
  • Attend select conferences in person, covering keynote sessions, new data, and patient/advocacy news as it happens
  • Partner with advocacy, editorial, news, audience development, and commercial teams to maximize the impact and reach of conference coverage

Content Development

  • Lead the end-to-end editorial process for conference coverage, from story ideation and assignment through reporting, editing, fact-checking, and publication
  • Assign, edit, and publish high-quality, factual news stories, research summaries, interviews, and analyses
  • Ensure coverage is accurate, timely, and engaging to the intended audience, translating complex scientific information into clear stories
  • Uphold the highest-level editorial standards, journalistic integrity, scientific rigor, and organizational guidelines
  • Conduct interviews with researchers, clinicians, advocacy groups, and industry leaders
  • Coordinate onsite reporters, freelancers, and contributors
  • Serve as a senior editorial lead at key conferences, leading fast-paced news coverage
  • Recruit, vet, and onboard a roster of freelance reporters capable of covering medical and scientific conferences
  • Manage freelancer budgets, deadlines, and performance

Cross-functional partnership

  • Partner with the Advocacy team and external advocacy organization partners to identify key sessions, connect with sources, and align coverage with community priorities
  • Work with the News team to ensure conference coverage integrates with broader editorial planning and breaking news needs
  • Work with the Patient Advisory Board and the Community team to understand what audiences want from conference coverage and incorporate that feedback into strategy
  • Report on coverage performance and continuously refine the conference coverage strategy based on audience engagement and community input

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of journalism experience, including experience covering medical, scientific, or health-related conferences
  • Demonstrated experience managing or editing freelance writers
  • Strong news judgment and ability to identify newsworthy angles quickly, including under deadline pressure
  • Excellent editing skills, with close attention to accuracy and AP style
  • Experience building relationships with sources, including researchers, clinicians, patient advocates, and advocacy organizations
  • Strong project management skills — able to juggle multiple freelancers, conferences, and deadlines simultaneously
  • Comfortable and effective working cross-functionally with editorial, advocacy, community and sales teams
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently to attend conferences (expected to be at 3-4 conferences a year)
  • Bachelor's degree in journalism, communications, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

Preferred:

  • Existing familiarity with the rare disease, chronic illness, or broader patient advocacy landscape
  • Experience with a content management system and basic multimedia reporting (photo/video/social from the field)

title: Senior Network Engineer
description:
Senior Network Engineer
Edinburgh

Hybrid
Permanent
£Competitive + benefits + flexible working



FNZ is on a mission to make wealth management more accessible, inclusive, and scalable worldwide. Supporting investment platforms used by over 20 million people, our EU/UK Network Engineering team underpins the critical infrastructure that powers global wealth technology.



We’re looking for an experienced Senior Network Engineer to join our Platform Services function. Reporting into the Network Engineering leadership team, this role will provide deep hands-on technical expertise across FNZ’s enterprise network estate, supporting the stability, performance, security, and ongoing optimisation of our on-prem, hybrid, and cloud environments.



What you’ll be doing



As Senior Network Engineer, you’ll be a key technical contributor within the regional Network Engineering team, helping to maintain, improve, and evolve secure, resilient, and high-performing network services across FNZ.



Your responsibilities will include:


Network Operations & Engineering

  • Supporting the operation, maintenance, and optimisation of FNZ’s enterprise network infrastructure
  • Acting as a senior escalation point for complex network incidents and service issues
  • Troubleshooting and resolving network performance, availability, and connectivity issues
  • Supporting lifecycle management activity including upgrades, patching, configuration improvements, and infrastructure refreshes
  • Ensuring network services remain highly available, secure, and aligned to business needs



Design, Delivery & Improvement

  • Contributing to the design and delivery of network solutions for new and existing systems
  • Working with Network Architecture to implement new tooling, infrastructure, and network capabilities
  • Evaluating existing technologies and recommending practical improvements
  • Helping to enhance automation and reduce manual, repeatable network tasks
  • Supporting continuous improvement of operational procedures, standards, and documentation



Collaboration & Stakeholder Support

  • Working closely with Platform Services, Infrastructure, Security, Cloud, and business teams to deliver reliable network outcomes
  • Supporting project delivery alongside BAU operational responsibilities
  • Providing clear technical updates, recommendations, and analysis to engineering leads and stakeholders
  • Translating technical issues into clear business impact, risks, and resolution options



What we’re looking for


You’ll be a highly capable hands-on network engineer who thrives in complex, high-availability environments and understands the importance of secure, resilient infrastructure in supporting business-critical platforms.


Essential experience:

  • Strong experience configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting enterprise-class network environments
  • Experience supporting complex network infrastructure across on-premises, hybrid, and public cloud environments
  • Strong incident response and problem-solving experience in business-critical environments
  • Strong understanding of network availability, performance, resilience, and security principles
  • Technical expertise and practical experience in:
  • Strong experience with Cisco Nexus switching technologies
  • Advanced Layer 2 and Layer 3 network design and troubleshooting
  • Proven expertise in OSPF and BGP routing protocols
  • Overlay and fabric technologies such as VXLAN and NSX-T
  • Network security principles and secure network design
  • Traditional ADN platforms, including F5 LTM/GTM

Desirable experience in the below areas would be advantageous:

  • Checkpoint and Fortigate firewall solutions
  • F5 Distributed Cloud
  • Network automation and orchestration, such as Terraform, Ansible, or CI/CD pipelines
  • Cloud networking across AWS, Azure, or GCP
  • LogicMonitor or similar enterprise-grade monitoring platforms



What you’ll need to succeed at FNZ


  • A strong technical mindset with excellent attention to detail
  • Calm, structured problem-solving skills in complex operational environments
  • Excellent communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and automation
  • The ability to balance operational stability with change and innovation
  • A strong sense of ownership, accountability, and delivery focus
  • A collaborative style with the ability to work effectively across teams



Why join FNZ?



At FNZ, you’ll work at the intersection of finance, technology, and global scale, alongside highly skilled teams who are shaping the future of wealth management.


We offer:

  • Competitive salary and benefits
  • Flexible and hybrid working options
  • Global career opportunities across UK, EU, US, Canada, South Africa and APAC
  • Private health and life insurance
  • Fully funded training and development
  • Paid parental and volunteer leave
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance culture



Ready to help shape enterprise networks at global scale?


Apply now to join FNZ as a Senior Network Engineer and use cutting-edge technologies to help power the infrastructure behind the world’s leading wealth platforms.


#LI-CW1




About FNZ


FNZ is committed to opening up wealth so that everyone, everywhere can invest in their future on their terms. We know the foundation to do that already exists in the wealth management industry, but complexity holds firms back.


We created wealth’s growth platform to help. We provide a global, end-to-end wealth management platform that integrates modern technology with business and investment operations. All in a regulated financial institution.


We partner with the world’s leading financial institutions, with over US$2.5 trillion in assets on platform (AoP).

Together with our clients, we empower nearly 30 million people across all wealth segments to invest in their future.

title: Associate Director, Clinical Supplies
description:
PTC Therapeutics is a global commercial biopharmaceutical company. For over 25 years our team has been deeply committed to a unified purpose: Extending life’s moments for children and adults living with a rare disease.

At PTC, we cultivate an inclusive culture where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team, fostering a strong sense of belonging.

Visit our website to learn more about our company and culture!
Site:

Job Description Summary:

The Associate Director, Clinical Supplies is responsible for operational oversight of the forecasting, planning, packaging, labeling, distribution, reconciliation, and destruction of Clinical Trial Materials (CTM) and any additional study medication/products to support PTC global clinical trials and serves as the Lead Clinical Supplies team member.

He/she is responsible for oversight and management of PTC clinical supply distribution and Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) and distribution providers.

The incumbent works closely and collaborates with PTC internal departments, third party vendors (including but not limited to: Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs), Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and shipping agents) and clinical study site representatives to ensure the availability of CTM at study sites globally.

The Associate Director, Clinical Supplies, ensures operations and activities are executed in accordance with all internal Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and in accordance with all local, county, state, and federal laws and regulations including current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) regulations, GCP, FDA and International Conference on Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines.

The incumbent works cross-functionally with internal departments and external resources on Clinical Supply related issues.
.

Job Description:

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


Primary duties/responsibilities:

Clinical Supplies Planning

  • Ability to read, interpret, and provide feedback on clinical protocols.
  • Engages in cross-functional planning at the program level, providing leadership on clinical supplies matters to ensure alignment across teams.
  • Ability to use the Protocol along with projected and real time data to create and manage a forecast demand for a given clinical trial and at the program level.
  • Leading the design of the packaging for the Clinical Trial.
  • Develop and manage the label text and proof generation process including the development of the Master English Label Text and working with a vendor to provide translations and regulatory information for the countries participating in the clinical trial.
  • Ensure primary and/or secondary packaging and labeling designs are maintained in accordance with product stability, clinical study dosing/dispensing, and local regulatory requirements.
  • Schedules and implements labeling, packaging and quality release operations with CMOs and internally with the Quality department to ensure continuous clinical supply.
  • Assist in the development of the clinical trial Pharmacy Manual.
  • Prepare CTM-related information presented at investigator meetings and ensure it is accurate, clear and compliant.
  • Ensures consistency across the program for presentation of investigational product, as applicable.
  • Define, test, and approve Interactive Voice Response/Interactive Web Resources (IVR/IWR) system specifications and user requirements for tracking inventory, allocation, distribution, use by-date management, destruction activities, reports, and alerts.
  • Accountable for ensuring the CTM-related information presented at investigator meetings is accurate, clear, and compliant.

Financial Management

  • Identify vendors/resources, create Request for Quote (RFQ), and lead negotiation of pricing and processing of the legal documents required to engage the vendor’s services.
  • Create, maintain, and monitor the clinical program budget.
  • Work with Finance if changes are required to the budget.
  • Work with Procurement to generate purchase orders/requisitions.
  • Responsible for the review of monthly invoices from vendors and aid accounts payable when an invoice is received.

Project Management

  • Manage the development of timelines for production release and distribution of clinical trial material.
  • Ability to influence other departments and vendors without direct management to ensure the clinical trial timeline is achieved.
  • Recognize potential study risks in advance and provide risk mitigation options.
  • Maintain “audit-ready” state ensuring investigational medicinal product (IMP) regulatory documentation is ALCOA+ and archived in the appropriate document repository.
  • Provide a monthly status report on assigned clinical trials to upper management.
  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to achieve the clinical trial timeline.
  • Participates in clinical study team meetings; advises the study team on the optimal supply strategy, aligns with study details and collaborates in achieving study objectives by providing supporting information to the study teams as required and communicates and discusses clinical trial supply timelines, cost and risk limitations.
  • Ensures receipt, documentation and resolution of product complaints and incidents from investigator sites.

Inventory Management

  • Monitor IMP inventory levels at regular intervals.
  • For expired supply; determine if the use-by date should be extended or request destruction where applicable.
  • Compare IRT inventory periodically to vendor inventory to ensure accuracy, if applicable.
  • Compare current inventory to projected consumption rate to assess the health of the IMP and to determine if/when additional campaigns will be required.
  • Work with vendors regarding the return, accountability, and destruction of IMP.
  • Responsible for adjudication of temperature excursions that occur at the Contract Distribution and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO), clinical site facilities, and while IMP is in transit to the clinical site.

Distribution

  • Define finished good IMP supply chain utilizing Distrbution Depots where required.
  • Monitor to ensure IMP shipments are being dispatched and received in a timely manner.
  • Ensure both clinical sites and Depots are performing IRT transactions where applicable.
  • Schedule and monitor QP release within the UK and EU and work with QP to ensure the Product Specification File (PSF) is up to date and contains all the necessary documentation required to release the IMP.

Process Improvement

  • Identifies and drives process improvement initiatives, taking ownership of implementation and outcomes.

People

  • Manages workload allocation for junior staff supporting assigned clinical supply activities across protocols and programs.
  • Acts as a coach and mentor to staff members across the team.
  • Can participate in interviews and hiring staff.
  • Leads by example to encourage others to prioritize personal and professional development.
  • undefinedPerform other tasks and assignments as needed and specified by management.undefined

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES REQUIRED

* Minimum level of education and years of relevant work experience.

  • Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 8 years of relevant clinical drug supplies experience in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, contract research organization (CRO), university medical center or related environment or Master’s degree with 6 years of relevant clinical drug supplies experience.

* Special knowledge or skills needed and/or licenses or certificates required.

  • Hands-on experience supporting and understanding GMP, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and ICH guidelines as related to CTM labeling, packaging and distribution operations and the overall drug development process.
  • Hands-on experience supporting clinical supply chain for clinical trials.
  • IRT (IVRS and/or IWRS) experience
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (including MS Project).
  • Excellent verbal and written communication and skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively, as required, in a fast-paced, matrixed, team environment consisting of internal and external team members.
  • Analytical thinker with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.
  • Excellent planning, organization and time management skills including the ability to support and prioritize multiple projects.
  • Experience shipping clinical supplies to domestic or international locations including knowledge of the shipping documentation required for both.

* Travel requirements

  • 10-20%

Expected Base Salary Range: $165,500 - $194,700. The base salary offered will be contingent on assessment of candidate education level, background, and experience relative to the requirements of the position they are being considered for, as well as review of internal equity.

title: Advisor, Bioanalytical Chemistry
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Orna Therapeutics, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company, is an innovative biotechnology startup based in Watertown, MA, committed to developing groundbreaking therapies for diseases that current approaches cannot address. With our pioneering circular RNA technology, developed at MIT, we are at the forefront of advancing the next generation of RNA therapeutics. Our pioneering expression and delivery platform positions us to tackle complex diseases, including B cell-driven autoimmune disorders, B cell malignancies, sickle cell disease, and beyond.


We are seeking an experienced scientist with expertise in liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to lead bioanalytical method development, validation, and sample analysis supporting pharmacokinetic (PK) and protein biomarker assessments across drug development programs. This role will contribute scientific and technical leadership to cross-functional teams supporting discovery studies, including biotherapeutics and novel modalities (e.g., LNP, RNA-based therapeutics).


Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and qualify LC-MS/MS methods for quantifying protein/peptide biomarkers and PK analytes in biological matrices (plasma, serum, tissue) in accordance with FDA/EMA Bioanalytical Method Validation (BMV) guidance
  • Lead technical strategy for immunoaffinity-LC-MS/MS (IA-LC-MS/MS) or hybrid LBA-LC-MS approaches for large-molecule and biomarker analysis
  • Oversee sample analysis campaigns supporting animal studies, including troubleshooting matrix effects, parallelism, and assay robustness issues
  • Author and review method validation protocols, reports, and SOPs; ensure compliance with regulatory and quality standards
  • Serve as scientific point of contact for CRO partners, overseeing method transfer, technical review, and data quality
  • Collaborate with discovery teams to support study design and interpretation of bioanalytical data
  • Present data and technical rationale in cross-functional settings
  • Mentor junior scientists and contribute to department-level technical training and process improvement

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences or related scientific discipline with 3+ years of relevant industry experience


Additional Skills/Preferences

  • Hands-on expertise with LC-MS/MS instrumentation (e.g., triple quadrupole, high-resolution MS) for quantitative protein/peptide bioanalysis
  • Understanding of PK assay development principles and regulatory bioanalytical guidance (FDA 2018 BMV, EMA equivalents)
  • Experience with large molecule/biotherapeutic bioanalysis (e.g., biomarker proteins, mAbs, fusion proteins, novel modalities)

title: Receiving Assistant
description:
Salary Range

USD $19.50/Hr. -

Overview

The Job in a Nutshell:

The Receiving Assistant is responsible for assisting the Receiving Manager in the successful operation of the receiving department.

Responsibilities

Main Ingredients:

  • Providing World Class Customer Service as a number one priority.
  • Exemplifying integrity, responsibility, and excellence and adhering to all policies.
  • Assisting the receiving department manager in accurately receiving all incoming products including date, accuracy and damage checking.

  • Assisting in training and monitoring of department personnel including assigning and following up on tasks.

  • Continually increasing product knowledge.
  • Using SAP and inventory management software, emailing and utilizing other IS programs as needed.
  • Working a schedule based on store needs which includes evenings, weekends, holidays. Position requires working five days, 40 hours per week and attending mandatory store meetings.
  • This position has limited Manager on Duty but is never intended to be the overall Manager on Duty for the store.

Although this is a general outline of job responsibilities all employees are expected to be “hands on” and do whatever it takes to get the job done and make the company thrive.

Qualifications

  • High School diploma, GED or equivalent preferred.

Employees are required to accomplish any and all tasks assigned to them by their Manager and/or other Store Support Center manager that might not be listed in this job description.

Provides medical care to patients under the supervision of a physician. Conducts physical examinations, orders and interprets diagnostic tests. PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:


  • Participation in daily inpatient rounding by taking patient history, conducting physical exam, reviewing laboratory and diagnostic data, performing medication reconciliation, procedures, and computer order entry as appropriate. Participation in daily multidisciplinary round by contributing specific surgical perspective and promoting integrated comprehensive patient care

  • Active team participant in mentoring and educating other team members
  • Inpatient consultation and admission at the direction of the collaborating physician.
  • Documentation of all patient encounters by computerized progress notes, brief operative note, procedural notes or admission/consultation/discharge summary dictation

Evaluates and treats patients with acute, chronic, and surgical concerns which include the following:

  • Admission/consultation of patients at the direction of the collaborating physician
  • Conduct medical history; performance of physical examination
  • Collection, interpretation & recording of diagnostic clinical laboratory data
  • Ordering, specimen collection & interpretation of all relevant laboratory/microbiological tests
  • Ordering & interpretation of all relevant radiologic/US/MRI/NM studies
  • Ordering, performance & interrelation of cardiac diagnostic testing
  • Diagnosis of acute and chronic conditions affecting all organs systems
  • Development of treatment plans
  • Ordering medications
  • Address the pharmacologic needs of patients by CPOE/written/oral methods


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS REQUIRED:

  • Dispense & Administration of medications
  • Performance medication reconciliation
  • Formulating interventions and performing therapeutic measures to ensure the appropriate individualized plan of care is implemented.
  • Applying knowledge of age specific needs, (pediatric, adolescents, adult and geriatric) to plan of care interventions and patients' responses to care
  • Activity & diet level designation
  • Ordering/renewal of restraints
  • Performance of rounds & recording of computerized written and/or dictated documentation of all patient encounters by computerized progress notes, brief operative note, procedural notes or admission/consultation/discharge summary dictation
  • Pre-operative patient evaluation and medical optimization
  • Post-operative patient ICU and floor management
  • Coordinating information flow among medical, ancillary, nursing, financial and insurance personnel
  • Facilitate and direct BLS/ACLS measures as necessary
  • Participation in Clinical & multidisciplinary rounds by contributing specific surgical perspective & promoting integrated comprehensive patient care, & assisting with discharge planning
  • Provide relevant patient education and counseling regarding heath status/test results/disease process & discharge planning
  • Address patient psychosocial needs by assessing patient's functional status & evaluating patient's mental status by Consultation/Referral to other health professionals & community agencies
  • Assessing clinical factors including, but not limited to, immunosuppression complications, drug toxicity, infections complications and risk rejection
  • Coordinating care of recipient and/or living donor as needed
  • Communicating frequently with referring physicians regarding the patient's status
  • Perform any other clinical responsibility within the PA's level of training and scope of practice
  • Assist the collaborating physician in any intervention in the interest of patient care/safety
  • Functions fully within the Outpatient and Inpatient setting
  • Providing on-call coverage for medical triage for outpatients in collaboration with the physician on-call

The expertise and experiences you’ll need to succeed:

  • Master's in Nursing or Physician Assistant Studies
  • One + years’ experience

LICENSURE, CERTIFICATION OR REGISTRATION REQUIRED:

  • Valid American Heart Association BLS & ACLS certifications
  • Licensure as a Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner in the State of Florida.
  • NCCPA or APRN Certification

All the benefits and perks you need for you and your family:

  • Benefits from Day One: Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Disability Insurance

  • Paid Time Off from Day One

title: Associate Director for Strategic Retention and Persistence
description:
Department:

Carla.Harcleroad@oregonstate.edu

Job Summary:

    The Division of Academic Affairs and University Advising and Educational Engagement is seeking an Associate Director for Strategic Retention and Persistence. This is a full-time (1.00 FTE), 12-month, professional faculty position.

    Reporting to the Executive Director of University Advising and Educational Engagement (EDUA&EE) within the Office of Undergraduate Education (OUE), the Associate Director for Strategic Retention and Persistence plays a central role in advancing OSU’s institutional commitment to achieving an 86% graduation rate with no opportunity gaps by 2030. The position leads and contributes to campus‑wide initiatives designed to identify and remove barriers to student retention at the policy, institutional, and direct‑support levels.

    The Associate Director collaborates closely with units across the Office of Undergraduate Education, student‑success partners throughout the university, Enrollment Management, Institutional Research, and senior leadership. Through these partnerships, the role analyzes policies, procedures, and structural factors that impede student progression and develops innovative, equity‑minded solutions that strengthen retention and completion outcomes.

    A key responsibility of the position is leading campus committees and working groups to map the student experience, identify friction points, and propose interventions that enhance persistence. This work includes designing and recommending direct student support programs, policy revisions, and institution‑wide strategies grounded in principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion.

    The Associate Director conducts research to understand students’ decisions related to enrollment, retention, and attrition, using these insights to inform both short‑term and long‑term strategies that advance OSU’s student success goals. Over time, the role may also oversee a team of retention specialist caseworkers, providing leadership and direction for individualized student support efforts.

    Key Responsibilities

    Strategic Retention and Persistence Management - 75%

    • Lead and project manage campus-wide student success initiatives related to retention and persistence in alignment with OSU’s strategic plan

    • Identify barriers to retention and create initiatives, policies, and programs to remove those barriers in order to support student retention and success

    • Serve as a key collaborator with OUE units, the colleges, Student Affairs, Institutional Research, and Enrollment Management to support strategic retention efforts

    • Participate in and coordinate with various campus- and division-level student success and care teams

    • In collaboration with senior leadership, develop strategies and initiatives to meet short- and long-term retention and completion goals

    • Provide direct retention and persistence support to a caseload of students as needed.

    • Supervise Strategic Retention Team members as needed.

    Student Persistence and Retention analysis and research - 20%

    • Utilize disaggregated student persistence and retention data to evaluate past interventions, guide future programming, and monitor persistence and student success outcomes

    • Research, develop, implement, and assess innovative policies and procedures related to retention and student success

    • Conduct research and analysis to understand why students leave, stop out, and/or return to OSU after an absence

    Other Duties including service - 5%

    • Serve on division and campus-wide committees as a subject matter expert for retention and completion initiatives

    Qualifications:

    Required Qualifications:

    • Master’s degree in student affairs, higher education, business, counseling, or another related field
    • Minimum of five years of work experience in higher education or a related field
    • Knowledge of theories and practices related to student success, retention, and graduation
    • Evidence of a commitment to inclusive excellence and experience conducting work to close opportunity gaps in higher education
    • Ability to manage multiple activities concurrently, continually monitor their status, and prioritize activities so deadlines are met with limited supervision
    • Ability to work with detailed information with attention to accuracy; strong skills in documentation, tracking, and data collection
    • Proven success in innovative thinking to develop and implement creative solutions to complex challenges
    • Ability to work collaboratively and constructively with people at multiple levels and with diverse perspectives
    • Demonstrated experience leading or project managing within a complex organization, such as a higher education institution
    • Ability to access, understand, and interpret data from multiple sources to promote student success through data-informed and innovative practices
    • Evidence of the ability to build consensus across multiple divisions of a complex organization
    • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to work diplomatically and effectively with campus partners.

    This position is designated as a critical or security-sensitive position; therefore, the incumbent must successfully complete a criminal history check and be determined to be position qualified as per University Standard: 05-010 et seq. Incumbents are required to self-report convictions and those in youth programs may have additional criminal history checks every 24 months.


    Preferred Qualifications:

    • Direct student advising experience (financial aid advising, academic advising, student affairs advising, disability support advising, etc.) at a large public institution
    • Supervisory and/or mentoring experience.
    • Experience with process mapping, policy analysis and/or project management
    • Experience implementing strategic initiatives to support the retention and success of underserved student populations
    • Past experience managing complex change initiatives in a collaborative, consensus-building environment
    • Experience teaching, advising, leading, and/or mentoring diverse undergraduate students
    • Experience leading a unit

title: Lathe Operator
description:
Job Title: Lathe Operator

Location: Bakersfield
Employment Type: Full-Time
Pay Rate: $19.00–$21.00+ per hour + Commission Opportunity

Position Overview

Legacy Staffing is seeking a skilled and motivated Lathe Operator on behalf of an industrial manufacturing client. This position is responsible for setting up, operating, and monitoring conventional lathe equipment to produce high-precision components used in oilfield and industrial applications.

The ideal candidate will have machining experience, strong blueprint-reading skills, and a commitment to producing high-quality work while meeting production goals. This role offers a competitive hourly wage plus commission opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Machine Operation

  • Operate lathes, mills, and other machining equipment safely and efficiently.
  • Monitor machine performance to ensure production goals and quality standards are met.
  • Maintain continuous production flow while minimizing downtime.

Setup & Machine Adjustments

  • Perform machine setup and changeovers as required.
  • Load raw materials using overhead lifting equipment and material handling devices.
  • Set offsets and make minor program adjustments to optimize machine performance.
  • Verify tooling and machine settings before production runs.

Quality Control

  • Conduct first-article inspections and in-process quality checks.
  • Use precision measuring instruments including micrometers, calipers, gauges, and other inspection tools.
  • Interpret engineering drawings and specifications to ensure parts meet required tolerances.
  • Document inspection results and report any non-conforming conditions.

Maintenance & Safety

  • Monitor tooling wear and replace tooling as necessary.
  • Perform basic preventative maintenance and housekeeping activities.
  • Remove chips and debris to maintain safe operating conditions.
  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures, including proper use of PPE.
  • Report equipment issues or safety concerns immediately.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Previous machining experience in a manufacturing environment required.
  • Experience operating CNC, lathes and/or conventional machining equipment preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret complex blueprints, drawings, and job specifications.
  • Ability to understand machining tolerances and quality requirements.
  • Willing to work other areas of the yard on downtime.

Technical Skills

  • Knowledge of:
    • Turning operations
    • Boring operations
    • Facing operations
    • Drilling operations
    • Threading operations
  • Experience with precision measuring instruments.
  • Ability to perform basic machine troubleshooting and offset adjustments.
  • Mechanical aptitude and strong problem-solving skills.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand for extended periods throughout the workday.
  • Ability to work in a heavy industrial manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to safely lift and move materials using overhead cranes and lifting devices.
  • Capability to perform repetitive motions and physical tasks associated with machining operations.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Commitment to safety and quality.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Excellent time-management and organizational skills.
  • Strong work ethic and reliability.
  • Ability to meet production deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Pay: $19.00–$21.00+ per hour DOE
  • Commission Opportunity Available
  • Potential for career growth within a stable manufacturing environment

If you have machining experience and take pride in producing precision parts while maintaining high safety and quality standards, we encourage you to apply. Legacy Staffing is proud to connect skilled trades professionals with rewarding opportunities in manufacturing and industrial operations.

title: Manufacturing Systems Analyst
description:
Manufacturing Systems Analyst

Job Description

Join the team behind iconic brands like Huggies®, Kleenex®, Cottonelle®, Scott®, Kotex®, Poise®, Depend®, and Kimberly-Clark Professional®. At Kimberly-Clark, it’s all here for you—innovation, growth, and the chance to make a real impact.

At the KC Warren Plant, we are building more than a manufacturing facility—we are building a High Performance Work System (HPWS) where employees are empowered to make decisions, solve problems, develop new skills, and directly influence business results.

Our culture is built around shared leadership, continuous learning, accountability, and respect for people. Employees are expected to contribute ideas, challenge the status quo, and work collaboratively to improve safety, quality, reliability, and performance every day.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The purpose of this role is to own the execution of the KCNA Digital Manufacturing strategy for the plant; focused on equipment, capability building, and value delivery. He/she will be a technical expert and support the advancement of major digital systems, processes, and capabilities to achieve a highly connected, operationally efficient, and effective manufacturing environment across the plant. Incumbent will also champion and support all other mobile digital applications used by the site (i.e. Poka, Seeq, Schedule Pro, etc.), in alignment with other Kimberly-Clark North America facilities. This role is viewed as an expert in complex application environments, encompassing both business process understanding and technical expertise. Influential communication, growth mindset, and the ability to strategically navigate at multiple levels of a diverse plant organization are important in this role. Key stakeholders include, but not limited to, KCNA Supply Chain Digital teams, Plant leaders, DTS, Engineering and Plant teams.

This role is responsible for the digital manufacturing strategy execution at the site level, in alignment with the KCNA Digital Strategy, as well as effectively leading business objectives for the site. The incumbent will work with project teams compiled of employees from multiple disciplines. This role will have interaction across sites and opportunities for involvement in broad based business projects. Objectives typically are focused at the plant level for safety, quality, continuous improvement, productivity, cost, internal control, asset management, and team capability development, but should drive standardization across KCNA. Incumbent reports to the site Continuous Improvement Leader.

As a person, you’re a learner – a natural leader – someone who is always taking initiative to make things better and bring others along with you. You live your life in alignment with the highest values of integrity and quality, always ensuring your responsibilities become a long-term success story. In this role, you’ll help us deliver better care for billions of people around the world. It starts with YOU.

About You

In one of our manufacturing roles, you’ll focus on winning with consumers and the market, while putting safety, mutual respect, and human dignity at the center. Job responsibilities include:

  • Provide analytical support for the data contained within and generated by the respective manufacturing system.

  • Site lead for deployment of SMOM (Smart Manufacturing Operations Management) system, ensuring the success by providing technical expertise and effective facilitation of the process.
    • Develop and maintain data flows into SMOM (manual entries, PLC inputs, etc.) for generating information (reports, dashboards etc.)
    • Support development and implementation of plans/programs for sustaining the long-term growth of SMOM to meet sector objectives.
    • Provide technical and operational expertise to achieve quick and timely solutions to SMOM related problems within all site asset team areas.

To succeed in this role, you will need the following qualifications:

  • Exposure to Lean and demonstrated examples of application of LEAN principles, (minimum of a blue belt).

  • Direct experience with large, interconnected software systems such as SAP ERP, MES, PLM, etc.

title: Filiaalmanager Bennekom
description:
Voor onze winkel in Bennekom zijn wij op zoek naar jou! Ben jij een leidinggevende die het liefst midden op de werkvloer staat? Bij Wibra ben je geen manager op afstand, maar een meewerkende leidinggevende. Je werkt dagelijks samen met je team in de winkel en geeft leiding door zelf het goede voorbeeld te geven. Samen zorgen jullie ervoor dat de winkel draait, de schappen gevuld zijn en klanten tevreden de deur uitgaan.

Werken bij Wibra is leuk. Je werkt in een klein team, de winkel is altijd in beweging en de werkdruk kan hoog zijn. Dat betekent dat je fysiek bezig bent, snel schakelt en continu het overzicht houdt. Juist die dynamiek maakt het werk afwisselend en geeft het veel energie. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het reilen en zeilen van de winkel: je coacht je team op de werkvloer, maakt duidelijke planningen en houdt de focus op resultaat en klanttevredenheid. Samen met je team en de regiomanager zorg je ervoor dat alles blijft lopen , ook op de drukke momenten.

Een dag als filiaalmanager bij Wibra
Je start je dag in de winkel en begint rustig met een kop koffie en het doornemen van de planning voor de dag. Vaak werk je met z’n tweeën of met een klein team, je stemt samen af wat er moet gebeuren en gaat daarna direct aan de slag op de werkvloer. Er is vracht binnengekomen, dus jullie zorgen ervoor dat alles snel en netjes in de winkel ligt. Je stuurt aan terwijl je zelf volop meewerkt, houdt overzicht, verdeelt het werk en zorgt dat de winkel er verzorgd en aantrekkelijk uitziet, ook als het druk is.

Tussendoor pak je administratieve taken op, coach je collega’s op de werkvloer en werk je aan de ontwikkeling van je team. Je voert sollicitatiegesprekken en hebt contact met de regiomanager over de voortgang van de winkel. Geen dag is hetzelfde en juist die afwisseling maakt het werk dynamisch en leuk.

Dit is echt iets voor jou als je van aanpakken houdt en energie krijgt van drukte in de winkel.

  • Je hebt ervaring als (Assistent) Filiaalmanager of Teamleider

  • Je hebt een mbo werk- en denkniveau

  • Je bent fysiek fit en vindt het fijn om actief bezig te zijn

  • Je geeft graag leiding en doet dit door zelf mee te werken

  • Je kunt goed plannen en organiseren, ook als het druk is

  • Je bent resultaatgericht en houdt van aanpakken

  • Je bent duidelijk en weet je team te motiveren


Dit bieden wij jou

Bij Wibra werk je hard, maar daar staat ook iets tegenover. Je komt terecht in een organisatie die groeit en waar jouw inzet echt het verschil maakt. Verder bieden we jou:

  • 32 - 38 uur per week

  • Bruto maandsalaris tussen € 2.670 en € 3.038 (op basis van 38 uur per week)

Fargo ND

title: Intern | Energy Practice | Paris
description:
Who We Are:


We are one of the world’s leading economic consulting firms. We strive to recruit and develop talented people to work together to produce meaningful economic analysis of exceptional quality, and to create a positive impact on our clients and society.


Our extensive expertise in the various Energy market ranges from market design & regulatory issues, strategy development and market modelling to comprehensive expert work in civil and antitrust / competition proceedings and carrying out due diligences for transactions. We work with utilities, energy infrastructure operators, large end-users of energy, energy regulators, law firms and investors.


You will work on both quantitative modelling and regulatory issues through a range of international projects.

Our work combines cutting-edge economic research, deep energy sector expertise with applied market and financial modelling to help clients navigate the rapid transformation of energy systems.

Our recent public studies include, among others, a report for Business Europe on European competitiveness in the energy and climate transition, a report for Eurelectric on the evolution of system flexibility needs and the evolving concept of security of supply, a report for Naturgy Foundation on the evolution of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and a report for the Clean Air Task Force on the deployment of clean power technologies.


About the Role

We are looking for an Intern to join our Paris team in Spring 2027 for a period of up to 6 months. Interns typically join during or shortly after completing their Master’s degree. Please indicate your availability and preferred duration in your cover letter.

This is an opportunity for candidates with a strong quantitative background to apply their skills to complex energy and carbon market modelling, financial modelling, regulatory analysis, and strategic advisory in a leading global economic consultancy.

You will be based at Compass Lexecon’s central Paris office, and work closely with other consultants and experts located across our European offices.


Duties & Responsibilities:


  • Contribute to economic and financial analysis in the context of the energy transition towards low carbon technologies
  • Support the development and enhancement of our internal market and financial models (e.g. decarbonisation pathways, asset valuation, policy impact assessments, contract pricing)
  • Conduct market research and policy analysis on electricity, gas, and carbon markets issues
  • Work in an international team on cross-office projects with colleagues across Europe, gaining exposure to diverse regulatory environments and energy systems
  • Present insights to senior team members and support delivery to clients (drafting, contribution to client presentations and expert evidence)

Skills and Profile Sought:


  • Currently undertaking or recently completed a Master’s degree in Economics, Finance, Engineering, Statistics, or a related field
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Financial modelling and quantitative skills; hands-on experience with financial models (e.g., asset valuation, project finance, transaction support) is a plus
  • Proficiency in MS applications including Outlook, Excel, and Word; experience with programming tools such as Python or R is a plus
  • Fluency in French and English is required, other languages are a plus
  • German-speaking skills are highly appreciated
  • Strong organisational and prioritisation skills
  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative environment
  • Previous internship experience in the energy sector is desirable.

Benefits of working at Compass Lexecon:


  • Competitive salary and benefits
  • A wide variety of interesting and challenging projects
  • An international team with a broad range of backgrounds and experience
  • A blend of professional and academic environments
  • A steep learning curve, coupled with a supportive and collaborative team
  • Consideration for a permanent position post internship.

Please apply online with your CV and Cover Letter.

Compass Lexecon is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Development Coordinator - UC Irvine
description:
At a glance

📣 Looking to build a career in fundraising and philanthropy? I’m excited to be partnering with UC Irvine to find their next Development Coordinator! This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who wants to get their foot in the door of advancement and gain hands-on exposure to the many pieces that make a Planned Giving program successful. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to:✨ Learn the ins and outs of Planned Giving alongside a supportive leader invested in your growth✨ Work across donor stewardship, marketing, events, prospect management, and gift administration✨ Partner with colleagues across both the university and health enterprise✨ Build toward a potential future in frontline fundraising You do not need Planned Giving experience to be considered. A background or interest in fundraising, nonprofits, communications, marketing, or business could translate well. We’re looking for someone who is curious, highly detail-oriented, self-motivated, and excited to learn! 📍 Irvine, CA | Hybrid – 3 days onsite💰 $29.74–$34.52/hour Interested or know someone who might be?

Description: What you'll be doing

Another Source’s client, University of California, Irvine, is recruiting a Planned Giving Coordinator to join their team in Irvine, CA. This is a hybrid opportunity working 3 days onsite.

Here’s a little about University of California, Irvine:

In 1965, the University of California, Irvine was founded with a mission to catalyze the community and enhance lives through rigorous academics, cutting-edge research, and dedicated public service. A top public university, UCI has become internationally recognized for improving lives through research and discovery, fostering excellence in scholarship and teaching, and engaging and enriching the community. Today, UCI continues to inspire change and pioneer new ideas with the support of its generous partners, alumni and friends.

Through the combined efforts of the University Advancement & Alumni relations team, the university is able to share its amazing achievements, build lasting relationships and generate support for important campus programs and initiatives. University Advancement seeks to strengthen contributions in research, education, and service; accelerate the university's place among globally preeminent research universities; and bring together passions, skills, and creativity to further improve people's lives.

The UC Irvine Office of Planned Giving is an integral component of this effort, helping donors create lasting legacies through estate gifts and charitable vehicles. Planned gifts have become an increasingly important source of philanthropic support for UC Irvine, providing future resources that will sustain scholarships, research, healthcare, faculty excellence, and innovative programs for generations to come. As the university continues to experience significant philanthropic growth, the Office of Planned Giving works closely with donors, professional advisors, and campus partners to facilitate meaningful charitable giving opportunities that align donors’ personal, financial, and philanthropic goals with the long-term priorities of the university.

About this role:

Under the direction of the Executive Director of Planned Giving, the Planned Giving Coordinator provides high-level administrative support, project management, and operational coordination to the Executive Director of Planned Giving and the Planned Giving Team. The Planned Giving Coordinator must possess the ability to work collaboratively with advancement colleagues and interact effectively with donors, prospects, professional advisors, trustees, executors, and campus stakeholders.

Your Contribution Will Likely Include:

Planned Giving Team & Administrative Support

  • Manage the calendars of the Planned Giving team, prioritizing meetings and choosing between conflicting appointments.
  • Coordinate and schedule meetings with departmental staff, faculty, university officers and administrators, Trustees, donors and others.
  • Maintain the department Annual Calendar of Events and Activities.
  • Initiate, compose, revise and process a variety of correspondence, reports, contact reports, memoranda, and confidential mailings for the Office of Planned Giving.
  • Prepare drafts and final copies of correspondence and gift agreements for the Executive Director’s signature using standard business and university formats.
  • Prepare marketing and other materials as needed.

Donor Relations, Stewardship & Events

  • Communicate tactfully and diplomatically with diverse groups of people, including Vice Chancellors, Deans, Directors, high-level business executives, major donors, and government officials.
  • Independently interpret and respond to a wide range of requests for information, data, background and biographical information.
  • Maintain confidential donor records, planned gift documentation, estate administration files, and related correspondence with university policies and applicable regulations.
  • Engage in a variety of stewardship activities, including via phone or email as needed, and ensure consistent tracking and stewardship of Legacy Society members.
  • Coordinate and support cultivation, stewardship, and educational events designed to engage donors, professional advisors, executors, trustees, and prospective planned giving donors.
  • Plan and coordinate details for the Annual Luncheon for UCI’s Legacy Society and workshop series, donor cultivation stewardship events, and quarterly meetings with professional advisors.

Prospect Management, Research & Reporting

  • Compile and maintain reports on program activities and results, providing information on program trends and basic analysis of data.
  • Independently gather data from a variety of sources, evaluate and analyze data, and prepare detailed information and recommendations for the Executive Director involving individual/corporate biographical information, charts, graphs, budget information, special projects, and presentations.
  • Provide Prospect Management support for the Planned Giving team.
  • Conduct research on alumni, friends, corporations, and foundations to identify prospects, prepare prospect lists, and assist in prospect screening activities.
  • Identify relationships between and among individuals and organizations and conduct appropriate donor follow-up with prospects.
  • Assist with the identification and tracking of planned giving prospects through analysis of donor giving history, engagement, wealth indicators, and estate planning interests.

Gift & Estate Administration

  • Manage the Planned Giving database, overseeing all data entry, imports and exports, data integrity, reporting, cleanup, and tracking.
  • Manage the multi-step gift processing procedure, including check processing within 24 hours of receipt of gift, collecting gift reports, preparing gift transmittal forms, and obtaining signatures for approval and delivery to Gift Administration.
  • Manage the multi-tiered acknowledgement process, including communicating new gifts to campus partners as appropriate.
  • Monitor estate administration matters and maintain records related to probate proceedings, trust administrations, estate distributions, and realized planned gifts.
  • Review gift reports and implement appropriate recognition and stewardship of all donors, including gift acknowledgement letters, stewardship reports and honor roll.
  • Follow the established gift acknowledgement matrix and assist the Executive Director with preparing follow-up correspondence and action items.
  • Coordinate mailings to donors and prospective donors, including welcome letters, renewal notices, pledge reminders, newsletters and follow-up packages after donor recruitment events.

Experience You Will Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training; significant work experience could substitute for the degree.
  • Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the campus and/or medical center and with external constituencies.
  • Good organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills. Resourceful in finding appropriate solutions to problems and initiative in presenting alternatives and implementing solutions to ensure effective change. Ability to anticipate problems and take necessary action to eliminate or mitigate potential negative effects.
  • Ability to be flexible in working independently as well as collaboratively with Advancement and faculty and staff to achieve defined goals. Use initiative to organize and follow through with complex tasks to meet deadlines.
  • Skill to use a personal computer and computer software programs at the level of sophistication required for the development office. Proven ability to use MS Office programs, and familiarity with the Internet to conduct searches.
  • Possess traits of good judgment and discretion in communicating with colleagues and constituents.
  • Skill to maintain confidentiality.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and poise in dealing with diverse contingencies including, among others, influential community leaders, University leadership, faculty, administrative personnel and volunteer groups.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with individuals at all levels.
  • Skill to develop reports, proposals and external relations materials.
  • Proven excellent organizational skills. Demonstrated ability to prioritize workload, meet deadlines, and work with frequent interruptions under constantly changing priorities.
  • Proven level of outstanding professionalism in providing executive assistance to supervisor including: scheduling meetings, coordinating all travel and lodging arrangements, liaison to faculty and staff, prioritizing incoming mail, screening telephone calls and general office management.
  • Superior ability to write clear, concise reports, summaries of donor and prospect information, correspondence and public relations materials with minimal direction. Superior ability to review, rewrite and edit all correspondence, from letters to emails, prior to dissemination.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of records management including the proven ability to develop and maintain a system to track and update a variety of information including an accurate detailed calendar. Demonstrated ability to operate office equipment proficiently.
  • Interest in learning and growing in a fundraising environment.
  • Experience in independently planning all aspects of special events.

Preferred Experience:

  • One to two years of office administrative support in a development setting preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Salesforce.
  • Knowledge of UCI policies and accounting forms such as invoices, travel vouchers, purchase orders, and check requests.
  • Familiarity with various gift-planning vehicles, including charitable gift annuities, charitable remainder trusts, charitable lead trusts, pooled income funds and bequests.
  • Experience working with SalesForce Marketing Cloud or other graphics programs.
  • Working knowledge of various University policies and procedures.
  • Familiarity with estate distribution processes related to wills and trusts.
  • Interest in learning about planned giving.

Special Conditions:

  • May be required to drive on occasion in order to perform the routine or essential job responsibilities for the position. Must possess a valid California driver license and participate in the DMV Pull Notice Program.

What’s in it for you:

The anticipated hourly salary range for this position is $29.74 - $34.52 per hour.

Another Source works with their clients, on a retained project basis. We are committed to building inclusive candidate pools as we partner with hiring teams. As you read through the job posting and review the list of qualifications (required and/or preferred), please do not self-select out if you feel you do not meet every qualification. No one is 100% qualified. We encourage you to apply and share your story with us.
