title: Asset Genius Strategic Program Lead
description:
When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Asset Genius Strategic Program Lead


Location(s)

GSK (Collegeville) - Customer Site PA

Job Description

The Asset Genius Strategic Program Lead is the single point of contact for oversight, accountability, and delivery of the Asset Genius program at a OneSource key account. Asset Genius is a OneSource technology that provides utilization insights for lab-based instruments that benefit the customer in multiple ways. These insights enable smarter capital investments, instrument fleet planning and operational decisions on service contract spend, which deliver significant impact to the customer’s Pharma R&D organization.

This role sits at the intersection of technical asset data and business decision-making, translating equipment utilization insights into action across instrument service contract renewals, capital planning, asset decommissioning, and overall fleet strategy. This is a client-facing role that partners closely with the client on both strategy and execution. Key to this role is matrix leadership, leading a cross-functional team and leading by influence at both the strategic and tactical level. The ideal candidate pairs a technical foundation (engineering, data-science or scientific background) with business acumen (MBA) to bridge the various functions which have a touchpoint with Asset Genius, such as R&D Lab Operations, Finance, Procurement, Capital Champions, and Instrument Management Owners.

This is an onsite position in Upper Providence, PA.

Job Responsibilities

Program Ownership, Strategy and Execution

  • Serve as the single point of contact for overall oversight and accountability across all Asset Genius workstreams, ensuring monthly, quarterly, and annual cadences are followed
  • Develop, maintain and execute the strategy for Asset Genius in partnership with the client
  • Act as the link between the client's Asset Genius strategy and the client-based OneSource technical teams, ensuring license deployment and data needs remain aligned with that strategy
  • Lead OneSource’s account-based cross-functional Asset Genius team, driving execution of the strategy and delivering results to the client
  • Monitor program performance in-line with client needs and proactively anticipate any client concerns or operational challenges
  • Report out on program activity and progress, summarizing license connection activity and economic value delivered to the client across each strategic pillar, demonstrating progress toward strategic objectives
  • Partner with client capital champions to embed OneSource tools into the client’s instrument management processes, including those for new capital purchases and end-of-life decisions
  • Facilitate discussions with the client to review Asset Genius recommendations, track follow-up actions, and drive them to closure
  • Engage internal site-based teams to ensure recommendations, such as decommissioning an asset, are acted on as needed

Continuous Improvement and Innovation

  • Drive continuous improvement of client-based Asset Genius processes to achieve greater process efficiency or improved business outcomes
  • Advocate across OneSource Digital product development team to ensure customer needs are clearly understood and translated into product design requirements
  • Own the launch and training of new products and features at client sites to improve adoption of utilization insights for CAPEX and OPEX decision making
  • Partner with Asset Genius leads within OneSource to bring outside-in best practices back to his/her client
  • Develop and regularly update OneSource documentation, best practices and RACIs to ensure consistency of performance

Critical Skills

  • Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to lead by influence especially in a matrix organization
  • Strong leadership presence, with the ability to lead a team and foster teamwork
  • Technical problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent customer service skills, complemented by the ability to listen to and interpret client requests
  • Aptitude for technical and practical matters
  • Strong financial acumen and experience
  • Strong analytical and quantitative reasoning abilities
  • Self-motivated and willing to learn
  • MS Office Skills: Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Teams

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related technical/scientific discipline
  • MBA (or equivalent) required
  • Minimum of 5 years of work experience in a technical environment
  • Demonstrated leadership ability, with a minimum of 2 years in a leadership role with direct reports and/or cross-functional team matrix environment
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills for interacting with peers, managers, customers, and other technical support professionals are critical to success in this role
  • Travel requirement of up to 20%

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $120,000 to $145,000. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

PerkinElmer is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, or veteran status or any other characteristics protected by applicable law. PerkinElmer is committed to a culturally diverse workforce.

Working at MLH means carrying the mission forward of caring for our community and impacting the lives of patients in every way through compassion, a deliberate focus on service expectations and a consistent thriving for excellence.

A Brief Overview
Performs daily activities for cleaning, disinfecting, sterilizing and storing of endoscopes and accessories. Maintains inventory levels and ensures proper care and operation of equipment. Assists in care of patients undergoing endoscopic examinations and invasive procedures under the direction of the physician or RN. Models appropriate behavior as exemplified in MLH Mission, Vision and Values.

What you will do
  • Pre-cleans, tests, decontaminates, inspects, disinfects and/or sterilizes endoscopes in accordance with industry standards, guidelines and regulations, and manufacturers’ instructions for use.
  • Identifies and uses all appropriate methods related to sterilization and disinfection to prepare endoscopy scopes, supplies, and equipment needed for endoscopy procedures.
  • Participates in quality monitoring and evaluation activities; documents and maintains daily records of QA and sterilization functions.
  • Ensures that supplies and equipment are maintained and ready for use on an as needed basis and are returned to correct storage areas.
  • Maintains and ensures adherence to the sterile field by applying principles of aseptic techniques in accordance with regulatory guidelines and infection control procedures.
  • Provides technical assistance to the physician for patients undergoing endoscopic procedures.
  • Ensures the procedure room is fully equipped for patient procedures. Sets up procedure room, equipment and supplies; ensures equipment is in proper working order.
  • Prepares patient for procedures with follow through of physician orders, assists with explaining procedure to patient, drapes and positions patient, and connects monitors to patient as needed.
  • Assists with monitoring patient’s physiological status continuously during procedure according to established guidelines. Notifies physician/RN of any significant changes.
  • Under the direct supervision of an RN, provide post-procedure care for patients undergoing endoscopy and conscious sedation.

Education/Formal Training Requirements
  • Required - High School Diploma or Equivalent
  • Preferred - Technical Degree or Diploma GI/Endoscopy

Work Experience Requirements
  • Preferred - experience working as a tech in the GI Lab or experience with care, handling, and assembly of surgical instrumentation and supplies and sterilization practices 1-3 years

Licenses and Certifications Requirements
  • Required - BASIC LIFE SUPPORT - American Heart Association

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
  • Knowledge and practice of basic patient care concepts and application of the principles of asepsis preferred.
  • Work requires the ability to read and understand complex instructions and perform basic arithmetic calculations.
  • Ability to perform the role of endoscopy tech for invasive procedures.
  • Ability to take emergency on-call responsibility on 24-hour rotating basis.
  • Ability to understand and prepare moderately complex written materials, such as patient records.
  • Ability to communicate verbally with Associates, physicians and other outside professionals.
  • Ability to work without close supervision and to exercise independent judgement.
  • Ability to organize multiple tasks and projects and maintain control of workflow.

Supervision Provided by this Position
  • There are no supervisory or lead responsibilities assigned to this job.

Physical Demands
  • The physical activities of this position may include climbing, pushing, standing, hearing, walking, reaching, grasping, kneeling, stooping, and repetitive motion.
  • Must have good balance and coordination.
  • The physical requirements of this position are: medium work - exerting up to 50 lbs. of force occasionally and/or up to 25 lbs. of force frequently.
  • The Associate is required to have close visual acuity including color, depth perception, and field of vision to perform an activity, such as assessing patients, preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; or extensive reading.
  • Frequent invasive and non-invasive patient contact.
  • Exposure to patient body fluids as well as exposure to hazardous or poisonous materials.
  • Ability to react quickly to emergency situations.

title: Operations Associate - Parametric
description:
ABOUT MORGAN STANLEY
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, wealth management and investment management services. With offices in more than 41 countries, the Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments, institutions and individuals. For further information about Morgan Stanley, please visit www.morganstanley.com.

ABOUT PARAMETRIC
Parametric is part of Morgan Stanley Investment Management, the asset management division of Morgan Stanley. We partner with advisors, institutions, and consultants to build portfolios focused on what is important to them and their clients. A leader in custom solutions for more than 30 years, we help investors access efficient market exposures, solve implementation challenges, and design multi-asset portfolios that respond to their evolving needs. We also offer systematic alpha and alternative strategies to complement clients' core holdings.

This role is part of Parametric's hybrid working model, which includes working in the office 3 days a week and choosing to work remotely or in the office the remaining days of the week.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The operations department consists of a team of professionals that focuses on the overall operations of Parametric. This group ensures the production process is complete from start to finish and lines up with the goals and functions of other departments within the firm. Examples include supervising, organizing and completing daily production, measuring and evaluating daily workload, and providing services to ensure the business runs as smoothly and effectively as possible.

THE ROLE
As part of the Global Operations Team, the Operations Associate is responsible for ensuring the timely and accurate completion of responsibilities set out below. Creating a Follow the Sun model between locations will require close collaboration and clear hand-offs to ensure service and operations excellence. Work closely on a set list of standard and ad hoc tasks that need to be performed during non-US market hours, and then provide a status report at local end of day. This role may continue to take on additional responsibilities over time, as opportunities and benefits are identified.

Onboarding at Parametric is responsible for setting up new client accounts to enable trading activity across equity and derivative products. The team covers equity and derivative shell building and flipper activities, with responsibilities that include building accounts in line with client documentation, transition analysis, and internal requirements. Onboarding partners closely with Client Service, Portfolio Management, Operations, and Oversight teams to ensure accounts are accurately established, restrictions are correctly applied, and accounts are progressed efficiently through to readiness for trading.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Complete daily assigned operations transactions, which includes new account setup, account activity verification, contact updates, etc. Do so in an accurate, timely, and comprehensive manner.
  • Research and resolve issues quickly and with a sense of urgency and accuracy.
  • Communicate with internal and external contacts regularly to resolve issues, confirm information, provide status updates or information, among others
  • Collect observations and turn into actionable insights and recommendations for improvement.
  • Perform verification checks on similar work done by others on the team, to ensure accuracy of information
  • Ensure thorough and accurate record keeping/maintenance of client records and files.
  • Maintain metrics and data
  • Ad-hoc and project work as needs arise

JOB QUALIFICATIONS
Required Experience: 3-6 years

Primary Skills

  • Bachelor’s Degree preferably in related discipline such as economics, finance, or banking; work experience in lieu of degree will be considered.
  • Familiarity with MS Office and the ability to learn additional internal/ external software programs
  • Relationship-building skills and ability to thrive in team environment
  • Ability to work independently and self-manage high volumes of data with tight deadlines
  • Strong attention to detail & highly process oriented
  • Strong problem solving and analytical skills
  • Ability to work independently under tight deadlines
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Good to Have Skills

  • Prior proven experience working in financial services

Parametric believes each member of our organization makes a significant contribution to our success. That contribution should not be limited by the assigned responsibilities. Therefore, this job description is designed to outline primary duties and qualifications. It is our expectation that every member of our team will offer his/her/their services wherever and whenever necessary to ensure the success of our client services.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY:

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices​ into your browser.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. title: Tavič / Cupola Operator
description:
ROCKWOOL je světovým lídrem ve výrobě izolací z kamenné vlny. Zaměstnáváme více než 11 000 zaměstnanců, ve 45 výrobních závodech na 5 kontinentech a působíme ve 38 zemích. Naše výrobky pomáhají vytvářet bezpečnější, úspornější a udržitelnější budovy ve více než 100 zemích světa.


V Česku působíme již od roku 1993 a od roku 1998 vyrábíme izolační materiály z kamenné vlny v Bohumíně, kde dnes zaměstnáváme přibližně 300 kolegů. Náš závod je evropským centrem technických izolací a díky dlouhodobým investicím do moderních technologií patří mezi nejmodernější výrobní závody skupiny ROCKWOOL. Vyrábíme izolace z přírodního kamene, které chrání před požárem, šetří energii, tlumí hluk a vydrží desítky let.


Naše produkty najdete v ikonických stavbách po celém světě od Empire State Building přes Eiffelovu věž až po Olympijský stadion v Londýně. Přidejte se ke společnosti, která spojuje stabilitu mezinárodního lídra, moderní výrobu a práci s reálným dopadem.


Hledáme zodpovědné a spolehlivé zaměstnance se zkušenostmi s obsluhou tavící pece.


Vyhovuje Vám práce ve směnném provoze? Zajímají vás bližší informace?

  • Budete zodpovídat za chod kupulové pece
  • Kontrolovat vážení a zavážení surovin do pece
  • Provádět odpich železa a jiné specifické činnosti
  • Budete pracovat ve 4 směnném provoze.


Tavič, kterého/rou hledáme, by měl/a splňovat následující požadavky:

  • Mít praxi s obsluhou
  • Mít oprávnění a zkušenosti s obsluhou mostového jeřábu.
  • Mít vazačský a jeřábnický průkaz.
  • Být ochotný/á se učit novým věcem a pracovat ve směnném provoze.


Pokud se stanete součástí našeho týmu, můžete se těšit na:

  • Stabilní a dlouhodobou práci na plný úvazek
  • Variabilní bonus ke mzdě

  • Příspěvek na dopravu

  • 5 týdnů dovolené
  • Věrnostní bonusový systém
  • Možnost kariérního a platového růstu

title: COR Program Specialist
description:
Overview

Nakupuna Federal is seeking a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) Program Specialist to join our team of talented consultants providing professional services to the Defense Health Agency (DHA). This full-time position supports the establishment and execution of a network-wide COR program, federal contract administration, acquisition planning, requirements development, process improvement, and stakeholder coordination. The ideal candidate has at least five years of federal contract management experience and the judgment to advise leadership and requiring activities on complex acquisition and contract administration matters.

Responsibilities

The following reflects management's definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other requirements.

  • Support the establishment and execution of the DHA COR program by recommending its structure, goals, performance measures, and operating approach.
  • Develop and implement standardized COR processes, templates, and standard operating procedures to promote consistency and compliance across supported military treatment facilities.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert to DHA leadership and provide guidance to CORs on complex contract administration matters.
  • Track COR appointments and terminations across the network and maintain complete, accurate, and current program records.
  • Establish and support a formal mentorship program that pairs experienced CORs with new appointees.
  • Collaborate with clinical, technical, contracting, and administrative stakeholders to improve contract management business processes and resolve program issues.
  • Advise requiring activities on acquisition strategies, procurement methods, contract vehicles, and acquisition planning for complex requirements.
  • Assist in developing acquisition and requirements documents, including performance work statements, quality assurance surveillance plans, and independent Government cost estimates for products and services of varying complexity.
  • Schedule and facilitate meetings; prepare and distribute agendas and minutes; and track action items through completion.
  • Prepare documentation in DHA-approved formats and maintain records in designated locations, including SharePoint and Microsoft Teams sites.
  • Serve as a point of contact for program-related inquiries and coordinate communication among diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Support special projects and provide contract management products and services that are timely, accurate, and complete.

Qualifications

Skills and Qualifications: The ideal candidate is an experienced federal contract management professional who communicates clearly, exercises sound judgment, and works effectively with Government and contractor personnel. Specifically, the candidate will demonstrate the following:

  • Strong knowledge of and experience applying Federal Acquisition Regulation Parts 8, 12, 13, 15, 16.505, 19, and 37.
  • Experience supporting COR programs, federal contract administration, acquisition planning, and contract management process improvement.
  • Experience developing requirements and acquisition documents, including performance work statements, quality assurance surveillance plans, and independent Government cost estimates.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft SharePoint and Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong customer service and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Education and Experience Required:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Business or a related field.
  • Five or more years of demonstrated experience in a federal contract management role. Former Federal 1102 series experience is desired.
  • Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act Level II certification in Contracting, Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting, or an equivalent certification.

Security Requirements: Must be a U.S. citizen and successfully pass the required security background investigation.

Location: Work is performed on-site in San Diego, California. Local hybrid telework may be permitted in accordance with DHA policies and with approval from the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). This is a full-time position. No travel is anticipated.

Physical Requirements: In addition to the skills and qualifications described above, candidates must, at a minimum, be able to meet the following physical requirements.

  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to use stairs without assistance.
  • Ability to perform repetitive motions with the hands, wrists, and fingers.
  • Ability to engage in and follow audible communications in emergency situations.
  • Ability to sit for prolonged periods at a desk while working on a computer.

The Nakupuna Companies use a market-based compensation strategy to ensure that our employees are compensated within applicable market ranges commensurate with multiple factors, including but not limited to the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability, organizational requirements, and position location. The projected compensation range for this position is $129,000.00 to $150,000.00 (annualized USD). The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Nakupuna Companies total compensation package for employees.

The NA People Solutions Advisor provides dedicated on-site support to plant-based leaders and employees, enabling effective HR self-service and delivering high-quality HR operational activities.

    Drive process standardization across North America in alignment with the HR Operating Model.

  • Partner with local Talent Business Partners to support business objectives and people strategy.

  • Provide responsive, high-quality service to employees and managers.

  • Collaborate with external vendors such as Benefits, Payroll, and HR service providers.

  • Work cross-functionally with the Legal Department and HR Operations team members to ensure compliance and operational excellence.

About Us

Huggies®. Kleenex®. Cottonelle®. Scott®. Kotex®. Poise®. Depend®. Kimberly-Clark Professional®. You already know our legendary brands—and so does the rest of the world. title: Kersthulp Den Haag
description:

Our values define the working environment we strive to create – where our people have a sense of belonging and everyone feels welcomed, respected and can contribute and grow. We welcome applications from talented people from all cultures, countries, races, genders, sexual orientations, disabilities, beliefs and generations and are committed to providing a working environment free from harassment, discrimination and retaliation.

Visit Inside Deutsche Bank to discover more about the culture of Deutsche Bank including Diversity, Equity & Inclusion, Leadership, Learning, Future of Work and more besides.

title: Food Storekeeper
description:
Job Description:

I. Position Summary:

The Storekeeper is responsible for receiving, storing and issuing food supplies and products for the Food Services Department. Responsible for inspecting all containers and covers to ensure that they are in good condition. The Storekeeper will work close with the Receiving Supervisor to ensure that the Storeroom is maintained in a clean and orderly fashion. Deliver MOW daily.

II. Position Responsibilities:

• On a daily basis, receive and store food supplies/products according to established procedures or as directed. Always practice FIFO when storing all foods.

• When receiving food, inspect all containers, covers, crates, cans, etc., to determine that they are in good condition as received. Determine that all products are kosher.

• Label and Date all perishable foods received.

• Subsequent to receiving food, store it in its appropriate environment as soon as possible according to established routines or as directed. Perishable foods should be stored first to preserve their quality. When storing food items, arrange them systematically according to commodity.

• Maintain the storeroom, loading dock, refrigerators and freezers in a clean, sanitary condition; clean them daily if necessary.

• Move racks and sweep and mop entire storeroom daily

• Clean air curtains Daily

• Do not allow odd items to accumulate, e.g., pallets.

• Check daily temperature sheets on refrigerators and freezers.

• Follow, and ensure adherence to, pertinent safety rules and regulations

• Assist supervisor in establishing and maintaining ordering and inventory systems.

• Call in milk and ice cream when needed.

• Contribute to the efficient and productive operation of the department.

• Deliver MOW Daily

• Exhibit timely completion of assignments with minimal assistance and appropriate follow-up.

• Exercise initiative, seeking additional tasks and projects from supervisor.

• Accept assignments readily.

• Recognize problems independently and work toward improving systems and procedures.

• Wears identification badge in a visible area above the waist line

• Wears uniform at all times.

• Perform additional related duties as required or as directed.

III. Core Competencies:

  • Promote effective interpersonal and interdisciplinary relationships, maintaining professional conduct at all times.

  • Identify interpersonal conflicts and resolve them constructively.

  • Display patience and tact when dealing with all Center employees.

  • Present department in a positive manner towards visitors, patients and staff.

  • Consistently maintain a courteous, pleasant, and supportive attitude toward visitors, patients and staff.

  • Must be able to listen, understand, and follow directions.

  • Must be able to communicate effectively with all staff.

  • Exemplify professionalism and exhibit values which contribute to the achievement of the mission of the Food Service Department and the Hebrew Rehabilitation Center.

IV. Qualifications

  • High school or equivalent.
  • 1-2 years experience
  • Must be act in a professional manner
  • Must have an optimistic and positive demeanor
  • Excellent oral communication skills
  • Able to adapt to changing priorities
  • Superb organizational skills.
  • Must be motivated to learn and flexible to change.
  • Knowledge of methods and procedures involved in purchasing, receiving, storing and disbursing food supplies/products, and supervisory responsibilities.
  • Proficiency in record keeping and the use of pertinent computer applications, operation of fax, copier, etc.
  • Valid Massachusetts driver’s license required

  • Must be able to speak and read fluently in the English language.

V. Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to lift, pull, and push 50 pounds
  • Must be able to stand for long periods of time
  • Frequent bending is involved
  • Exposure to extreme cold/heat

On-site

title: STA - Financial Risk Officer - Financial Risk Controls
description:
This role is a STA for 6 months with the possibility to extend if needed.

The Financial Risk (FR) department sets and controls the financial risk strategy across the bank by living its purpose of safeguarding ING’s financial health. The department provides strategic guidance on financial risk (in banking and trading books and in relation to the ING balance sheet), in line with regulatory compliance and acts as risk manager for Treasury activities globally.

The oversight control department within FR Framework and Control, looks after the risks in the entire Bank’s balance sheet. The department covers all financial related risks and contributes to the optimisation of positions on the balance sheet based on Regulatory and Economic Capital.

FR F&C includes an Integrated Process Control (IPC) chapter looking after the integrated processes within Financial and control risk activities overarching to Financial Risk. IPC coordinates firm-wide and departmental change initiatives on processes and controls overarching to Financial Risk including the set-up and definition of global data and infrastructure strategy and related control framework for FR.

What does a Financial Risk Officer IPC do?

As a Financial Risk Officer - Financial Risk Controls you play a key role in executing FR strategy set by the FR MT. We will set the right priorities and change initiatives and aligning these to ING’s overall and FR domain specific direction. Your excellent communication and stakeholder management skills are key to maintaining good relations with our stakeholders, other risk teams globally in head-office as well as in locations, Finance, , also our external stakeholders and the auditor of ING if required.

In this role you will:

  • Contribute to analysis and advice regarding overarching financial risk management processes and controls.

  • Safeguarding compliance of FR with ING internal policies as well as external policies and regulations from an operational process and control perspective.

  • Contribute to firm-wide and departmental change initiatives with the goal to make overarching financial risk management operational processes and controls efficient and effective.

  • Contribute to establish and guide FR on best practices in RCSA and KCT activities, including Sox404 testing.

  • Support FR in ad hoc requests within and from outside ING on FR processes and controls

  • Support FR in remediation of gaps and mitigation of risks with regard to processes and controls

Who are we looking for?

  • An experienced professional with an up-to-date high-level understanding of non-financial risk management; focus on banking and/or trading risk.

  • Excellent analytical skills on processes and controls including data requirements

  • Knowledge on ERM framework and NFR topics

  • Key Control Testing and Sox testing process is preferred

  • At least 4 years of relevant experience in the banking industry specifically in a non-financial risk or audit area.

  • The ability to challenge the status quo

  • Great team player skills with a hands-on mentality

  • Excellent communication skills

Rewards and benefits

We want to make sure that it’s possible for you to strike the right balance between your career and your private life. Find out more about our employment conditions.

The benefits of working with us at ING include:

  • 25-28 vacation days depending on contract

  • Pension scheme

  • 13th month salary

  • 8% Holiday payment

  • Hybrid working

  • Personal growth and challenging work with endless possibilities

  • An informal working environment with innovative colleagues

About us

Curious about how ING empowers people and businesses to move forward? Discover what we do and what we can offer you.

Questions?

Contact the recruiter attached to the advertisement. Want to apply directly? Please upload your CV and motivation letter by clicking the ‘Apply’ button.

Provide recruiter and/or manager contact details.

Overview & Position Summary

This role provides hands-on project management support for land acquisition, entitlement, and land development activities in residential community projects. Working under moderate supervision, the position manages portions of development projects, coordinates consultants and contractors, and ensures tasks are executed on schedule, within budget, and in compliance with quality and regulatory standards. The position serves as a key liaison between internal teams, consultants, municipalities, and external partners, while supporting departmental effectiveness through tracking, reporting, and process management.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Coordinate day-to-day land development activities, including grading, utilities, infrastructure installation, and site preparation tasks.
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets, and scopes to ensure timely and cost-effective execution of development milestones.
  • Assist in managing consultants, engineers, and contractors by tracking progress, reviewing deliverables, and addressing issues to maintain compliance with project requirements.
  • Support preparation, review, and processing of development plans, engineering drawings, permits, and regulatory documentation.
  • Conduct site visits to evaluate progress, identify potential issues, and ensure adherence to safety, quality, and design specifications.
  • Collaborate with municipalities, utility providers, and regulatory agencies to facilitate inspections, approvals, and required project coordination.
  • Manage administrative and financial tasks, including invoice processing, document management, and budget tracking for assigned projects.
  • Prepare project status updates, reports, sequence sheets, presentations, and other materials for internal stakeholders and leadership.
  • Coordinate Final Plat recordation, HOA documentation (CC&Rs, disclosures), and other community readiness deliverables.
  • Maintain organized project files, databases, and tracking tools to support compliance, reporting, and efficient workflow.
  • Assist with community opening schedules, bond management, and cross-functional coordination to support operational readiness.
  • Identify and recommend process improvements for project management workflows, document handling, and cross-team collaboration.

Education & Experience

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, planning, real estate development, or a related field; or 6–8 years of equivalent experience.
  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in land development, civil engineering, or construction project management.

Preferred:

  • Experience supporting land development projects in the homebuilding industry.
  • Exposure to site development permitting processes and consultant/contractor coordination.

Skills & Competencies

  • Working knowledge of land development processes, civil engineering concepts, and construction sequencing.
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities to manage multiple project tasks.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills for interacting with contractors, consultants, and internal partners.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, reports, and development plans.
  • Problem-solving skills using prior experience and analytical thinking to address moderately difficult issues.
  • Proficiency with project management software, spreadsheets, and related tools.
  • Attention to detail in reviewing documents and monitoring project progress.
  • Ability to influence team members through clear explanation of standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to work effectively across functions.
  • Willingness to support and mentor junior staff members.

Working Conditions

Work is performed in both office and field environments. Regular visits to active construction and development sites are required, involving exposure to varying weather conditions, uneven terrain, dust, noise, and heavy equipment. Occasional travel may be required to meet with municipalities, consultants, or contractors in support of project coordination.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods during office tasks and meetings.
  • Ability to walk development sites, including uneven or rugged terrain.
  • Ability to lift and carry materials up to 20 pounds.
  • Ability to operate standard office equipment and field tools.

title: Settlement Worker in Schools
description:
The YMCA of Southwestern New Brunswick is committed to strengthening our communities by responding to critical needs across the region, including population growth and change, health and well-being, youth retention, poverty, and the successful settlement and inclusion of newcomers. At the Y, we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to feel welcomed, connected, and supported. We are committed to creating an inclusive community where each person is valued for the unique perspectives, experiences, and contributions they bring.

Across 20 locations in Saint John and surrounding communities, the Y offers a diverse range of programs and services supported by approximately 475 employees and 500 volunteers. Through our Newcomer Community Connections team, we help newcomers build connections, access supports, navigate their new communities, and create a sense of belonging as they establish their lives in Southwestern New Brunswick. If you don’t have a Y story yet, now is your opportunity to get involved and discover what the power of belonging can do for you, your career, and your community.

POSITION OVERVIEW
Y Newcomer Connections works in partnership with local schools to support the settlement of newcomer students and their families in our community. The Settlement Worker in Schools helps with the orientation and registration of newcomer children in K-12 in Anglophone school districts. This position actively researches and makes referrals to appropriate support services. The Settlement Worker in Schools also works in designated schools 2-3 days/week to provide practical assistance to newcomer children and their families, to support Guidance Counsellors and EAL mentors, and to help promote a welcoming and inclusive school environment. Evening and weekend work may be required on occasion.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES
This individual will assist newcomer youth and family settlement and integration in the following key areas throughout the calendar year:
During the school year:

Provide orientation on the Canadian education system and schools in Saint John when new families arrive in Saint John;
Work with newcomer families to register children and youth K-12 in local schools;
Liaise with schools to organize orientation sessions for newcomer youth and their parent(s);
Provide in-school support to newcomer children and youth, guidance counsellors, EAL mentors, and other relevant school staff, such as to:

Assist with school activities relating to orientation week, parent-teacher appointments, field trips, and involvement in extra-curricular activities;
Work with schools to recruit student volunteers as “buddies” or “mentors”;
Ensure parents understand the schools’ expectations and their own rights and responsibilities;
Facilitate and encourage the involvement of parents in the academic and social life of their children;
Advocate for newcomer students in difficult situations with school personnel students, and parents, helping all to understand the problems faced by the others;
Support school administration to coordinate the provision of cultural competency training for staff;
Support school administration in charting options and pathways to post-secondary education;
Collaborate with Integrated Services Delivery staff as required to support youth and their families who may experience physical disabilities, behavioral issues, mental health challenges or other barriers;

During the summer/holiday season:

Coordinate back-to-school sessions to assist newcomer families with purchase of school supplies;
With the support of the Newcomer Youth Advisor:

Coordinate information sessions for summer employment opportunities where appropriate;
Make referrals to appropriate support services;
Coordinate the application process for children who require daycare/afterschool programs/summer camp services during the summer months;
Assist in planning YMCA summer day camps to serve youth, as applicable;

On-going duties:

Build and maintain relationships with Anglophone School District representatives and staff across the city;
Manage ongoing client caseload to ensure regular check-ins towards client settlement goals;
Initiate activities and programs to further assist the integration of newcomer students into the school system, for both newcomers and local students (i.e. workshops on cyber-bullying, cultural diversity, etc.);
With the support of the Newcomer Youth Advisor:

Apply for P.R.O. Kids /Strong Communities funding for clients who require financial assistance to participate in community programs;
Bring forward unique or especially difficult student challenges and needs to relative program staff;
Assist caseload youth and parents towards settlement outcomes of integration and full participation in the broader community;

Input and maintain client records in the Y Newcomer Connections CRM database on a regular basis;
Report all client-related activity on the iCARE database on a daily basis;
Compile and submit regular reports to the Community Connections Supervisor and Manager, of Resettlement and Settlement Services as requested;
Submit monthly expenses within the mandated deadlines;
Attend staff meetings;
Perform other duties as assigned by the GM, Newcomer and Community Connections.

EXPECTED RESPONSIBILITIES

Acts as a champion for immigration, cultural competency and volunteerism;
Models appropriate behaviours in line with the YMCA of Southwestern NB’s mission, vision and values; establishes rapport and maintains effective relationship-building behaviour with staff, volunteers and members.
Represents the YMCA of Southwestern NB and Newcomer Connections professionally;
Understands and integrates the value of philanthropy and volunteerism and imparts this knowledge and beliefs upon staff, volunteers and members;
Self-manages personal professional development;
Attends staff meetings as requested.

SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

A Bachelor's Degree, Community College diploma or similar from an accredited institution
Approachable and possessing a strong client-centric attitude
Heightened sensitivity to the needs of our immigrant community
A minimum of 3 years work experience in a cross-cultural environment
Exceptional oral and written communication skills
Exceptional organizational and interpersonal skills
Computer literate (MS Word & Excel)
Ability to work flexible hours
Must be fluent in the English language, knowledge of other languages is a great asset – preference will be given to Arabic Speakers.
Knowledge of NB schools & the school system and policies

COMPETENCIES REQUIRED

Communication: Communicates in a clear, professional, and timely manner and supports information sharing and goal achievement
Creativity and Innovation: Develop new ways or adapt existing ideas to help us achieve desired results
Relationship Building and Collaboration: Builds positive interaction both internally and externally to achieve work-related goals
Self-Management: Works independently with minimal supervision
Sensitivity: Ability to develop an appreciation for the challenges of our clientele and display needed patience and resourcefulness.
Sense of Community: Demonstrates an awareness and understanding of community and responds to identified needs
Teamwork: Actively builds teams and encourages open relationships for maximum organizational effectiveness

WORKING CONDITIONS

As a full-time YMCA of Southwestern NB staff person, your hours of work and location may be adjusted due to programming needs. There is no guarantee of the number of hours worked within a work week.
The YMCA of Southwester NB has a Joint Health and Safety Committee which meets every month to discuss health and safety within the workplace. Questions or concerns about your workplace must be brought forward to committee members.
In this role, you will be required to work in an environment that is often busy with high noise levels.
As a YMCA of Southwestern NB staff person, you are responsible for your travel to and from work.
You are responsible for the member/client’s safety daily. You will be required to perform first aid and CPR when and if necessary and you are certified to do so.
You will be responsible for following and abiding by The Y Way, ensuring all staff persons require a clean and well-maintained centre.

INTERESTED IN JOINING US?
Interested candidates are invited to apply with us online at Careers | YMCA of Southwestern New Brunswick. We ask all applicants to submit their cover letter and resume. The YMCA of Southwestern New Brunswick appreciates the interest of all applicants; however, only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY COMMITMENT
We value the unique perspectives and contributions of each individual and are committed to building an inclusive, diverse workforce.
DUTY TO ACCOMMODATE

The YMCA is committed to creating inclusive and accessible environments for all. If you require an accommodation at any stage of the application or employment process, we encourage you to let us know so we can ensure equitable opportunities for all.

Build the Future With Us

title: Electrical Reliability Technician
description:
Electrical Reliability Technician

Job Description

Electrical Reliability Technician - $5,000 Sign-On Bonus!!!

Chester, PA

Join the team behind iconic brands like Huggies®, Kleenex®, Cottonelle®, Scott®, Kotex®, Poise®, Depend®, and Kimberly-Clark Professional. At Kimberly-Clark, it’s all here for you—innovation, growth, and the chance to make a real impact.

You were made to create Better Care for a Better World: this is your opportunity to troubleshoot complex electrical systems, implement and improve maintenance practices in a facility that creates top-notch products for nearly ¼ of the world’s population. Get recognized often by your manager, supported by your team, and see those essential products being used by your own loved ones each day.

About You

In one of our manufacturing roles, you’ll focus on winning with consumers and the market, while putting safety, mutual respect, and human dignity at the center.

You will be maintaining equipment associated with the production, packaging and distribution of Kimberly-Clark products through preventative, predictive and corrective maintenance work. This role is part of Kimberly-Clark’s investment in creating new jobs and expanding its capabilities to produce premium products that are essential to millions of lives around the world, and right here in Chester, PA. It starts with YOU.

In this role, you will:

  • Actively participate in a High-Performance Work Team environment, sharing knowledge and skills with all other team members

  • Support the planning and execution of daily/weekly/and shutdown activities

  • Actively participate in failure analysis and equipment/systems troubleshooting and identify patterns of failures and ways to design out failures

  • Participate in shutdown planning and two-week planning processes, including work and parts preparation

  • Read blueprints, schematics, drawings and related technical literature as required.

  • Troubleshoot industrial electrical equipment, including analog and digital systems. Good solid general electrical troubleshooting and maintenance fundamentals for 600V and less industrial electrical systems are a must.

  • Learn window-based computer systems and Kimberly Clark specific systems like SAP

  • Be willing and have the electrical aptitude to lead and execute repairs on high-speed rotating equipment

  • Work with and on occasion, lead others (operators, maintenance technicians, contractors, suppliers)

To succeed in this role, you will need the following qualifications:

  • Be 18 years or older and authorized to work in the United States.

  • Have a state and/or US Department of Education accredited high school diploma, GED Grade 12 certificate.

  • Have either a 2-year related technical degree and 3+ years of industrial electrical work experience or 5+ years of industrial electrical work experience

  • Able to maintain a work schedule of 12-hour rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, holidays and overtime

  • Willing to work nights, weekends, and respond to call-ins as required to resolve equipment failures and to support planned shutdowns

  • Have basic computer knowledge, mechanical aptitude and good math skills

  • Able to read and write basic English

  • Able to work on elevated work platforms, catwalks, scaffolding, etc. and enter confined spaces

  • Can pass a pre-employment assessment and a pre-employment drug + background screening

  • Can pass post-offer / pre-hire Physical Abilities Test (PAT)

  • Follow all site and asset safety practices and procedures and must value working safely

  • Understand predictive/preventative maintenance concepts and demonstrate willingness to learn and continue education

At least one of the following is required:

  • Related two-year technical degree

  • Completed Apprenticeship

  • Equivalent military MOS

  • Minimum 5 years of trade/work experience in a related manufacturing field or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

  • 3+ years of work experience in a manufacturing field or equivalent

  • Experience with high-speed manufacturing and converting equipment

  • Knowledge of SAP

  • Knowledge of Variable Speed and Motion Drive Systems and AC Motors, especially Allen-Bradley PowerFlex and ABB Drive systems

  • Knowledge of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) systems, especially Allen-Bradley Controllogix (RSLogix5000). Knowledge of Modicon and G&L PLC system programming is a plus

  • Knowledge of Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs), especially Panelviews. FactoryTalk programming and understanding of Virtual Workstation environments are a plus.

  • Knowledge of Allen-Bradley PLC (GuardLogix) and non-PLC based safety systems (MSR/GSR/SIS)

  • Knowledge of Operational Technology (OT) Network Systems, especially Ethernet and ModBus- based systems

  • Knowledge of Digital Sensors (proximity, photoeye, load) and camera vision systems

  • Knowledge of Electrical Construction, Maintenance, and Safety Fundamentals, including NEC and NFPA70E Codes

  • Knowledge of Distributed Control Systems (DCS), especially Honeywell TDC 3000 and Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk View systems

  • Knowledge of Instrumentation Field Devices, including pressure, flow, level, and temperature transmitters and switches

  • Knowledge of Low Voltage (600V and less) Motor Control Centers (MCCs) and Panelboard experience is strongly preferred. Knowledge of Medium Voltage MCCs (2300V) is a plus.

  • High voltage electrical distribution power system experience (13.2kV to 69kV), including oil circuit breakers, transformers, switchgear breakers, and high voltage switches is a plus.

Led by Purpose. Driven by You.

Total Benefits

We believe that our employees are our greatest asset, and we're committed to providing them with the resources they need to be successful. If you're looking for a rewarding career with a company that cares about its employees, then Kimberly-Clark is the place for you.

Here are just a few of the benefits you’d enjoy working in this role for Kimberly-Clark. For a complete overview, see .

Great support for good health with medical, dental, and vision coverage options with no waiting periods or pre-existing condition restrictions. Access to an on-site fitness center, occupational health nurse, and allowances for high-quality safety equipment.

Flexible Savings and spending accounts to maximize health care options and stretch dollars when caring for yourself or dependents.

Diverse income protection insurance options to protect yourself and your family in case of illness, injury, or other unexpected events.

Additional programs and support to continue your education, adopt a child, relocate, or even find temporary childcare.

To Be Considered
Click the Apply button and complete the online application process. A member of our recruiting team will review your application and follow up if you seem like a great fit for this role.

In the meantime, please check out the careers website.

And finally, the fine print….

For Kimberly-Clark to grow and prosper, we must be an inclusive organization that applies the diverse experiences and passions of its team members to brands that make life better for people all around the world, which is why we seek to build a workforce that encompasses the experiences of our consumers. When you bring your original thinking to Kimberly-Clark, you fuel the continued success of our enterprise. We are a committed equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, pregnancy, genetic information, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Taxation Head
description:
Job Description

Your Role

The purpose of this job is to support development and implementation of tax policy and strategy and be responsible for ensuring tax compliance of direct tax, indirect tax, transfer pricing and international tax obligations for all legal entities in Egypt.

A Typical Day

· Plan, facilitate and manage the preparation and review of company all types of taxes, be responsible for the accurate, timely filing of all tax forms for all legal entities in Egypt; maintains tax records as well as returns, reports and other related materials.

· Ensure all monthly/ quarterly/ annually tax reporting and tax provisions are submitted on time accurately.

· Maintain effective control procedures over all aspects of the tax process.; find and implement opportunities for process improvement in company tax procedures.

· Act as tax business partner to the commercial teams in relation to tax advisory, planning and governance, to develop and implement strategic tax planning for the company.

· Work closely with larger finance team to secure company’s position.

· Supervise and manage all types of tax audits with external or internal parties and communicate with tax authority to defend the tax position and ensuring smooth tax audit process.

· Monitor legislative and regulatory tax law developments, communicate its impact on our business and financial statements, and work to create strategies to capitalize on changes to taxation legislation.

· Optimise capital and legal structure for the group operations in Egypt. Coordinate and prepare transfer pricing documentations for the legal entities to ensure compliance of transfer pricing regulations.

  • Responsible for tax advisory and international tax matters, including but not limited to withholding taxes, treaty applications and etc.
  • Develop the tax organization in Egypt, organize training and learning with finance and non-finance team.

Who You Are

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or other related majors. CPA/Masters/related degree in taxation is preferred.

· 10+ year of relevant experience with extensive corporate tax knowledge in Multinational company and/or accounting firm.

  • Excellent technical tax knowledge in tax code, compliance and procedures for corporations, direct experience with a variety of tax operations and ability to drive process improvements.
  • Collaborator with excellent interpersonal communication skills to work with people across functions and culture.

· Strong ability to utilize project management and accounting best practices to organize and prioritize tasks and the tasks of other tax team members.

· Initiative-taker with strong leadership and influencing skills to engage and develop tax team.

· Strong accounting, analytical, and research skills.

· Fluent written and spoken English communications skills to communicate with regional and global team within the group.

· Strong computer skills with drive for using technology as an enabler. Proficiency in Microsoft applications viz. Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, etc. Knowledge of Oracle and/or SAP would be an added advantage.

Core Competencies

title: Dated Item Clerk
description:
About Us

Join us at WinCo Foods, where we're more than just a grocery retailer - we're a growing family of over 140 supermarkets in 10 states with over 22,000 employee owners. Our purpose is to make the lives of our customers and employee owners better by offering the lowest possible prices to feed their families. Overview

Job Summary

Inspects dated items, maintains rotates and replenishes stock in a safe and efficient manner to meet customer purchasing needs. Generally works 6-8 hour shifts between the hours of 8:00 pm to 8:00 am.

Typical Duties and Responsibilities

  • Maintains the quality condition of dated items.
  • Completes the Scanned Item Rotation Report at the beginning of each shift and flags items pending rotation within allowable rotation time standards.
  • Pulls product prior to expiration and rotates daily per guidelines using the Quality Assurance Display.
  • Maintains Quality Assurance database daily including addition of new or untracked items once the database for the store has been established using the Scanned Item Exception Report.
  • Scans out Quality Assurance pulled stale/damaged product at the backroom scanner.
  • Periodically inspects vendor items reporting short dated issues to the Receiver and Assistant Manager.
  • Periodically inspects outer department rotation.
  • Periodically inspects LRQT (Large Quantity Items) rotation.
  • Audits flagged items thrown by freight crew reporting findings to the Assistant Manager.
  • Reports repeated rotation issues to the Assistant Manager and appropriate Department Manager.
  • Reports ongoing rotation issues to the Store Manager.
  • Notifies store management of large quantities of product pending expiration within two weeks (sooner for refrigerated LRQT) so management can determine whether the product will be marked down.
  • Assists customers with questions; performs training duties.
  • Maintains a safe, secure and sanitary work environment.
  • Performs all job duties and responsibilities with honesty and integrity.
  • Reports short dated product shipping from the warehouse to appropriate Warehouse Inventory Supervisor including order number and UPC number.
  • Occasionally transmits data to General Office.

Performs other duties as assigned or needed.RequirementsAbility to:

  • Work varied shifts in a 24/7 operation; including night, weekends and holidays.
  • Reach, lift, stack and maneuver objects of varying dimensions and weights up to 40 lbs., within the range of floor level to overhead occasionally.
  • Stand, walk and move rapidly for long periods of time.
  • Bend, stoop, twist and turn frequently.
  • Ensure safe and accurate completion of work activities.
  • Learn and memorize location of products, company policies, and Quality Assurance procedures.
  • Exhibit manual dexterity and good hand/eye coordination to rotate product.
  • Conduct visual inspection of merchandise being placed on shelves.
  • Communicate (hearing & speech) to provide customer service during shift.
  • Perform primary duties efficiently and accurately.
  • Meet or exceed established scanned item rotation report time standards.
  • Must be 18 years of age or older.
  • Machines and Equipment Operated:
  • Pallet jack
  • Hand truck
  • Garbage and cardboard compactor
  • Electronic fork lift
  • Scanner and AS-400

title: Associate Director of Development
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:

The Associate Director of Development works closely with development teams in Virginia and Maryland/DC to plan, implement, and coordinate effective multi-year strategies and plans for individual major gift prospects and suspects. This position is based in TNC’s Arlington office and requires in-office work a minimum of three days per week.

The Associate Director of Development is responsible for expanding TNC’s major-gifts pipeline in the Northern Virginia market, with a significant focus on identifying, engaging, and qualifying prospective donors in support of all of TNC’s conservation priorities – both local and global. Working closely with development colleagues, prospect development staff, conservation leaders, trustees, volunteers, and other partners, they will develop and implement strategies to build relationships with individuals who have the interest, capacity, and potential to support TNC at the major-gift level.

The ADoD will conduct a high volume of discovery outreach and meetings; assess philanthropic interests, giving capacity, readiness, and connections to TNC; and determine appropriate next steps for cultivation, solicitation, referral or disqualification. As prospects are qualified, they will manage a developing portfolio and create individualized engagement and solicitation strategies aligned with local and global priorities. They will maintain timely and accurate records in the Conservancy’s donor database, coordinate internal partners, develop proposals and other donor materials as needed, and represent TNC persuasively in the Northern Virginia philanthropic community.

Responsibilities include:

  • Lead major-gifts discovery and qualification in Northern Virginia, managing a pool of discovery prospects and building a portfolio of qualified donors.

  • Collaborate with the DC-MD team to develop a coordinated market strategy, and partner with prospect development staff to identify and prioritize prospects.

  • Conduct proactive outreach and meetings to assess prospects’ interest, capacity, and alignment with TNC; document qualification decisions and next steps in the donor database.

  • Engage trustees, volunteers, donors, and staff to open doors, build TNC’s visibility, and strengthen its philanthropic network in Northern Virginia.

  • Move qualified prospects into cultivation and solicitation or coordinate their handoff to another fundraiser.

  • Act independently and in the supervisor’s stead as needed, exercising sound judgment on decisions that may have program-wide, financial, or legal impact.

  • Handle confidential information sensitively and ensure compliance with TNC policies and external donor, legal, and IRS requirements.

  • Persuasively represent TNC’s mission and participate in complex, high-profile, or sensitive negotiations as needed.

  • Travel regularly throughout Northern Virginia and the greater Washington, D.C., region, including occasional evenings, weekends, long hours, and short-notice travel.

  • Work environment involves infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion or strain.

  • Once the portfolio is developed, manage 60 – 100 donors with the capacity to give $100,000 or more. Responsible for 60 – 100 visits and 180 – 300 moves annually. Annual fundraising goal of $1,000,000 or more, along with a goal for bequest notifications.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6 years related experience or an equivalent combination.

  • Experience building and maintaining long-term relationships with fundraising constituents.

  • Experience in asking for and closing gifts of $50,000 or more.

  • Experience in managing and tracking multiple prospects and donors.

  • Experience working with cross-functional teams, preferably in a large non-profit.

  • Experience working with fundraising principles and practices.

  • Experience, coursework, or other training in current trends in charitable giving in the areas of capital campaigns, major gifts or planned giving.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.

  • Ability to design and manage fundraising plans, including individualized cultivation, solicitation and recognition plans.

  • Ability to determine an individual’s interests, capacity and potential for helping the Conservancy meet its goals, and act appropriately to tie those interests with the Conservancy’s work.

  • Ability to educate and inform prospective and existing donors about appropriate giving vehicles.

  • Demonstrated experience using listening, diplomacy and tact to build strong relationships and motivate donors and volunteers.

  • Proven ability to negotiate complex, high profile or sensitive agreements.

  • Working knowledge of charitable gift planning.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Salary Information:

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $125,000 – $145,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

Job Summary

Performs a variety of duties in the Center, as a member of the surgical team. Scrubs on all types of cases performed at the Center, including orthopedic, pain and local cases. Assists in preparation for cases by "picking instruments" and set-up and maintenance of sterile field. May also function as surgeon's second assistant. Assist OR team in all aspects of room turnover. Pick soft goods and instrumentation to facilitate preparation for following days' surgery.

Essential Functions
  • C. Environment and Demands 1. Environmental Demands: Indoor area with frequent exposure to mild discomfort from dust, fumes, temperature and noise. Tasks that involve exposure to blood, body fluids, tissues, and other potentially infectious materials. 2. Essential Physical and Cognitive Demands, Manual Dexterity: Requires prolonged periods of standing in place at sterile field. Requires ability to perform lifting and transport of patients. Lift/handle/carry materials, trays or equipment of moderate weight (20 to 50 lbs). B. MISSION/STRATEGIC PLAN: Participates in activities which support the mission of the hospital C. JOB SPECIFIC COMPETENCIES: Montefiore Nyack Ambulatory Surgery Center (ASC) specific job competencies: 1. Prepares for next days scheduled procedures by cases, using surgeon’s preference cards to assure that all necessary supplies, soft goods, instruments and equipment are available. Labels case order and prepares a needs list accurately in collaboration with Central Sterile team. 2. Actively assists without direction in surgery suite maintenance including case preparation, turn-over, and terminal cleaning. Follows AORN Recommended Practices and Center policy. 3. Assists team and with inventory control, informing & updating materials team of low par-levels 4. Performs daily stocking and re-stocking of OR and clean-supply stock room. Ambulatory Scrub Tech Clinical job competencies: 1. Demonstrates appropriate sterile and aseptic techniques, at all times in the surgery suite. 2. Demonstrates appropriate dress, according to policy, at all times in the surgery suite. 3. Performs scrub technician and surgery assistant function according to AORN Recommended Practices and Center policies: A. Performs appropriate hand scrub at beginning of day and for each case thereafter. B. Dons sterile dress appropriately, using closed glove technique. C. Demonstrates set-up and maintenance of the sterile field for all assigned cases. D. Demonstrates instrument set-up, arranging instrumentation, equipment and supplies on the mayo and back table(s) as appropriate for the assigned case and according to AORN Recommended Practices, Center policy and the surgeon’s preference card. E. Anticipates the intra-operative needs of the surgeon and other members of the surgical team, such as instrumentation, sponges, sutures, suction and cautery. F. Assists surgeon in holding retractors after placement by the physician, whenever possible. G. Passes instruments to members of the surgical team in a safe manner and in such a way as to not divert attention away from the operative field, whenever possible. H. Handles sharps appropriately and performs required and as-needed sharps counts, per policy, so as to safeguard the patient, self and other members of the surgical team. I. Manages the operative field, including drapes, equipment, instrumentation, and personnel during the procedure and in a manner which assures maintenance of the sterile field. J. Assists in observing the patient, during the operative procedure, for complications such as hemorrhage and furnishes equipment and supplies to provide for optimum patient outcome. K. Handles specimens appropriately, per Center policy. L. Assists in application of sterile dressing prior to removal of drapes from field. M. Prepares clean and contaminated instruments and supplies utilized in the surgery suite for transport, in an appropriate manner, and transports to decontamination for processing and re-sterilization. title: Assistent filiaalmanager Malden
description:
Voor onze winkel in Malden zijn wij op zoek naar jou! Ben jij iemand die graag de leiding neemt, maar ook zelf actief meewerkt op de werkvloer? Dan is de rol van Assistent Filiaalmanager bij Wibra echt iets voor jou.

Als Assistent Filiaalmanager ben je een meewerkende leidinggevende. Je werkt dagelijks samen met je team in de winkel en ondersteunt de filiaalmanager in het aansturen van het team en de winkel. Je geeft het goede voorbeeld door zelf mee te werken en zorgt er samen voor dat de winkel draait, de schappen gevuld zijn en klanten tevreden de deur uitgaan.

Werken bij Wibra is leuk. Je werkt in een klein team, de winkel is altijd in beweging en de werkdruk kan hoog zijn. Dat betekent dat je fysiek bezig bent, snel schakelt en overzicht houdt. Juist die dynamiek maakt het werk afwisselend en geeft het veel energie. Samen met de filiaalmanager ben je verantwoordelijk voor het reilen en zeilen van de winkel. Je coacht collega’s op de werkvloer, ondersteunt in de planning en zorgt dat alles soepel verloopt. Bij afwezigheid van de filiaalmanager neem jij het voortouw.

Een dag als Assistent Filiaalmanager bij Wibra
Je start je dag in de winkel en begint met een kop koffie en het doornemen van de planning. Vaak werk je met z’n tweeën of in een klein team, je stemt samen af wat er moet gebeuren en gaat daarna direct aan de slag op de werkvloer. Er is vracht binnengekomen, dus jullie zorgen ervoor dat alles snel en netjes in de winkel ligt. Je stuurt collega’s aan waar nodig terwijl je zelf volop meewerkt, houdt overzicht en zorgt dat de winkel er verzorgd en aantrekkelijk uitziet, ook als het druk is.

Tussendoor pak je administratieve taken op, help je collega’s op de werkvloer en werk je samen met de filiaalmanager aan de ontwikkeling van het team. Je springt bij waar nodig en zorgt dat alles blijft draaien. Geen dag is hetzelfde en juist die afwisseling maakt het werk dynamisch en leuk.

Dit is echt iets voor jou als je van aanpakken houdt en energie krijgt van drukte in de winkel.

  • Je hebt ervaring in de Retail, bijvoorbeeld als teamleider, senior verkoopmedewerker of in een vergelijkbare rol

  • Je hebt een mbo werk- en denkniveau

  • Je bent fysiek fit en vindt het fijn om actief bezig te zijn

  • Je vindt het leuk om collega’s aan te sturen en te helpen ontwikkelen

  • Je kunt goed plannen en organiseren, ook als het druk is

  • Je neemt initiatief en pakt verantwoordelijkheid

  • Je houdt van aanpakken en werkt graag actief mee

Dit bieden wij jou

Bij Wibra werken we hard en zetten we samen de schouders eronder. Je komt terecht in een organisatie die groeit en continu in ontwikkeling is, waar jouw inzet echt het verschil maakt. Verder bieden we jou:

  • 28 uur per week

  • Bruto maandsalaris tussen € 2.619 en € 2.751 (op basis van 38 uur per week)
    Waar je precies wordt ingeschaald, bepaalt de regiomanager en is afhankelijk van de ervaring die je meebrengt

  • 24 vakantiedagen (op basis van 38 uur per week)

  • Toeslagen op zon- en feestdagen

  • 20% personeelskorting

  • Aangesloten bij pensioenfonds Detailhandel

  • Mogelijkheid tot doorgroeien naar Filiaalmanager

Dit kan je verwachten in de sollicitatieprocedure:

Solliciteer meteen en beantwoord de volgende vragen, we kijken uit naar je reactie!
