Attached resumes WILL NOT be accepted in lieu of completing this application and WILL NOT be used for screening for qualifying credit. "See Resume" or “See Attachment" within the fillable application sections WILL NOT be accepted and will be considered an incomplete application and will not be processed. Answers to Supplemental Questions must refer to education or work experience listed on this application to receive credit. Degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions. To receive credit for your work history and credentials, you must list the information on the application form. For additional information about applications and processes with the state of NC, please visit: State Government Application Resources.


For consideration for this vacancy, all applicants must complete an online application. If multiple applications are submitted to an individual posting, only the most recent application received prior to the posting close date will be evaluated for consideration.


Applications for positions requiring specific coursework must be accompanied by a copy of the applicant's transcript. If applicants earned college credit hours but did not complete a degree program, they must attach an unofficial transcript to each application to receive credit for this education.


Re-Entry for Formerly Incarcerated Individuals
Our Agency supports the Governor's Executive Order 303 which seeks to re-employ individuals that were previously incarcerated. Formerly incarcerated individuals are invited to apply for any vacant Commerce position(s) in which they believe they are qualified.


Please note: This position is subject to a National and International Background Investigation and/or Fingerprinting as required by applicable law.


By providing the requested information, you certify that you have given true, accurate and complete information on this attachment to the best of your knowledge. In the event confirmation is needed in connection with your work, you authorize educational institutions, associations, registration and licensing boards, and others to furnish whatever detail is available concerning your qualifications. You authorize investigation of all statements made in this application and understand that false information or documentation, or a failure to disclose relevant information may be grounds for rejection of your application, disciplinary action or dismissal if you are employed, and(or) criminal action. You further understand that dismissal upon employment shall be mandatory if fraudulent disclosures are given to meet position qualifications (Authority: GS 126-30, GS 14- 122.1).


Due to the volume of applications received, we are unable to provide information regarding the status of your application over the phone. To check the status of your application, please log in to your account and click "Application Status." If you are selected for an interview, you will be contacted by management. If you are no longer under consideration, you will receive an email notification. The processing of applications will take an average of 5 business days due to the high volume of applications received. It is not necessary to contact the Human Resources Office to check the status of an application or possible interview.


If applicants earned a foreign degree, foreign degrees require an official evaluation for U.S. equivalency and must be submitted to Human Resources for verification. There are several organizations that perform this specialized service, feel free to use any service of your choosing. The National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES) has several options on their website that can provide credential verification.












Minimum Education and Experience

Some state job postings say you can qualify by an “equivalent combination of education and experience.” If that language appears below, then you may qualify through EITHER years of education OR years of directly related experience, OR a combination of both. description:

Integration & Solutions Analyst


Turn complex technical challenges into scalable solutions that improve the customer experience and strengthen Gogo's operational excellence.


At Gogo, we connect business aviation customers to the people and information that matter most. As our technology and operations continue to evolve, we rely on innovative problem-solvers who can identify opportunities for improvement, optimize systems, and help deliver exceptional customer experiences.


As our Integration & Solutions Analyst, you'll serve as a key technical resource supporting Customer Operations and the broader Gogo ecosystem. You'll work closely with Customer Operations, Engineering, System Administrators, Database Administrators, and Network Engineers to identify process inefficiencies, troubleshoot operational challenges, and implement automated solutions that improve performance, scalability, and customer outcomes.


If you're someone who enjoys solving complex problems, thrives in a collaborative technical environment, and is passionate about continuous improvement, we'd love to meet you.


What You'll Do


  • Support and maintain the Gogo Test Lab, while driving initiatives that improve testing capabilities and operational efficiency
  • Provide technical expertise that helps advance Customer Operations objectives and enhance customer experience
  • Troubleshoot, test, and investigate operational failures and anomalies across Gogo hardware and software platforms
  • Partner with Customer Operations, Engineering, and infrastructure teams to develop and implement solutions that improve business processes and service delivery
  • Develop and support proof-of-concept projects that validate new architectures, technologies, and operational solutions
  • Work cross-functionally with System Administrators, Database Administrators, and Network Engineers across multiple service lines to resolve complex technical issues
  • Create, interpret, and maintain technical documentation, implementation plans, system diagrams, and production environment designs
  • Build documentation that adheres to company standards and supports the long-term maintenance of systems and solutions

What You'll Bring


  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 1-2 years’ experience in information technology, technical support, systems administration, or a related discipline
  • Strong customer support and customer-facing troubleshooting experience
  • Demonstrated experience with IP-based networking concepts and network troubleshooting tools
  • Experience identifying technical issues and implementing sustainable solutions in operational environments
  • Ability to interpret technical requirements and translate them into practical implementations

Even Better If You Have


You don't need to check every box below. If you bring experience in some of these areas, we'd especially like to hear from you:


  • Network+ Certification
  • AeroIT Certification
  • Working knowledge of data structures and algorithms
  • Strong understanding of Linux operating systems, system internals, and operating environments
  • Experience creating technical documentation, implementation plans, and system architecture diagrams
  • Exposure to proof-of-concept development and solution validation projects
  • Knowledge of high-volume, high-availability production environments
  • Experience within the business aviation, aerospace, telecommunications, or technology industries
  • Familiarity with process automation and operational efficiency initiatives
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within cross-functional technical teams

Why Gogo?


At Gogo, we're transforming how people connect in the sky.


Our teams build and support technology that powers connectivity aboard business aircraft around the world. That means the work you do here has a destination beyond a screen, spreadsheet, or meeting; it becomes part of an experience happening thousands of feet above the ground.


You'll work alongside people who know their craft, challenge ideas, solve difficult problems, and care about building what comes next.


Ready to help shape the future of connected aviation? Come aboard.

title: Senior Compensation Analyst
description:
At YETI, we believe that time spent outdoors matters more than ever and our gear can make that time extraordinary. When you work here, you’ll have the opportunity to create exceptional, meaningful work and problem solve with innovative team members by your side. Together, you’ll help our customers get the high-quality gear they need to make the most of their adventures. We are BUILT FOR THE WILD™.

About the Role

The Senior Compensation Analyst supports the design, administration, analysis, and ongoing management of compensation programs across the organization. This role partners with Talent Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and business leaders to provide data-driven guidance on market pricing, job evaluation, salary structures, incentive programs, compensation planning, and pay-related compliance.


This role requires strong analytical capability, sound compensation judgment, and the ability to translate complex data into practical recommendations. The Senior Compensation Analyst independently manages recurring compensation processes and contributes to broader projects that support competitive, equitable, compliant, and scalable pay practices.


What You'll Do

Compensation Strategy & Program Administration

  • Support the design, administration, and governance of base pay, variable pay, and other compensation programs.
  • Manage key components of annual compensation planning processes, including eligibility reviews, data validation, planning tools, statement testing, approvals, communications, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Conduct market pricing, compensation benchmarking, pay range analysis, and internal equity reviews to inform pay recommendations.
  • Maintain salary structures, pay ranges, guidelines, and compensation-related documentation across assigned populations or geographies.
  • Review compensation requests, including new hire offers, promotions, transfers, adjustments, and other pay actions, ensuring alignment with guidelines, budget, internal equity, and market data.
  • Provide guidance to Talent Acquisition, Talent Business Partners, and leaders on compensation policy, offer positioning, pay decisions, and exception processes.
  • Partner with HRIS teams to test and validate compensation-related Workday data, processes, reports, and configuration changes.

Job Architecture & Organizational Design

  • Support the administration of the organization’s job architecture, including job levels, grades, job profiles, and related governance practices.
  • Conduct job evaluations, leveling assessments, and job description reviews using established frameworks and market data.
  • Create, update, and maintain job profiles and compensation-related job data in Workday.
  • Partner with Talent Business Partners and leaders to ensure roles are appropriately aligned to job responsibilities, organizational structure, and compensation levels.
  • Conduct periodic audits to support data quality, job structure integrity, and consistent application of leveling guidelines.

Incentive Compensation & Bonus Programs

  • Administer annual, quarterly, and other incentive or bonus programs, including eligibility validation, payout calculations, and participant data reviews.

title: System Design Architect
description:
Job Description

System Design Architect

Derby

Full time


An exciting opportunity has arisen for a System Design Architect to join the Systems Design and Architecture team within the Systems Engineering and Product Performance group, helping to shape the future of advanced aerospace and power systems.


We are seeking an enthusiastic System Design Architect to develop next-generation products and technologies, including new engine architectures that support future airframes. You will be joining a multidisciplinary team where engineers are expected to develop their skills across cycle design, mechanical integrity and aircraft/systems integration.


As a System Design Architect, you will play a pivotal role in translating business, customer and regulatory requirements into robust engineering solutions. You will collaborate across engineering disciplines to ensure designs meet performance, mechanical integrity, reliability, safety and lifecycle objectives, with a particular focus on gas turbine cycle design and engine performance.


What you will be doing:

  • Owning the definition and development of gas turbine cycles for future products.
  • Developing and maintaining thermodynamic performance models to predict engine performance across the operating envelope in the conceptual design stage.
  • Defining and assessing cycle-level requirements and providing performance data to component and subsystem teams.
  • Investigating the impact of component performance, technology assumptions and design changes on overall engine performance.
  • Developing system requirements, interfaces, functional models and design specifications.
  • Supporting nacelle, engine systems and aircraft integration.
  • Undertaking mechanical integrity assessments of the powerplant, engine and subsystems.
  • Supporting responses to customer data requests and working with managed service providers on data generation for customers and methods development.
  • Developing engineering solutions and, where applicable, generating patents and protecting intellectual property.
  • Leading cycle and architecture trade studies, design reviews and technical decision-making activities.
  • Ensuring compliance with applicable industry standards, certification requirements and engineering processes.
  • Supporting verification and validation activities throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Identifying technical risks and developing appropriate mitigation strategies.
  • Contributing to technology roadmaps and future product development initiatives.
  • Working closely with subsystem and component groups, manufacturing and safety teams to develop integrated engineering solutions.

Position Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Strong technical knowledge of thermodynamics and gas turbine performance.
  • Experience in gas turbine cycle design, performance modelling or engine performance analysis.
  • Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, methodologies and lifecycle management.
  • Cycle modelling skills, including proficient use of tools such as Numerical Propulsion System Simulation (NPSS).
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and presentation skills.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Knowledge of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) principles.
  • Experience of system architecture, requirements development and functional modelling.
  • Experience of nacelle, engine systems and/or aircraft integration.
  • Knowledge or experience of mechanical integrity assessments.
  • Experience of supporting cycle and architecture trade studies, design reviews, verification and validation activities.
  • Knowledge of functional safety and reliability engineering.
  • Aerospace, defence or energy experience is desirable but not a prerequisite.
  • Chartered Engineer (CEng) status or working towards professional registration.
  • Enthusiasm and a willingness to learn, with the ability to grow, adapt quickly to changing requirements and actively seek to influence future products.

title: Covenant Data Specialist
description:
Job Description:

Overview:

We don’t simply hire employees. We invest in them. When you work at Chatham, we empower you — offering professional development opportunities to help you grow in your career, no matter if you've been here for five months or 15 years. Chatham has worked hard to create a distinct work environment that values people, teamwork, integrity, and client service. You will have immediate opportunities to partner with talented subject matter experts, work on complex projects, and contribute to the value Chatham delivers every day.

Summary:

As a Covenant Data Specialist on Chatham’s Investment Management team, you will help ensure institutional real estate investors have accurate and consistent covenant information to understand financing obligations, anticipate important requirements, and proactively manage risk across complex debt portfolios. You will review commercial real estate loan agreements and related financing documents to identify and interpret financial, reporting, performance, and other loan covenants, translating complex and varied legal language into Chatham’s established standardized covenant data structure. You will also serve as a key quality-control resource, reviewing covenant data, identifying inconsistencies, and helping the team maintain established data-quality standards.

In this role you will:

  • Review commercial real estate loan agreements, amendments, guaranties, promissory notes, and other financing documents to identify relevant financial, reporting, performance, and other covenants.
  • Interpret covenant provisions, related definitions, calculation requirements, thresholds, testing periods, cure provisions, exceptions, and other terms necessary to understand the full requirement.
  • Translate varied legal language into Chatham’s established standardized covenant data structure and consistently apply defined data conventions across different loans and document structures.
  • Distinguish substantive covenant requirements from supporting language and recognize when provisions are unusual, ambiguous, or require additional interpretation.
  • Perform detailed quality-control reviews of covenant data prepared by others, comparing captured information with underlying loan documentation for accuracy and completeness.
  • Identify errors, inconsistencies, and departures from established data standards and provide clear, actionable feedback.
  • Recognize recurring data-quality issues and identify opportunities to improve procedures, training, standards, and quality controls.
  • Partner with teammates across data, implementation, and advisory functions to resolve questions involving loan terms and covenant interpretation.
  • Share subject-matter knowledge and help reinforce consistent covenant interpretation and data-quality practices across the team.

Your impact:

  • Help provide institutional real estate investors with reliable covenant information they can use to understand financing obligations and proactively manage their debt portfolios.
  • Improve the accuracy and consistency of covenant data by applying established standards and conducting thorough quality-control reviews.
  • Partner across Chatham’s data, implementation, and advisory teams to resolve complex or ambiguous questions involving loan terms and covenant interpretation.
  • Develop expertise in commercial loan documentation and covenant structures, enabling you to identify when interconnected provisions require additional analysis or judgment.
  • Strengthen the team’s data-quality practices by identifying patterns in errors and contributing to improvements in processes, standards, training, and controls.
  • Become a trusted covenant data and quality resource by consistently producing high-quality work, sharing subject-matter expertise, and supporting consistent interpretation across the team.

Contributors to your success:

  • Experience reading and interpreting commercial loan documents or other complex legal or financial agreements.
  • Working knowledge of commercial lending concepts and loan covenants.
  • Strong attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy and completeness.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate information in context and exercise sound judgment when information is unclear, unusual, or does not align with established standards.
  • Ability to interpret varied document language and translate it into a consistent, standardized format.
  • Ability to independently identify discrepancies and determine when unusual or ambiguous provisions require additional review.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear and constructive feedback.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to maintain accuracy while working across a high volume of detailed information.
  • Experience with commercial real estate lending, debt management, loan servicing, covenant monitoring, underwriting, or a related field is preferred.
  • Experience performing quality-control, quality-assurance, or peer-review responsibilities is preferred.
  • Familiarity with financial covenants such as debt service coverage ratio, debt yield, loan-to-value, liquidity, net worth, and other borrower- or property-level requirements is preferred.
  • Experience working with structured financial data or established data standards is preferred.
  • Experience identifying requirements across loan agreements, amendments, guaranties, and other interconnected financing documents is preferred.

For Colorado based candidates, the compensation range for the position is expected to be between $100,000 and $115,000 annually. Total compensation, including base pay, discretionary individual bonus and company bonus, may be higher than the range listed depending on applicant's skills, qualifications, and experience. Benefits include health insurance, life and disability insurance, 401K, EAP, paid holidays, and paid time off.

Chatham Financial is the leading independent capital markets advisor, delivering an integrated blend of expert advice and powerful technology to help you reduce risk and seize opportunity. With decades of capital markets strategy, execution, monitoring, and performance expertise, we serve as an unwavering advocate for your best interests and your innovation partner. Our technology platform unifies data across assets, debt, and derivatives, giving you unmatched agility, transparency, and insight.

It’s clear ahead.

Our commitment is to carry that light forward in every partnership, every solution, and every market we serve.

We help guide the way—giving clients the insight and momentum to move forward with confidence, no matter what lies ahead.

description:
Overview

Apogee has an exciting new opportunity for a Network Administrator to join the team. The technical expert filling this position will be a trusted advisor and consultant to the government supporting government-led ongoing and future sustainment, modification, and capability upgrade efforts across the Space Virtual Labs Network contract supporting the Strategic Warning and Surveillance Systems (SW&SS) division. A key focus for this position is the planning, analysis, design, development, testing, quality assurance, configuration, installation, implementation, and integration of networks supporting these systems. This position will also support broader systems engineering activities associated with these systems.

This is a full-time opportunity located at Peterson SFB, CO

Responsibilities

  • Conduct reviews of the program portfolio to evaluate and/or recommend alternative plans, improve systems engineering programs/processes, manage/sustain the program technical baseline, and design/perform system-level tests to assure that subsystems and system performance are achieved in accordance with approved specifications
  • Prepare technical documents which define, specify, and recommend system/subsystem characteristics. Prepare management reports and conduct technical presentations for planning, implementation, and corrective action using application of engineering economy principles
  • Perform validation of systems, including development of criteria and procedures. Analyze and/or evaluate results of major engineering systems with a concentration on end-to-end communications from sensor/source through C2 node(s) to end users
  • Provide system engineering, technical support, and technical training to support programs/initiatives including, but not limited to, acquisition, development, integration, sustainment, continued evolution, deployment/fielding and installation, and operations oversight
  • Advise and ensure high-quality work that involves the planning, analysis, design, development, testing, quality assurance, configuration, installation, implementation, integration, maintenance, and/or management of networked ITW/AA C2 systems across all levels of the mission environment (day-to-day through scintillation). Functions in this area may include:
    • Analyzing and recommending network requirements
    • Recommending and maintaining network architecture and infrastructure
    • Analyzing network workload
    • Monitoring network capacity and performance
    • Diagnosing and resolving network problems
    • Recommending network backup and recovery procedures
    • Installing, testing, maintaining, and upgrading network operating systems software; and/or ensuring the rigorous application of information security/ cybersecurity policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of network services.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Citizenship: Must be a U.S. Citizen

Clearance: A minimum active Secret clearance with the ability to obtain a Top Secret security clearance

Education: High School Diploma

Years’ experience: 15 years of directly related experience with proper certifications, 8 of which must be in the DoD

Additional experience:

  • Have the advanced knowledge, experience, and demonstrated ability to perform tasks related to the technical/professional discipline as a senior Network Administrator
  • Possess the ability to oversee and guide the efforts of junior and mid-level network administrators

Preferred Qualifications:

Clearance: Active Top Secret

Education: Bachelor's Degree

Years of Experience: 12 years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, 5 of which must be in the DoD; OR Master's Degree 10 years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline being performed, 5 of which must be in the DoD

Additional experience:

Support implementation and execution of Agile software execution in concert with Government and Prime contractors

  • Represent the Government’s interests by performing Agile Product Owner roles and responsibilities.
  • Familiarity with Missile Warning, Missile Defense and/or Space Domain Awareness or Command and Control Systems
  • Familiarity and/or experience with Cloud-based technologies
  • Relevant industry certifications from Cisco and CompTIA are preferred.
  • Good understanding of networking protocols - switching technologies, routing fundamentals, firewalls, IP subnets, firewalling, load balancing, zones, and Management Networks.
  • Working knowledge of network systems, protocols, and standards such as Ethernet, LAN, WAN, xDSL, TCP/IP, fiber, T1, 802.11x, etc.
  • vSphere Certification: VCP-DCV
  • NSX-T Certification: VCP-NV
  • Cisco Certified Network Professional: CCNP
  • Experience with DoD STIGs (as related to networking devices)
  • Experience with Palo Alto Firewall configurations
  • Experience with the ITIL framework and ITIL-based processes, including continual service improvement, change management, and problem investigation.

Additional Information:

Location: Onsite at Peterson SFB in Colorado Springs, CO

Travel: Travel may be required (approx. 10-20%)

Pay Range

USD $80,000.00 - USD $110,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

The NC Department of Administration is the business manager for North Carolina state government. The department oversees Government Operations such as building construction, purchasing and contracting for goods and services, maintaining facilities, managing state vehicles, acquiring and disposing of real property, and operating auxiliary services such as courier mail delivery and the sale of state and federal surplus property. Additionally, the department manages many of the state's advocacy programs that provide assistance and services to diverse segments of the state's population that have been traditionally underserved.

Description of Work

The North Carolina Department of Administration is seeking applicants for a Maintenance/Construction Technician Ill position for our Facility Management Division. The Facility Management Division provides preventive, routine and emergency maintenance and repair services to the State Government complex and some facilities used by government workers in outlying areas. This position requires a thorough working knowledge of fuel oil and gas boilers. Duties include maintenance and repair of boilers and boiler room auxiliary equipment such as condensate systems, reducing stations, pumps, steam and water valves, air compressors, steam traps, and domestic hot water heat exchangers. Position will ensure that all controls, feed water draft, etc., are maintained for optimum plant operation. Position will perform maintenance and make repairs to the underground steam distribution system and reduced pressure steam systems throughout the complex.



This position is located at: 412 N McDowell St. Raleigh, NC

  • The preferred applicant will have previous experience working with Boilers and reducing stations and will have experience in the maintenance and repair of steam distribution systems.

title: Starter Ranger-Main Golf Shop-Seasonal
description:
SUMMARY:
A Starter/Ranger is responsible for the overall management of orderly play by members and guests on the golf courses.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:
High School diploma or General Education Degree (GED) and a minimum three months related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Be knowledgeable regarding the general rules of the play of golf
Be able to stand for several hours consecutively
Be physically able to operate a golf cart, getting in and out periodically for several hours a day
Be able to tolerate adverse weather conditions
Have good interpersonal skills.
Checking tee sheets, and directing players to the starting tee in a timely fashion.
Inform players about daily course conditions, special playing conditions, and any general guidelines regarding play at Pinehurst each day.

title: Kersthulp Laren
description:
Ben jij op zoek naar een leuke bijbaan tijdens de drukste en gezelligste periode van het jaar, waarin je veel contact hebt met mensen én werkt in een gezellig team? Dan hebben wij de perfecte uitdaging voor jou!

Als kerstkracht in onze boutique in Laren ben jij hét gezicht van My Jewellery tijdens de drukke feestdagen. Je verwelkomt klanten met energie, helpt ze bij het vinden van hun favoriete items en zorgt ervoor dat iedereen met een glimlach de winkel verlaat. Samen met je team creëer je een Boutique die straalt en uitnodigt. Van het aanvullen van de collectie tot het adviseren van klanten en het feestelijk inpakken van cadeautjes: jij zorgt voor een fijne en inspirerende winkelervaring.

Benieuwd hoe het is om in een van onze Boutiques te werken? Bekijk deze video!

Jouw taken als Kersthulp

Als Kerstkracht bij My Jewellery werk je tijdelijk in oktober, november en december in onze Boutique en bied je belangrijke ondersteuning tijdens de drukke periode rondom de feestdagen. Samen met het team zorg je ervoor dat alles op de winkelvloer soepel verloopt.

  • Je helpt en adviseert klanten bij het vinden van hun favoriete items;

  • Je zorgt voor een fijne winkelervaring en persoonlijke service;

  • Je pakt cadeautjes feestelijk in met zorg en aandacht;

  • Je houdt de boutique netjes en overzichtelijk;

  • Je ondersteunt je collega’s tijdens drukke momenten.

  • Je bent beschikbaar in oktober, november en december;

  • Je bent in het weekend minimaal één dag beschikbaar;

  • Je bent flexibel inzetbaar tijdens de drukke periode rondom de feestdagen;

  • Je werkt graag in een dynamische omgeving;

  • Je krijgt energie van klantcontact en helpt graag anderen;

  • Je hebt oog voor detail, bijvoorbeeld bij het mooi inpakken van cadeautjes;

  • Je woont in of nabij Laren.

Over My Jewellery

My Jewellery is een van de snelst groeiende merken en e-commerce bedrijven van Nederland met internationale bekendheid. We ontwikkelen collecties en campagnes die het leven van vrouwen een beetje mooier maken. Met meer dan 1.000 collega’s bouwen we elke dag aan een merk vol ambitie en creativiteit. Onze cultuur? Persoonlijk, betrokken en sprankelend. Jij mag hier helemaal jezelf zijn en krijgt de ruimte om te groeien, te leren en impact te maken. Ondanks onze sterke, internationale groei blijven de lijnen kort, de structuur plat en het saamhorigheidsgevoel op hoog niveau. Als team proberen we iedere dag het verschil te maken!

Het aanvragen van een VOG of het raadplegen van het Waarschuwingsregister van het FAD kan onderdeel uitmaken van het sollicitatieproces.

title: Groundworker
description:
Hourly Wage: $27.22 - $29.62


Job Title: Groundperson

Pay Rate Type: Non-Exempt

Creation Date/Revision Date: 04/24/2026


Job Summary:

The Groundperson assists in supporting all activities that occur on the ground during vegetation maintenance and management along power lines. This role identifies safety hazards while utilizing various types of tools and equipment to address brush and clean-up debris.


Essential Job Duties:

  • Loads vehicles and equipment with manageable size limbs and logs not suited for wood chipping.
  • Works on the ground using hand saws, ground saws or other applicable tools to cut brush, limbs and logs of larger trees.
  • Gathers manageable size brush, limbs and logs and carries to the designated chipping area.
  • Applies herbicide and growth regulators to brush and stumps.
  • Operates and works around hazardous equipment, such as chainsaw, pole pruner, stump grinder, woodchipper, etc.
  • Adheres to and helps educate less experienced employees on company policies, on-the-job safety practices, approved work methods and OSHA regulations.
  • Utilizes a variety of tools (i.e. rake, shovel, leaf blower) to remove debris from work area.
  • Feeds brush and debris into woodchipper.
  • Sets up warning signs, barriers, flags, relays hand-signals, directs traffic and other applicable traffic control devices to protect employees and members of the public from hazards in and around the work area. Cooperates with property owner, customer, and emergency personnel when blocking streets or driveways.
  • Staging and clean-up of tools and equipment at the job site. Maintains a neat and orderly work area.
  • Conducts routine maintenance on company vehicles, equipment and tools. Reports specialized vehicle maintenance or equipment needs to General Foreperson.
  • During emergencies or natural disasters may be required to be on duty and travel outside of regular work location for the duration of the disaster.
  • Support, actively participate, and act in accordance with Wright’s culture of safety and employee ownership.
  • Comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations; maintain knowledge of and follow all company policies and procedures.
  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance at work and meetings.

Other Duties:

  • Drives and operates vehicles and equipment as assigned.

Supervisory Duties:


Knowledge, Skills & Ability Requirements:

  • Ability to adhere to company and industry safety requirements.
  • Ability to learn quickly and to follow instructions accurately.
  • Must be able to communicate with others and represent Wright Tree Service in a professional manner.
  • Must be able to comprehend and/or read and write both written and verbal job instructions and safety information.
  • Ability to recognize poisonous plants and take proper safeguard against them.
  • Must be able to wear necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.
  • Ability to work long hours and overtime during emergencies (including holidays, weekends, storm work) and will be subject to call-out work.
  • Demonstrate knowledge on how to perform tree and bucket rescue.
  • Ability to operate and service all required tools and equipment.
  • Ability to work both independently and in a group.

Education, Certification & Experience Requirements:

  • High School diploma or equivalent preferred, but not required.
  • Must have valid First-Aid and CPR cards or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire.

Other Preferred Requirements:

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a valid driver’s or commercial driver’s license (dependent upon Division and utility/contract requirements) and DOT medical card in accordance with FMCSA regulations.
  • Drive a vehicle with an attached chipper or other trailing unit to, from or within the work area.
  • Maintain herbicide application certification or equivalent as required by Wright Tree Service and local, state, and federal law.

Language Requirements (read, write, speak):

English - ☒ Read, ☒ Write, ☒ Speak

Spanish - ☐ Read, ☐ Write, ☐ Speak

Other Language _________________ - ☐ Read, ☐ Write, ☐ Speak

☐No-Seldom

☐Yes-Occasional (up to 5%)

☐Yes-Moderate (5% to 25%)

☐Yes-Substantial (25% to 50%)

☒Yes-Extensive (greater than 50%)


Physical Characteristics:

This position may require physical demands and activities including:

  • Effective bending, reaching, standing, walking, climbing, lifting, carrying, grasping, talking, hearing, and repetitive motions. Occasionally reach upward and downward.
  • Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 50 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 50 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • Possesses the ability to lift, move, and maneuver up to 50 pounds on an infrequent basis and up to 30 pounds on a frequent basis.
  • Must be able to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of work assigned or make general observations of the community; close visual acuity, such as reading a computer screen, reading printed material, inspection of small defects, and using measurement devices.
  • Ability to enter and exit vehicles and equipment numerous times per day.

Environmental Factors:

This position may be exposed to the following factors:

  • Routine exposure to indoor and outdoor working conditions.
  • Routine exposure to weather, climate and temperature, such as rain, heat, sun, cold, snow.
  • Routine exposure to nature, such as irritating plants, biting or stinging insects, dust, etc; position works outdoor on rugged terrain.
  • Routine exposure to noise, vibration, working hazards such as proximity to moving parts, mechanical equipment, moving vehicles, gasoline powered equipment, electrical current, heights, exposure to heat, exposure to chemicals, work in close quarters, narrow aisles or passageways, communicable diseases, bloodborne pathogens, cleaning chemicals, dust, odors, and a variety of pests.

Cargo: Groundperson

Tipo de salario: No exento

Fecha de creación/Fecha de revisión: 04/24/2026


Resumen del puesto:

El Groundperson asiste en todas las actividades que se realizan en el suelo durante el mantenimiento y la gestión de la vegetación a lo largo de las líneas eléctricas. La persona en esta función identifica los peligros de seguridad mientras utiliza diversos tipos de herramientas y equipos para lidiar con la maleza y limpiar residuos.


Funciones esenciales del puesto:

  • Carga vehículos y equipos con ramas y troncos de tamaño fácil de manipular que no sean aptos para el triturado.
  • Trabaja en el suelo con sierras manuales, sierras de uso en el suelo u otras herramientas aplicables para cortar arbustos, ramas y troncos de árboles grandes.
  • Recoge ramas, maleza y troncos de tamaño fácil de manipular y los transporta al área designada para astillar.
  • Aplica herbicidas y reguladores de crecimiento a la maleza (brush) y los troncos.
  • Opera y trabaja cerca de equipos peligrosos, como motosierras, podadora de extensión, trituradoras de troncos, trituradoras de madera, entre otros.
  • Cumple y ayuda a capacitar a empleados con menos experiencia sobre las políticas de la empresa, las prácticas de seguridad en el trabajo, los métodos de trabajo aprobados y las normativas de la Administración de Salud Ocupacional (OSHA).
  • Utiliza diversas herramientas (por ejemplo, rastrillo, pala, soplador de hojas) para retirar los residuos del área de trabajo.
  • Alimenta la trituradora de madera con maleza y residuos.
  • Coloca señales de advertencia, barreras, banderas, transmite señales manuales, dirige el tráfico y utiliza otros dispositivos de control de tráfico según corresponda, para proteger a los empleados y al público de los peligros en y alrededor del área de trabajo. Coopera con los propietarios, clientes y personal de emergencia cuando sea necesario bloquear calles o entradas.
  • Se encarga de la preparación y limpieza de herramientas y equipos en el lugar de trabajo. Mantiene un área de trabajo limpia y ordenada.
  • Efectúa el mantenimiento rutinario de los vehículos, equipos y herramientas de la empresa. Informa al General Foreperson. sobre las necesidades de mantenimiento especializado de los vehículos o equipos.
  • Durante emergencias o desastres naturales, puede ser necesario permanecer de servicio y desplazarse fuera del lugar habitual de trabajo durante la duración del evento.
  • Apoya, participa activamente y actúa de acuerdo con la cultura de seguridad y sentido de pertenencia de Wright.
  • Cumple con las leyes, normas y reglamentos federales, estatales y locales aplicables; mantiene el conocimiento y cumplimiento de todas las políticas y procedimientos de la empresa.
  • Mantiene una asistencia regular y puntual al trabajo y a las reuniones.

Otras funciones:

  • Conduce y opera los vehículos y equipos asignados.

Funciones de supervisión:


Conocimientos, habilidades y aptitudes requeridas:

  • Capacidad para cumplir los requisitos de seguridad de la empresa y del sector.
  • Capacidad para aprender rápidamente y seguir instrucciones con precisión.
  • Capacidad para comunicarse con otras personas y representar a Wright Tree Service de manera profesional.
  • Capacidad para comprender o leer y escribir tanto las instrucciones laborales como la información de seguridad, en forma escrita y verbal.
  • Capacidad para reconocer plantas venenosas y adoptar las medidas preventivas adecuadas.
  • Debe ser capaz de llevar el equipo de protección personal (PPE) requerido.
  • Capacidad para trabajar jornadas prolongadas y realizar horas extras durante emergencias (incluidos feriados, fines de semana y trabajos por tormentas), estando sujeto a llamadas de emergencia.
  • Conocimiento sobre cómo realiza rescate en árboles y con elevador aéreo (canasta).
  • Capacidad para operar y mantener todas las herramientas y equipos requeridos.
  • Capacidad para trabajar tanto de forma independiente como en equipo.

Requisitos de formación, certificación y experiencia:

  • Se prefiere título de educación secundaria o equivalente, aunque no es obligatorio.
  • Debe contar con credenciales vigentes de resucitación cardiopulmonar (CPR), o poder obtenerlas en un plazo de 90 días tras la contratación.

Otros requisitos preferidos:

  • Capacidad para obtener y mantener una licencia de conducir válida o una licencia comercial (según la división y los requisitos del cliente o contrato) y una tarjeta médica emitida por el Departamento de Transporte (Department of Transportation, DOT) conforme a las regulaciones de la FMCSA.
  • Conducir un vehículo con una astilladora u otra unidad remolcada acoplada hacia, desde o dentro del área de trabajo.
  • Mantener la certificación o equivalente en aplicación de herbicidas según lo requieran Wright Tree Service y las leyes locales, estatales y federales.

Requisitos de idioma (leer, escribir, hablar):

Inglés: ☒ leer, ☒ escribir, ☒ hablar

Español: ☐ leer, ☐ escribir, ☐ hablar

Otro idioma _________________ - ☐ leer, ☐ escribir, ☐ hablar


Requisitos de viaje:

☐No, rara vez

☐Sí, ocasional (hasta el 5 %)

☐Sí, moderado (del 5 % al 25 %)

☐Sí, sustancial (del 25 % al 50 %)

☒Sí, extenso (más del 50 %)


Características físicas:

Este puesto puede requerir las siguientes exigencias y actividades físicas:

  • Flexionarse, estirarse, permanecer de pie, caminar, trepar, levantar, cargar, sujetar, hablar, oír y realizar movimientos repetitivos de manera efectiva. Ocasionalmente alcanzar hacia arriba o hacia abajo.
  • Ejercer hasta 100 libras (45 kg) de fuerza ocasionalmente o hasta 50 libras (23 kg) de fuerza con frecuencia, o hasta 50 libras (23 kg) de fuerza de manera constante para mover objetos.
  • Poseer la capacidad para levantar, mover y maniobrar hasta 50 libras (23 kg) ocasionalmente y hasta 30 libras (14 kg) con frecuencia.

Factores ambientales:

Las personas en este puesto pueden estar expuestas a los siguientes factores:

  • Exposición habitual a condiciones de trabajo tanto interiores como exteriores.

  • Exposición habitual a la naturaleza, como plantas irritantes, insectos que pican o muerden, polvo, etc.; el puesto se desarrolla al aire libre en terrenos irregulares.
  • Exposición habitual a ruido, vibraciones, peligros laborales como la proximidad a piezas móviles, equipos mecánicos, vehículos en movimiento, equipos con motor de gasolina, corriente eléctrica, alturas, calor, productos químicos, espacios reducidos, pasillos o conductos estrechos, enfermedades transmisibles, patógenos de transmisión sanguínea, productos de limpieza, polvo, olores y diversos tipos de plagas.

title: Audit Senior (Part-Qualified) - Mid Market
description:
Forvis Mazars is a leading global professional services network providing audit & assurance, tax, and advisory services. Forvis Mazars in the UK spans 14 offices across the nation and has over 3,400 professionals, with 190 partners. We have a clear purpose and a shared commitment to shape a better future.

You’ll join a collaborative and inclusive team where you’re supported to grow your skills, explore new opportunities, and contribute from day one. You’ll work with a diverse client base, develop meaningful connections, and gain experience that extends beyond your local team. Together, we grow, belong and impact.


About The Team


In Audit, you will join a growing team of relationship driven, curious, problem solvers who add value to their clients every day. Our audit teams provide assurance services that strengthen internal controls, build investor confidence, and ensure financial credibility. We support a wide variety of clients, from privately owned businesses to UK listed companies, financial services clients, and some of the world’s largest FT Global organisations.


As part of our uniquely integrated structure, you’ll benefit from working in collaborative teams, gaining early responsibility and being empowered to challenge, learn and lead in a supportive, values-driven environment. Our commitment to quality, independence of thought and innovation helps us play a key role in shaping the future of audit.


Our Mid-Market Audit team partners with ambitious, privately owned organisations to deliver tailored, value-added audits. We work with:

  • Family-owned and entrepreneur-led businesses
  • Private equity and venture capital-backed groups
  • Privately held businesses and groups with revenue typically between £10m and £150m
  • Unregulated asset managers and real estate owners with assets under £1bn

Our clients span a range of sectors, from food manufacturing and engineering to healthcare and fintech, and often operate across borders or are scaling rapidly.


About the role


As an Audit Senior (SN1), you will take the lead on multiple audit engagements from planning through to completion. You’ll supervise and coach junior staff, manage client communications, and ensure the delivery of exceptional, timely audit services.


Role & Responsibilities


  • Audit Delivery – Manage audits for Mid-Market, SMEs and privately owned businesses, supporting the process from planning through to completion, ensuring work is delivered on time, within budget, and to quality standards.
  • Planning & Organisation – Assist in developing audit strategies and scoping plans, ensuring resources and timelines are effectively managed.
  • Technical Application – Apply up-to-date technical knowledge (UK GAAP / FRS 102, IFRS, Companies Act) to audit assignments, escalating complex matters to senior colleagues as needed.
  • Review & Reporting – Draft sections of key reporting outputs such as the audit opinion summary, group reporting packs, and audit committee documents for review by Managers and Partners.
  • Team Support – Lead and supervise audit assistants and seniors during fieldwork, allocating tasks, reviewing work, and providing constructive on-the-job feedback.
  • Coaching & Development – Support the growth of junior team members by providing guidance, feedback, and informal training.
  • Quality & Compliance – Ensure audit files are completed to the required standard, review points are addressed, and firmwide methodologies and regulatory requirements are followed.
  • Client Relationships – Act as a day-to-day contact for clients, responding promptly to requests and building professional, trusted relationships.
  • Commercial Awareness – Monitor time spent against budget, assist with billing in line with agreed plans, and identify opportunities to add value or cross-sell services.
  • Collaboration – Work closely with colleagues across audit and other service lines, contributing to business development and firmwide initiatives.

What we are looking for


  • Part-Qualified (final year) – ACA / CA / ACCA (or equivalent).
  • Sector Experience – Experience in external audit, ideally with Mid-Market, SMEs and privately owned businesses.
  • Level of Responsibility – Experience of leading audit assignments from planning through to completion, with increasing responsibility for managing client relationships.
  • Leadership Experience – Experience supervising and coaching audit trainees and seniors, with the ability to delegate effectively and review work to a high standard.
  • Technical Expertise – Up-to-date knowledge of UK GAAP (including FRS 102), IFRS, and the Companies Act.
  • Stakeholder Engagement – Ability to build professional relationships with clients, act as a point of contact during audits, and handle queries promptly.
  • People Management – Provides on-the-job training and constructive feedback to junior team members, supporting both technical and personal development.
  • Communication Skills – Strong written and verbal skills, with the confidence to explain technical matters clearly to clients and colleagues.
  • Technology Skills – Proficient in audit software and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Project Ownership – Takes responsibility for audit assignments, monitoring budgets and ensuring compliance with quality and risk management processes.
  • Innovation and Improvement – Willing to contribute to process improvements, adopting new methodologies and approaches to improve efficiency.
  • Analytical Thinking – Able to identify potential issues, apply professional judgement, and provide practical solutions.
  • Knowledge Sharing – Shares expertise and provides guidance to colleagues, contributing to a culture of collaboration and continuous learning.
  • Networking – Begins to build a network of client and professional contacts, supporting both personal development and firm growth.

#LI-DNP


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Forvis Mazars diversity, equity and inclusion are central to our values. We value our people's unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experience, and know this diversity create better outcomes for our clients. We seek to attract, develop, and retain the best talent, inclusive of sex, ethnicity, disability, socio-economic background, sexual orientation, gender identity, nationality, and faith. We select candidates based on skills, knowledge, qualifications, and experience and aim to support all our team members to reach their potential. At Forvis Mazars, we promote an environment in which you can grow your skills, belong to a team that values your ideas, and make an impact that matters.

title: Senior Psychologist - Central Regional Hospital
description:
Agency

Dept of Health and Human Services

Division

Central Regional Hospital

Job Classification Title

Psychologist Senior (NS)

Position Number

Grade

MH20

About Us

The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is one of the largest, most complex agencies in the state, and has approximately 17,000 employees. It is responsible for ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of all North Carolinians, providing human service needs for special populations including individuals who are deaf, blind, developmentally disabled, and mentally ill, and helping poor North Carolinians achieve economic independence.


Description of Work

The primary purpose of this position is to assist the PST Director and Department Heads implementing long- and short-range goals necessary for the delivery of effective, integrated treatment for children, adults, and adolescents. This position requires conceptualization of difficult cases, liaising with treatment/management teams on novel solutions to improve service provision, addressing interdepartmental communication issues, providing supervision/guidance to staff regarding de-escalation/redirection, guiding line staff regarding any behavioral interventions, providing in the moment direction to supervisory and line staff when environmental or behavioral issues arise, as well as facilitating departmental workgroups, projects, committees, and training activities.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities/Management Preferences

Salary Range: $82,857.00 - $136,714.00

Recruitment Range: $95,000.00 - $125,000.00


*A Sign-on bonus of $15,000 may be offered to the successful applicant(s) of this posting, contingent on Budget Approval.


Candidates now meet the minimum qualifications of a position if they meet the minimum education and experience listed on the vacancy announcement.

The Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)/ Management Preferences are not required. Applicants who possess the following skills are preferred:


  • Advanced competency in behavioral assessment, including preference and reinforcer assessments and the functional analysis of conditions maintaining problem behavior.
  • Competency in the provision of psychological treatment including individual and group psychotherapy, techniques for increasing adaptive behavior such as shaping, differential reinforcement of behavior, modeling, and behavioral skills training, and techniques for reducing problem behavior via contingency management.
  • Knowledge of community resources, institutional policies/procedures, and state law regarding psychological treatment.
  • Knowledge of the theories and practices of the field of psychology including behavior analysis and other learning theories, the social learning model, biological bases of behavior and human development (normal and psychopathological) throughout the life span; with knowledge of issues of assessment and treatment of patients with severe behavior disorders and mental illness.
  • Knowledge of psychometrically sound psychological, neuropsychological, neurodevelopmental, and educational tests including those of a complex, comprehensive nature, with specific knowledge of their age and need-appropriate use with patients.

This Position Is Exempt And Is EXEMPT From Certain Provisions Of The State Human Resources Act (GS 126)


This is a full-time position and eligible for the full State benefits package. The normal work hours are Monday-Friday, 8:00am-5:00pm; however, flexibility is required.


*Eligibility for Sign-on Bonus

To qualify for the Sign-on Bonus, a newly hired permanent full-time or permanent part-time employee must work 30 to 40 hours per week to be eligible. Those who are eligible and working less than 40 hours a week will receive a prorated rate.


An employee is not eligible for a sign-on bonus if:

  • The employee has held a position in the North Carolina State government, including the judicial system, or the University of North Carolina system, within the last 12 months (the employee shall remain ineligible for 12 months from the separation date)
  • The employee has previously received a sign-on bonus from any State agency
  • DHHS has paid any contract placement or recruitment fees.

All Sign-on Bonuses are contingent upon budget and final eligibility determination as of the effective date of hire. Additional information regarding the Sign-on Policy can be found here.


About the Facility:

CRH is a State-of-the Art psychiatric hospital located in Butner, NC. CRH is one of three regional state psychiatric hospitals in North Carolina whose purpose is to diagnose and treat children, adolescents and adults with mental illness. Our location is ideal with four seasons, mild temperatures and provides an easy commute to the N.C. mountains or beaches. Butner possesses small town charm but is within 30 minutes of a major metropolitan area including Research Triangle Park, Raleigh, Chapel Hill, and Durham, NC. The people we serve are at the heart of our facility. Our team is critical to the mission of the hospital. We strive to create an environment in which every team member contributes to the overall success of the hospital to positively impact the lives of those around them and the individuals we serve.


Supplemental Contact Information:

DHHS uses the Merit-Based Recruitment and Selection Plan to fill positions subject to the State Human Resources Act with the most qualified individuals. Hiring salary will be based on relevant qualifications, internal equity, and budgetary considerations pertinent to the advertised position.

Positions in the Division of State Operated Healthcare Facilities shall be subject to pre-employment drug testing and criminal record background checks. Also, the use of tobacco products of any kind including vapor products are prohibited from our campuses. All employees are required to adhere to the facility's Vaccination Policy.


Application Process
Be sure to complete the application in its entirety. Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of completing this application.

  • Information should be provided in the appropriate areas, to include the following: Education, including high school and all degrees obtained, Work Experience, and Certificates & Licenses. It is critical to our screening and salary determination process that applications contain comprehensive candidate information.
  • Answers to Supplemental Questions are not a substitute for providing all relevant information within the body of your application. To receive credit for the supplemental questions, you must provide supporting information within the "Work Experience" section of the application, to support your answers.
  • The posting will close at 11:59 p.m. the night before the end date.
  • Due to the volume of applications received, we are unable to provide information regarding the status of your application over the phone. To check the status of your application, please log in to your account. Upon the closing date, applications are "Under Review" and will be screened by Human Resources for the qualified applicants. The hiring process may take several weeks.
  • Degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions. Transcripts and degree evaluations may be uploaded with your application. The State of North Carolina/Office of State Human Resources uses the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES) as a referral resource for applicants who need to have their credentials certified as equivalent. For a list of organizations that perform this specialized service, please visit the NACES membership website at .

Veteran’s and National Guard Preference

  • Applicants seeking Veteran's Preference must attach a DD-214 Member-4 Form (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty) to their applications.
  • Applicants seeking National Guard Preference must attach an NGB 23A (RPAS), along with the state application if they are a current member of the NC National Guard in good standing.
  • Applicants who are former member of either the NC Army National Guard or the NC Air National Guard, with honorable discharge and six years of creditable service, must attach a copy of the DD 256 or NGB 22, along with the state application.

ADA Accommodations

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA), DHHS is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, DHHS will ensure that people with disabilities, or known limitations covered by the PWFA, are provided with reasonable accommodation. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the person indicated below.


Applicants will be communicated via email only for updates on the status of their application. If there are any questions about this posting other than your application status, please contact HR at 919-764-7200.


Minimum Education and Experience

Some state job postings say you can qualify by an “equivalent combination of education and experience.” If that language appears below, then you may qualify through EITHER years of education OR years of directly related experience, OR a combination of both. See the Education and Experience Equivalency Guide for details.


Eligibility for licensure in North Carolina under the provisions of the NC Psychology Practice Act (G.S. 90-270) and two years of professional psychological experience, one of which must be postdoctoral. Refer to the law for specifics regarding experience requirements.

Candidates will be considered while completing licensure requirements. Licensure must be obtained prior to beginning employment.
